output: Prescription Drug Monitoring Act of 2016 This bill requires each state that receives funding under the prescription drug monitoring program (PDMP) under the Departments of Commerce, Justice, and State to: (1) require prescribing practitioners to consult the PDMP of that state before initiating treatment with a controlled substance listed in schedule II, III, or IV of the Controlled Substances Act, and every three months thereafter as long as the treatment continues; (2) provide notification to practitioners when patterns indicative of controlled substance misuse are detected; (3) make quarterly data releases available to state practitioners; and (4) make available a data sharing single hub to facilitate the sharing of PDMP data among states and the access of practitioners.

Contributions Legally Interdicted from Noncitizens To Our Nonprofits Act of 2016 or the CLINTON Act of 2016 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to prohibit a federal official organization from being treated as an organization for which the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) has a tax-exempt status.  A federal official organization must accept or solicit contributions from any person connected to a foreign government. A federal official organization that accepts a contribution from any person and learns that the person is connected to a foreign government must return the contribution within 30 days. A federal official organization that accepts a contribution from any person and learns that the person is connected to a foreign government must return the contribution within 30 days.  The bill imposes a tax on any federal official organization that accepts a contribution from any person connected to a foreign government.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to permit issuance of private activity bonds for use as qualified municipal bond or energy development bond for electric output facilities. 
Provides for the nonrefundation of refunding bonds.

United States-Afghanistan Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) Act of 2011 - Directs the President to seek to negotiate and enter into a bilateral status of forces agreement with the government of Afghanistan.

Requires the status of forces agreement to prohibit the permanent basing or military presence of U.S. Armed Forces in Afghanistan.

Authorizes the status of forces agreement to provide for the authorization of specific exercises, activities, or missions of the U.S. Armed Forces in Afghanistan.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the President should submit the status of forces agreement to Congress for its advice and consent to ratification as a treaty or alternatively the President should request statutory authorization for the status of forces agreement by Congress.

Requires the President to submit to the House and Senate Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence a copy of the status of forces agreement.

Return of Talent Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish the Return of Talent Program to permit eligible aliens to temporarily return to the alien's country of citizenship to make a material contribution to that country if the country is engaged in post-conflict reconstruction activities, for a period not exceeding 24 months, unless an exception is granted under specified circumstances.

Authorizes the Secretary to extend the program by an additional 24-month period upon a showing that circumstances warrant that an extension is necessary for post-conflict reconstruction efforts.

Requires the spouse, parents, siblings, and any children of an alien who participates in the Return of Talent Program to be considered: (1) for purposes of the special immigrant description, for purposes of naturalization; and (2) to meet the continuous residency requirements.

Requires the Secretary to oversee and enforce the requirements of this Act.

Amends the Improvement Act of 1998 to include among eligible immigrants for permanent resident purposes a citizen of a country in which U.S. armed forces are engaged, or have engaged, in the 10 years preceding such determination.

Strategic Withdrawal of Agencies for Meaningful Placement Act of 2018 or SWAMP Act This bill amends federal law governing the relocation of executive agencies to allow the temporary reallocation of such agencies' heads from the Washington metropolitan area to other metropolitan areas. The bill repeals the requirement that a federal agency's headquarters be located in the Washington metropolitan area. The bill prohibits the use of competitive bidding procedures for the relocation of an agency's headquarters. The bill also prohibits the use of federal funds to offset the cost of relocating the agency's headquarters.

Minority Business Development Improvements Act of 2010 - Requires the Director of the Minority Business Development Agency (the agency) to establish the Minority Business Development Program to assist qualified minority businesses.

Authorizes the Director to certify as a qualified minority business any entity that satisfies: (1) at least 51% of the entity's direct and independent control; (2) each officer or other individual who exercises control over the regular operations of the entity; (3) the net worth of each principal of the entity; (4) its place of business; (5) the entity's business operations in not less than one sector of industry that has a North American Industry Classification System code; and (6) any additional requirements the Director determines appropriate.

Terminates the program when a qualified minority business fails to comply with the requirements of this Act.

Authorizes the Director to enter into agreements with persons to provide technical assistance.

Authorizes the Director to enter into agreements with the federal government and any department, agency, or officer having procurement powers for purposes of providing for the fulfillment of procurement contracts and providing opportunities for qualified minority businesses with regard to such contracts.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to make a grant to an eligible public university to establish the Center for the Study of Women and Workplace Policy to compile and analyze available data and data sets on the difference between the earnings of men and women, including the Panel Study of Income Dynamic housed at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, and to identify factors which affect earnings differences.

Requires the Center to: (1) disseminate its findings annually to the public, using a website and other appropriate means; and (2) publish one best practices guide for businesses and families containing recommended guidelines for workplace equity, retaining women in the workplace, and promoting a family-friendly workplace.

Small Business Access to Capital Act of 2009 - Amends the Small Business Act to: (1) increase from 75 to 90% of the value of collateral of a small business-related loan to a small business that does not involve the expansion of a small business concern; (2) allow small businesses to refinance non-essential loans; (3) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (4) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (5) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (6) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (7) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (8) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (9) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (10) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (11) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (12) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities; (13) allow small businesses to refinance loans to non-essential entities;

Census Improvement Act - Prohibits participation in the Planning Partnership Program for the 2010 census of population unless: (1) an organization has been indicted for a federal or state law election; or (2) an organization employs applicable individuals.

Requires the following to be part of the requirements for reconsideration of a prohibition: (1) a specified disclosure requirement; and (2) a specified requirement that the prohibition be repealed or otherwise limited.

Requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to review and report to Congress on the questions proposed to be included in the 2010 census of population and the American Community Survey (next scheduled to be carried out after the enactment of this Act).

Prohibits any person from seeking answers to any questions relating to any household or any member of such household from any person outside of the household.

Electronic Campaign Disclosure Act of 1998 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to establish a public Internet site within 10 days of the submission of a report required by the Act to the House of Representatives and the Senate on the Federal Election Commission's contribution to the election of the President. 
Requires the FEC to permit each person required to file a report to post the report directly on the site. 
Requires the FEC to permit any person to post a report on the site by posting it on the Internet (or by filing it by such electronic method as the FEC may designate to enable the FEC to post the report on such site immediately upon receipt). 
Requires the FEC to require a person to file a report in accordance with the methods described in clause (1) during an election cycle if the aggregate amount of contributions or expenditures reported previously by the person during the cycle exceed $25,000.

Amends Federal law to grant the Civil Air Patrol administrative responsibility as a Federal charter corporation. 
Directs the Secretary of the Air Force to appoint a National Board of Directors for the Civil Air Patrol. 
Requires the Board to appoint:  (1) a National Commander to be appointed from the civilian volunteer membership of the Air Force; (2) an Executive Director; (3) a Safety Officer; and (4) an Inspector General. 
Requires the Board to report directly to the Secretary through the National Board of Directors. 
Authorizes the Chief of Staff to assign officers and enlisted members of the Air Force on active duty and civilian employees of the Department of the Air Force to serve on the staff of the national headquarters of the Civil Air Patrol. 
Prohibits the use of the Airfield and the personnel of the Airfield staff and employees to the extent that they are Federal employees and subject to Federal employment laws. 
Subjects all funds provided to the Airfield to the approval of the Secretary of the Air Force and is subject to any policies, regulations, or instructions issued by the Secretary.

Children's Bicycle Helmet Safety Act of 1993 - Authorizes the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to make grants to States, State political subdivisions, and nonprofit organizations for programs that require or encourage individuals under age 16 to wear approved bicycle helmets. 
Requires such grants to be used to:  (1) enforce a law that requires such individuals to wear such helmets while riding on bicycles; (2) assist such individuals in acquiring such helmets; (3) develop and administer a program to educate such individuals on the importance of wearing such helmets in order to improve bicycle safety; or (4) carry out any combination of the activities described. 
Requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to begin a proceeding under Federal law to review the interim standards and establish a final standard based on such requirements. 
Makes such standards inapplicable to any standard issued under such proceeding. 
Provides that until the final standard takes effect, a bicycle helmet that does not conform to an interim standard as required under this Act shall be considered in violation of a consumer product safety standard promulgated under the Consumer Product Safety Act. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Electronic Employment Verification Reauthorization Act of 2008 - Amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to terminate a pilot program at the end of the 11-year period beginning on the first day the pilot program is in effect.

Amends the Illegal Immigration and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to authorize: (1) U.S. contractors to participate in the basic pilot program; (2) the basic pilot program to be expanded to include basic pilot program employees; (3) employers to participate in the basic pilot program; and (4) the pilot program to be expanded to include employees of federal agencies.

Requires a small business to use the E-Verify program to verifies the employment eligibility of its newly hired employees.

Directs the Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to establish a demonstration program that assists small businesses in verifying the employment eligibility of their newly hired employees.

Selected Reserve Home Loan Equity Act - Makes permanent the authority for veterans to make loans to themselves and their dependents, and to the veterans' organizations that participate in the Armed Forces, including the veterans' home loan guarantee program.

New Aid for Trustworthy, Affordable Drugs Act (NAFTA Drugs Act) - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA) to direct the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to seek to enter into agreements with other North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) countries to harmonize regulatory requirements for drugs to allow drugs approved for commercial distribution in any NAFTA country to be imported or exported from any NAFTA country into any other NAFTA country.

Older and Disabled Americans Criminal Protection Act of 1998 - Authorizes a shared housing referral agency to request the Attorney General to conduct a search and exchange of records regarding any applicant for participation in a shared housing arrangement as a service provider resident by:  (1) submitting fingerprints and a written statement authorizing the agency to request the search and exchange of records regarding the applicant; and (2) making such submission within 7 days after acquiring the information.  Directs the Attorney General to provide such information to the appropriate State or local governmental agency. 
Authorizes the agency to charge a fee of up to $50 to any such agency requesting such a search and exchange. 
Requires the Attorney General to report to the House of Representatives and the Senate on the number of requests for searches and exchanges of records made by such agencies and the disposition of such requests. 
Makes a shared housing referral agency that reasonably relies upon such information liable for any damages resulting from completeness or inaccuracy of the information. 
Makes such agency's service provider resident information.

Revises provisions regarding the Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS) and the Fish and Wildlife Service (SFWS) Retirement System to: (1) make a law enforcement officer eligible for retirement benefits if such officer is a fish and wildlife officer; (2) make a law enforcement officer eligible for retirement benefits if such officer is a firefighter or a fish and wildlife officer; and (3) make a law enforcement officer eligible for retirement benefits if such officer is a firefighter or a fish and wildlife officer.

Revises provisions regarding the CSRS and the SFWS Retirement System to: (1) make a law enforcement officer eligible for retirement benefits if such officer is a firefighter or a fish and wildlife officer; and (2) make a law enforcement officer eligible for retirement benefits if such officer is a firefighter or a fish and wildlife officer.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior to make payments to Federal employees who serve as fish and wildlife officers into the Civil Service Retirement and Disability Fund.

Assault Weapons Prohibition Act of 1993 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit the transfer or possession of an assault weapon after the effective date of this Act. 
Makes it unlawful for a person to:  (1) transfer an assault weapon; or (2) possess such weapon after the 90-day period that begins with the effective date of this Act. 
Provides that such prohibition shall not apply to a transfer to or by, or possession by, the United States or any department or agency thereof, or any State or a local government, or any political subdivision, agency, or governmental subdivision. 
Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to prescribe regulations to carry out this Act. 
Authorizes the Secretary to recommend to the Congress that the definition of an assault weapon be modified to include firearms not covered by the definition which should be so modified. 
Directs the Attorney General to investigate and evaluate the recreational and other noncriminal uses of assault weapons.

Open Our Democracy Act of 2014 - Requires each state to hold a single open primary election for each office of the House of Representatives, with the exception of a state where the candidate of a political party is eligible to stand for election to such office.  Requires the candidate to declare a political party preference at the time of filing to run for such office.  Prohibits a party from: (1) designating a candidate not to declare a political party preference as a candidate to declare a political party preference, or (2) giving a candidate a party preference on election day.  Prohibits a political party from: (1) establishing procedures to endorse or support candidates or to participate in all elections, or (2) giving a candidate a party preference at the time of registering to vote.  Treats the election day in the same manner as a law-related public holiday.  Requires the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on the feasibility and desirability of enacting national standards and criteria for congressional redistricting.

Hospital Price Disclosure Act of 2005 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a hospital to report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) data on its outpatient department (OPD) and hospital operating room (HR) data on its ambulatory surgical center (ASCM) data on procedures and drugs selected under specified provisions.

Requires a hospital to report to the Secretary also data on its outpatient department and hospital operating room data on its outpatient department and its ASCM data on procedures and drugs selected under specified provisions.

Requires the Secretary to report to the hospital on the availability of the following data: (1) the 25 most frequently performed hospital inpatient procedures; (2) the 25 most frequently performed hospital outpatient procedures; (3) the 50 most frequently administered drugs in a hospital inpatient setting; and (4) the 100 most frequently administered drugs in a hospital outpatient setting.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) publicly post such data on the HHS Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) website; and (2) set forth in a manner that promotes price comparison among hospitals and ASCMs.

Directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to conduct an experimental program to test whether low-power FM radio stations will result in harmful interference to existing FM radio stations if such stations are not subject to the minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels required by this Act.
Requires the FCC to select an independent testing entity to conduct field tests in the markets of the stations in the experimental program. Requires the FCC to submit a report to Congress on the experimental program and field tests, including an analysis of the public comment received by the FCC on the program and the public opinion on the need for third-adjacent channels.

Turkish Human Rights Act - Prohibits assistance under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 until the Secretary of State has determined that there has been significant progress in:  (1) the Government of Turkey's human rights monitoring organizations; (2) its Kurdish citizens' monitoring organizations; (3) its military operations against Kurdish civilians; (4) its actions and policies to demilitarize Cyprus; and (5) its support for a peaceful resolution of the Kurdish issue.

Environmental Finance Act of 1995 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to establish an Environmental Financial Advisory Board to provide expert advice on issues affecting the costs and financing of environmental activities at the Federal, State, and local levels. 
Directs the Board to:  (1) work with the Science Advisory Board to identify and develop methods to integrate risk and finance considerations into environmental decisionmaking; (2) develop and recommend initiatives to expand opportunities for the export of U.S. financial services and environmental technologies; (3) develop alternative financing mechanisms to assist State and local governments in paying for environmental programs; (4) develop alternative financing mechanisms and strategies to meet the unique needs of small and economically disadvantaged communities; and (5) undertake such other activities as the Board determines will further the purpose of this Act. 
Authorizes the Board to recommend to Congress and the Administrator legislative and policy initiatives to make financing for environmental protection more available and less costly. 
Directs the Administrator to establish and support an Environmental Finance Center in an institution of higher education in each of the regions of the Environmental Protection Agency.  Authorizes appropriations.

High School Sports Information Collection Act of 2009 - Amends the Education Sciences Reform Act of 2002 to require the Statistics Commissioner to: (1) annually collect information from each coeducational secondary school receiving federal financial assistance that has an athletic program for each student that participates in the school's athletic competition; and (2) make such information available to students and potential students, upon request, and to the public.

Requires secondary schools to provide such information to the Commissioner at least 15 days after the Commissioner makes such information available.

Generating American Income and Infrastructure Now Act - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to sell, under terms established by the Secretary of the Treasury, distressed notes and other obligations held by USDA. Requires 50 percent of the proceeds from such sale to be deposited in an account designated for carrying out infrastructure projects in low-income communities, and 50 percent to be retained in the Treasury for purposes of deficit reduction.

Requires USDA to: (1) consult with the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a fair market valuation for the sale of the distressed notes or other obligations; (2) notify the borrower that the USDA intends to sell such note or other obligation; (3) provide an opportunity for notice and public comment in a manner that protects the personally identifiable information relating to the borrower; (4) notify the borrower that the USDA intends to sell such obligation; (5) obtain the highest possible return from the sales of distressed notes or other obligations; and (6) require persons offering to purchase the note or other obligation to demonstrate that they: (1) are able or resources to provide necessary servicing; and (2) are able to generate capital to provide the borrowers of the distressed notes or other obligations with the necessary credit.

National Youth Summer Jobs Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to eligible entities for providing summer employment for out-of-school youths.

Requires grantees to use the funds to expand their summer employment programs, including to provide job training and support services, including health and nutrition referral, housing transfer, financial literacy, and instruction on basic daily living skills.

Gives grant priority to entities operating in communities where: (1) at least one of specified rates of unemployment, poverty, or juvenile offender rates was higher than the national average; and (2) each rate was higher than the national average for at least 20 years.

Medicare Pharmacist Services Coverage Act of 2001 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000, to provide for Medicare coverage of pharmacist services.

Reducing Barriers to Veterans' Benefits Act - Amends the Veterans' Benefits Act to consider service-connection for hearing loss associated with particular military occupational specialties or combat service, notwithstanding no record of evidence of such hearing loss or tinnitus, as the case may be, during the period of such service.

Directs the Secretary of the military department concerned to: (1) issue proposed regulations setting forth such presumption; and (2) publish such determination in the Federal Register and submit a report to the congressional veterans' committees.

Requires the Secretary of the military department concerned to ensure that a member of the armed forces receives an audiometric test at the 8000 Hz frequency (or other test that the Secretary determines has the ability to discover potential future hearing loss) to evaluate the hearing of such member before the date on which the member is discharged, separated, or retired.

Coal Cleanup Taxpayer Protection Act - Amends the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 to prohibit the Secretary of the Interior from approving as part of a State or Federal program an alternative system that would: (1) achieve the objectives and purposes of the bonding program pursuant to such Act; and (2) result in no greater risk of financial liability to the Federal Government or a State government than the bonding program under such Act. Prohibits the Secretary from accepting a bond of the applicant itself or a separate surety or collateral bond, consistent with the terms of such a bond, by replacing the bond with another form of bond acceptable to the Secretary under this Act by not later than the earlier of: (1) the date of renewal of the permit under the Act; and (2) the date of any major permit modification. Directs the Secretary to notify all State regulatory authorities that allow applicants to self-bond that the approved regulatory programs of the State regulatory authority must be amended to remove the authority for applicants to self-bond and to require coal mining operations covered by a self-bond to replace the self-bond with another form of bond acceptable by the Secretary. Directs the Secretary to issue rules establishing limitations on surety bonds

United Nations Oil-for-Food Accountability Act of 2004 - Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to withhold certain U.S. assessed contributions from amounts appropriated for international organizations until the President certifies to Congress that: (1) the United Nations has in effect procedures that provide the General Accounting Office access to all documents relating to the oil-for-food program; (2) the United Nations Secretary General has confirmed that the United Nations will not assert the inviolability of U.N. papers and internal records that concern the oil-for-food program or a sanction imposed on Iraq related to such program; (3) the United Nations has waived immunity enjoyed by any U.N. official from the judicial process in the United States for any civil or criminal acts or omissions under Federal or State law that may have transpired within the jurisdiction of the United States in connection with the oil-for-food program; and (4) any U.N. official who benefited financially from the oil-for-food program has reimbursed the Government of Iraq and any other entity affected by the illicit activity of such official the full amount that such official improperly received from the oil-for-food program.

Energy-Efficient Cool Roof Jobs Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to revise the definition of "qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property" to: (1) include roof systems that have a 20-year property recovery period, and (2) allow for a 25% depreciation allowance for such systems.

Federal Propaganda Prohibition Act of 2005 - Requires an executive agency to submit to each congressional committee a written notification containing the name of the contractor, the amount of the contract, the purpose of the contract, a summary of the statement of work for the contract, and any other information the agency considers relevant.

Prohibits an officer or employee of the United States government from making or authorizing a expenditure or obligation of funds for publicity or propaganda purposes unless authorized by law.

Requires each advertisement or other communication paid for by an agency, either directly or through a contract awarded by the agency, to include a prominent notice in informing the target audience that the advertisement or other communication is paid for by that agency.

Confederate Commemorative Works Inventory and Joint Resource Study Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to: (1) conduct a full inventory of Confederate commemorative works under their respective administrative jurisdictions; and (2) submit a copy of such inventory to the Director of the National Park Service (NPS). Requires the Director to conduct a special resource study that: (1) examines works, commemorating and interpreting the Civil War, the commemoration, the soldiers, people on the home front and battle lines, and the related locations in the United States from 1861 through 1865; and (2) identifies: (1) a historical assessment of each inventoried works, (2) an evaluation of the suitability and feasibility of retaining the works; (3) the identification of properties that could meet criteria for listing in the National Register of Historic Places or criteria for designation as National Historic Landmarks or if the works are already on the or part of another designation or district; (4) an evaluation of relevant historical research on, education about, interpretation of, and public awareness of the works; and (5) any other matters that the Director determines to be appropriate for this study.

Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard Deadline Harmonization Act of 2015 This bill requires the Governors of each state to designate in accordance with the Clean Air Act (CAA) all areas of the state as attainment, nonattainment, or unclassifiable with respect to the 2015 ozone standards. The EPA must promulgate final designations for all areas in all states with respect to such standards. Each state must submit a plan for the 2015 ozone standards. The EPA may not: (1) complete, before October 26, 2025, any review of the criteria for ozone published under the CAA or the national ambient air quality standard for ozone promulgated under such Act, or (2) propose revisions to such criteria or standards. The EPA must report to Congress on the next review of the ozone standards.

Endangered Species Community Advisory Board Act of 1995 - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish an Endangered Species Community Advisory Board to:  (1) assist local government officials in identifying the needs and concerns of the affected local community and individual landowners regarding designation of an area as a critical habitat or a National Wildlife Refuge as designated by the Secretary; and (2) publish recommendations received from the Board regarding the continued accuracy and sufficiency of the scientific findings that were the basis of that designation. 
Requires the Board to:  (1) monitor and periodically report to the Secretary on progress made in the conservation and recovery of species for which that critical habitat or Refuge was designated; and (2) periodically review and report to the Secretary regarding the continued accuracy and sufficiency of the scientific findings that were the basis of that designation.

Freedom to Mourn in Peace Act of 2011 - Prohibits any person from carrying out: (1) a demonstration on the property where a funeral is held unless it has been approved by the cemetery superintendent or the owner of the property on which the funeral is held; or (2) any part of such demonstration which includes any individual making or assisting in the making of any noise or diversion that disturbs or tends to disturb the peace or good order of the cemetery or other property, or which is within 1,000 feet of such cemetery or other property and impedes its access to or egress from such cemetery or other property, if there is visible at each place that is at the applicable distance from such cemetery or other property a sign which clearly and conspicuously states that a funeral will be held on such cemetery or other property and so states the time interval during which the funeral will be held.

Helping to Encourage Real Opportunities (HERO) for At-Risk Youth Act This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) allow a work opportunity tax credit for summer employment of at-risk youth, (2) extend the eligibility period for such credit through 2019, and (3) extend the authority for the Department of the Treasury to make a new empowerment zone designation through December 31, 2019.

Save America's Utility Infrastructure and Secure America Now Act of 2008 - Amends the Federal Power Act to authorize the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to impose civil penalties for violations of certain reliability standards approved by FERC.

Requires FERC to issue a rule to prohibit disturbances lasting greater than five days at substations subject to such standards.

Directs the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), acting through the Assistant Secretary of the Office of the Infrastructure Protection, to examine gaps in emergency plan preparedness for vulnerable populations, including individuals with physical and mental disabilities, limited English Proficiency, and economically disadvantaged households and communities.

Small Company Capital Formation Act of 2011 - Amends the Securities Act of 1933 to exempt from the additional issues exemption any securities offered and sold in excess of $50 million in the prior 12 months.

Requires the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to by rule or regulation add a class of securities to the securities exempted pursuant to this Act in accordance with specified terms and conditions.

Authorizes the SEC to require an issuer of a class of securities exempted to make periodic disclosures regarding the issuer to investors and to suspend or terminate such disclosures when necessary to protect investors.

Requires the SEC to study and report to Congress on the impact of state laws regulating securities offerings, or "Blue Sky laws," on the regulation offerings offered by the SEC.

Federal Election Integrity Act of 2004 - Amends the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 to require the applicant for a Federal election to provide a photographic copy of any document which provides proof that the applicant is a U.S. citizen.

Requires the applicant for a State election to provide a photographic copy of any document which provides proof that the applicant is a U.S. citizen, in accordance with guidelines established by the Election Administration Commission (EAC).

Prohibits the appropriate State or local election official from: (1) providing a ballot for an election for Federal office (including an absentee ballot) unless the individual provides the official with a current and valid photo identification; or (2) accepting a ballot for an election for Federal office provided by an individual who votes by mail unless the individual submits with the ballot a copy of a current and valid photo identification.

Prohibits the appropriate State or local election official from accepting a ballot for an election provided by an individual who votes by mail unless the individual submits with the ballot a copy of a current and valid photo identification.

Prohibits the appropriate State or local election official from accepting a ballot provided by an individual who votes by mail
Child Care Lending Pilot Act of 2003 - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to authorize the use of child care loan proceeds for the purchase of a home for a child with a disability.

Flexible Refinancing for American Families Act of 2012 - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to carry out a program to provide for the refinancing of qualified mortgage mortgages on single-family housing owned by such enterprises through a refinancing mortgage having a 50-year term and for the purchase of and securitization of such mortgages, in accordance with policies and procedures that the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) shall establish.

Requires such program to require such mortgages to be refinished within 50 years of the beginning of the amortization of the mortgage and to fully amortize over such term, except that the mortgagee may require payment in full of all obligations owed on the date that is 30 years after the beginning of the amortization of the mortgage, but only if the mortgagee provides written notice to the mortgagor of such acceleration of indebtedness of not fewer than 90 days in advance of such acceleration.

Requires the mortgage to bear an interest rate that is equal to the premium received by the enterprise on the mortgage being refinanced plus the cost of selling

This bill authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to make a specified amount of new discretionary budget authority available for FY2010 for the VA health care system for: (1) medical services; (2) medical administration; (3) medical facilities; and (4) Clerical amendments to the table of sections at the beginning of this bill.  The VA must conduct a study of the adequacy and accuracy of the budget projections made by the Enrollee Health Care Projection Model (HCPM) as utilized for estimating and projecting VA health care expenditures with respect to the fiscal year involved and the subsequent four fiscal years.  The Government Accountability Office must report to Congress on the adequacy and accuracy of the budget projections made by the HCPM.

(Sec. 1) This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to conduct a study and report to the FCC on the filing requirements for eligible telecommunications carriers or service providers that receive universal service support under the Communications Act of 1934 for the provision of service under a Universal Service Fund (USF) program.  The FCC must: (1) analyze the filing requirements for covered carriers participating in a USF program, including any filings required by the FCC's Commission Administrative Company (CIC); (2) analyze the financial impact of those filing requirements on covered carriers participating in a USF program; and (3) make recommendations on how to consolidate redundant filing requirements for covered carriers participating in a USF program.  The FCC must initiate a rulemaking to consolidate redundant filing requirements for covered carriers participating in a USF program and incorporate the recommendations into an ongoing rulemaking for consolidating redundant filing requirements of the FCC. Hunt Unrestricted on National Treasures Act or the HUNT Act - Requires each head of a federal public land management agency to make a public access and egress list of the location and acreage of land more than 640 acres in size under the jurisdiction of such agency's land on which the public is allowed, under federal or state law, to hunt, fish, or use the land for other recreational purposes.

Requires the agency's plan for a land-based travel management plan to provide for such easement, right-of-way, or fee title acquisition.

Requires the agency's head to consider public access and egress to the legal boundaries of the land in determining whether public access and egress to such boundaries are reasonable and consistent with the travel management plan.

Amends the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965 to provide for recreational public access to federal land through easements, rights-of-way, or fee title acquisitions from willing sellers.

Clean Alternatives for Energy Independence Act of 2005 - Repeals certain tax credits for: (1) small refiners and small business users of energy; and (2) investment in fuel cell vehicles.

Increases the maximum credit for investment in fuel cell vehicles from $500 to $1,000.

Expands the number of new qualified fuel cell motor vehicles eligible for the fuel economy credit from 60,000 to 120,000.

Increases the credit for alternative fuel vehicle refueling property from $30,000 to $60,000.

Extends through 2019 the authorization of appropriations for the Department of Energy's (DOE) program to develop and implement hydrogen-related fuel cell vehicles.

Fixed Asset Relief Act of 2015  Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the maximum depreciation allowed in property to 100% and make permanent the alternative depreciation system for such property; (2) allow a 100% bonus depreciation for qualified property; and (3) allow a deduction for alternative minimum tax purposes.

Amends the Siletz Tribe Indian Restoration Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to accept title to any additional number of acres of real property located within the boundaries of the original 1855 Siletz Coast Reservation (established by Executive Order dated November 9, 1855) composed of land within the political boundaries of Benton, Douglas, Lane, Lincoln, Tillamook, and Yamhill Counties in Oregon, if such real property is conveyed or otherwise transferred to the United States by or on behalf of the tribe.

Requires that all real property that is taken into trust under this Act become part of the tribe's reservation.

Requires that any real property taken into trust be considered and evaluated as an on-reservation acquisition under part 151.10 of title 25, Code of Federal Regulations (or successor regulations), if the Board of County Commissioners or other appropriate County executive in which the real property is located submits written approval of that consideration and evaluation in the form of a resolution or other appropriate governing document.

Authorizes a Board of County Commissioners or other appropriate County executive that submits written approval to the Secretary to revoke such approval by submitting written documentation of the revocation in

Measuring the Economic Impact of Broadband Act of 2018 This bill requires the Department of Commerce, in consultation with the Bureau of Economic Analysis and the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information, to assess and analyze the effect of broadband deployment and adoption on the economy of the United States.

Increasing Medical Oversight in the Department of Veterans Affairs Act of 2014 - Establishes the Office of the Medical Inspector within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to: (1) review the quality of health care provided by VA health care providers and by VA health care agencies; (2) review the offices of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) that have an impact on the quality of health care provided to veterans by VA health care agencies and the performance of VA policies and procedures in providing such care; (3) review VHA offices and facilities that have an impact on the quality of health care provided to veterans and the performance of VA policies and procedures in providing such care; (4) review VHA offices and facilities that have an impact on the quality of health care provided to veterans and the performance of VA policies and procedures in providing such care; (5) review any systemic issues that arise within the VHA, including the performance of VA policies and procedures in providing such care; and (6) establish temporary investigative teams to review or investigate such issues. Requires the Medical Inspector to report to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) and the Under Secretary for Health (under Secretary) on any problems or deficiencies encountered in VA programs and operations,

Rehab and Ahmed Amer Foster Care Improvement Act of 2012 - Amends part E (Foster Care and Adoption Assistance) of title IV of the Social Security Act to require a state to: (1) exercise due diligence to identify and provide notice to all adult grandparents and other adult relatives of a removed child from the custody of the parent or parents of the child within 30 days after such removal; (2) provide such notice to each parent of the child, each relative who has expressed an interest in caring for the child, the guardian, and the guardian ad litem for the child, the attorney for the child, the attorney for each parent of the child, the child (if able to express an opinion regarding placement), and the prosecutor involved; and (3) establish procedures to allow a person who receives notice of a proposed placement decision to request documentation of the reasons for the decision, allow the attorney for the child to petition the court involved to review the decision, and require the court to conduct such review on the record.

National Strategic Gasoline Reserve for Purposes of National Security Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to establish a Strategic Gasoline Reserve system with a total capacity of 10 million barrels of regular unleaded gasoline.

Requires the Secretary to determine strategic locations for no less than three and no more than five Gasoline Reserve sites, each located in a different geographical region of the United States.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) initiate a transportation process to fill the Reserve to a minimum of 90% within two years of enactment of this Act; (2) conduct an annual review of the gasoline supply to ensure the reserves in the Reserve do not exceed their shelf life; (3) sell gasoline from the Reserve if the Governor of a state submits a written request that provides sufficient evidence that the sale or supply of gasoline in the region in which the state is located has been severely disrupted, caused by, but not limited to, an interruption in the normal distribution or availability of gasoline which dramatically affects the price of gasoline, and provides sufficient evidence that the state would experience further adverse effects without the sale of gasoline from the Reserve; and (4) sell gasoline from the Reserve if the President issues an executive order requiring immediate

Skill Game Protection Act - Amends the Wire Act to exclude from the definition of "bets or wagers," as defined by the Act, any operation of a game of skill on the Internet. 
Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to prescribe regulations requiring each person who operates a game of skill on the Internet to:  (1) maintain safeguards to ensure that the individual participating is 18 years of age or older; (2) ensure that all taxes relating to Internet games of skill due to Federal and State governments and to Indian tribes are collected as required by the time of payment of any proceeds of such games; (3) combat fraud and money laundering as may be prescribed by regulations issued by the Secretary or a designee of the Secretary; (4) combat compulsive participation in Internet games of skill; and (5) protect the privacy and security of any person engaged in such games of skill.

Spearfish Canyon and Bismarck Lake Land Exchange Act - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to convey specified federal land in South Dakota to the Secretary of Agriculture and the state of South Dakota if the state conveys to the Secretary all right, title, and interest of the state in and to the non-federal land, the Secretary shall convey to the state all interest of the United States in and to the federal land, and the Secretary shall select an appraiser to conduct appraisals of the federal land and non-federal land. Requires the value of the federal land and non-federal land to be determined based on the agricultural value of the federal land and non-federal land to be exchanged. Requires the exchange to be subject to any additional terms and conditions that the Secretary and the state may agree on.

Requires the non-federal land acquired by the Secretary under this Act to: (1) be added to, and administered as part of, the Black Hills National Forest in South Dakota; and (2) be managed in accordance with the laws applicable to the National Forest System.

Troubled Asset Relief Program Enhancement Act - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 (EESA) to require the Comptroller General (GAO) to be given access to all information, data, schedules, books, accounts, financial records, reports, files, electronic communications, or other papers, things, or property belonging to or in use by the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) of the federal government, or any TARP vehicle, officer, director, employee, or TARP agent, and to the officers, employees, directors, independent public accountants, financial advisors, or other TARP agents and their employees at such time as the Comptroller General may request.

Requires the Comptroller General to be afforded full facilities for verifying transactions with the balances or securities held by, and custodians of, such entities.

Prohibits the public disclosure of proprietary or trade secret information obtained under this Act.

Prohibits the Comptroller General from publicly disclosing proprietary or trade secret information obtained under this Act.

American Livestock Protection and Ranching Opportunity Act of 2014 - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) the overwhelming majority of consumers in the United States want to know where animals used to produce the meat is born, raised, and slaughtered; (2) country-of-origin labeling provides information consumers in the United States have a right to know; and (3) country-of-origin labeling facilitates supply chain information critical for food safety. Amends the Animal Health Protection Act to prohibit the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) from: (1) allowing the importation of fresh meat or meat products from a country with foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) without vaccination until the Secretary certifies to Congress that such country is free of FMD without vaccination, or initiate, administer, finalize, or enforce any rulemaking allowing for the importation of fresh meat or meat product from such country; or (2) providing grants to eligible entities for research and development relating to surveillance methods, vaccines, vaccination delivery systems, or diagnostic tests for diseases in domestic livestock that present a potential concern to public health and safety. Amends the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 to establish a livestock disease initiative to provide competitive grants

Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance Adjustment Act of 2002 - Amends Federal law to increase the rates of educational assistance for veterans and dependents through FY 2004. Revises the formula for determining the amount of a veteran's educational assistance allowance based on the amount of the veteran's active-duty service and the amount of the veteran's active-duty pay. Revises the formula for determining the amount of a veteran's vocational rehabilitation allowance based on the amount of the veteran's active-duty service and the amount of the veteran's active-duty pay. Revises the formula for determining the amount of a veteran's special training allowance based on the amount of the veteran's active-duty service and the amount of the veteran's active-duty pay. Revises the formula for determining the amount of a veteran's residential educational assistance allowance based on the amount of the veteran's active-duty service and the amount of the veteran's active-duty pay. Revises the formula for determining the amount of a veteran's other educational assistance allowance based on the amount of the veteran's active-duty service and the amount of the veteran's active-duty pay. Revises the formula for determining the amount of a veteran's other vocational

Strengthening Entrepreneurs' Economic Development Act of 2013 - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to establish a program of direct loans and other loans to small businesses that have less than 20 employees.  Directs the Administrator to establish a process for lenders to apply for such loans.  Requires the Administrator to: (1) establish a process for lenders to apply for loans under the SBA's Direct Loan Program, and (2) offer to sell such loans.  Amends the Small Business Act to direct the SBA to assess, collect, and retain a fee not to exceed a certain percentage of the outstanding balance of the deferred participation share of the loan.

Affordable Housing Preservation and Revitalization Act of 2009 - Amends the United States Housing Act of 1937 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to ensure that funds in the residual receipts account of an eligible multifamily housing property are transferred to a preservation entity for: (1) rehabilitation costs; (2) social and other services that directly benefit the tenants of the property; or (3) any other costs that have been approved by the housing agency.

District of Columbia Government Improvement and Efficiency Act of 1996 - Amends the District of Columbia Code to reduce the number of members of the District of Columbia Board of Trustees from 45 to 25. 
Repeals the application of the Servic Contract Act of 1965 to the District of Columbia. 
Authorizes the Mayor of the District of Columbia and the Director of the Bureau of Prisons to enter into an agreement waiving the requirements of the Service Contract Act of 1965 for certain District of Columbia convicts so long as notice is given to the congressional committees on the subject. 
Amends the District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act to exempt certain District of Columbia employees of the Office of the Inspector General from certain requirements of the Code relating to the duty to appear before the Board at the request of the Commissioner of Inspector General. 
Amends the District of Columbia Government Comprehensive Merit Personnel Act of 1978 to authorize the Director of Personnel to waive the application of certain requirements of the Code to certain employees of the Office of the Inspector General. 
Amends the District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act

Children's Express Lane to Health Coverage Act of 2003 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to authorize a State to base a child's eligibility for Medicaid or Child Health Assistance on financial determinations made by a program providing nutrition or other public assistance.

State Prescription Drug Discount Act of 2002 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require a manufacturer of a drug that is covered under Medicaid (Medicare+State Children's Health Insurance Program) to enter into an agreement with a state prescription drug discount program to provide rebate payments for drugs covered by such a program in the same amounts as are paid by the manufacturer to the state for such drugs under a rebate agreement. Defines "state prescription drug discount program" as a State program under which, with respect to a rebate period, not less than 95 percent of all the rebates paid to the state under such agreements are provided to eligible state residents in the form of discounted prices for the purchase of outpatient prescription drugs. Prohibits any offset against medical assistance.

Minuteman Missile National Historic Site Establishment Act of 1998 - Establishes the Minuteman Missile National Historic Site in South Dakota as a unit of the National Park System. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to make minor adjustments to the boundary of the Site. 
Requires the Secretary to consult with the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of State to ensure that administration of the Site is in compliance with applicable treaties. 
Authorizes the Secretary to acquire lands and interests therein within the Site's boundaries by donation, purchase, exchange, or transfer from another Federal agency. 
Requires the Secretary to prepare a general management plan for the Site. 
Requires the Secretary to consider consolidating or coordinating appropriate administrative, management, and personnel functions with other Federal lands and airfields in order to develop the plan. 
Authorizes appropriations. 
Requires the Secretary of the Air Force to transfer to the Secretary any funds specifically appropriated to the Air Force for the maintenance, protection, or preservation of the facilities described in this Act. 
Requires the Secretary to transfer such funds to the Secretary for the Legacy Resource Management Program.

Provides that procedures for consideration of such a joint resolution shall apply only to the consideration of such a resolution in the same manner as such procedures apply to a joint resolution concerning the defense personnel management system of the Department of Defense.
Provides that the Federal Advisory Committee Act shall not apply to the Commission.
Provides that Congress shall in the concurrent resolution on the budget for the fiscal year beginning on the following October 1 establish a limit on total outlays to be made under the Medicare program for the fiscal year.
Provides that if Congress has not enacted a joint resolution under the Medicare Act of 1995 before the first day of the fiscal year, there shall be a sequestration to eliminate any budgetary excess in the Medicare program.
Requires: (1) reductions under this Act in amounts under the Medicare program for the fiscal year; and (2) reports on the date on which such sequestration takes place.

Theodore Roosevelt Wildlife Legacy Act of 1997 - Requires the Secretary of the Interior to:  (1) ensure that the mission and purposes of the National Wildlife Refuge System (NWPS) are carried out; (2) ensure that opportunities for the use of the System are wildlife observation and photography, hunting, fishing, and environmental education and interpretation; and (3) plan, propose, and direct expansion of the NWPS, to accomplish the System's purposes and the purposes of each National Wildlife Refuge, and to contribute to the conservation of the ecosystems of the United States. 
Prohibits the Secretary from initiating or permitting a new use of a National Wildlife Refuge or expanding, renew, or extending an existing allowed use unless the Secretary determines that the use is compatible with the primary purposes of the refuge and the System's mission and purposes. 
Requires the Secretary to:  (1) identify, prior to acquisition, existing compatible priority public uses that shall be permitted to continue on an interim basis pending completion of comprehensive planning; and (2) develop and implement a process to ensure an opportunity for public involvement in the preparation and revision of conservation plans. 
Requires the Secretary to prepare a conservation plan for any refuge established after this Act

Government Shutdown Prevention Act - Amends Federal law to provide for continuing appropriations (i.e., funds provided in the current fiscal year to cover the costs of continuing appropriations in the current fiscal year) in the absence of regular appropriations for a fiscal year.

Investment Tax Incentive Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow the deduction of accelerated cost recovery system (ACC) for certain property placed in service in taxable years beginning after December 31, 1992. 
Repeals provisions of the increased tax rate provisions of the ADDITIVE TAX which apply to depreciable property placed in service in taxable years beginning after December 31, 1992.

Deter Revolving-door Appointments In Our Nation; Stop Washington Appointees from becoming Manipulative Petitioners Act or the DRAIN the SWAMP Act  This bill amends the federal criminal code to impose a five-year ban on a political appointee of the executive branch who knowingly serves as a registered lobbyist for a foreign government.  The bill amends the Foreign Agents Registration Act of 1938 to prohibit a political appointee from registering as a foreign agent of a foreign government if the appointee is subject to the restrictions contained in this Act.

Requires a dealer to disclose, to each consumer who purchases a new automobile, in a clear and conspicuous written format at the time of purchase, the presence and location of an event data recorder installed in the automobile, as well as the type of information recorded by the recorder and the potential use of such information in a law enforcement proceeding.

Requires the manufacturer of such an automobile to include in the owner's manual such disclosures.

Provides that: (1) any event data recorder in the vehicle and recorded information on such recorder may not be downloaded or otherwise retrieved by a person other than the owner; and (2) any information recorded by such recorder may not be the subject of a court order to recover the costs of replacing the vehicle or restoring it to its former condition.
