Stabilize Medicaid and CHIP Coverage Act - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to revise requirements for a state Medicaid or CHIP plan to provide that an individual who is determined to be eligible for benefits under such plan shall remain eligible and enrolled through the end of the month in which the 12-month period ends.

Amends title XXI (Children's Health Insurance Program) (CHIP) of the Social Security Act to revise requirements for a state CHIP plan to provide that an individual who is determined to be eligible for benefits under such plan shall remain enrolled through the end of the month in which the 12-month period ends.

Authorizes a state to elect through a state plan amendment to apply the above requirements on any date before the enactment of this Act.

National Milestones to Measure Progress in Ending the Opioid Epidemic Act of 2018 This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop national indicators to measure success in curtailing the opioid epidemic, with the goal of significantly reversing the toll of opioid misuse and opioid-related morbidity and mortality in the United States within five years of this bill's enactment.  The indicators shall include: (1) a reduction in fatal and non-fatal opioid overdose and emergency room visits, (2) an increase in public and provider education, (3) an increase in the number of individuals in sustained recovery from opioid use disorder, (4) an increase in the number of providers prescribing medically assisted treatment for opioid use disorder in different settings, (5) an increase in the number of harm reduction organizations, (6) an increase in the number of individuals admitted to opioid use disorder treatment, and (7) additional indicators or metrics, such as metrics pertaining to specific populations, including women and children, American Indians and Alaska Natives, individuals living in rural and non-urban areas, and justice-involved populations.  HHS may extend the period for meeting the goal of not fewer than 10 indicators or metrics if the goal

Deems the full equalization of allotments within the meaning of the Act entitled "An Act to provide for the equalization of allotments on the Agua Caliente (Palm Springs) Reservation in California, and for other purposes," approved September 21, 1959, commonly known as the "Agua Caliente Equalization Act of 1959, to have been completed.
Deems the fourth undesignated paragraph of such Act to be repealed.
Applies such provisions to the Band as of March 31, 1983.
Provides that any per capita distribution of tribal revenues of the Band made after this Act's enactment date shall be made to all members.

Special Needs Trust Fairness and Medicaid Improvement Act (Sec. 1) This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to modify the definition of "woman" under title XIX to make the individual subject to Medicaid coverage if the woman is pregnant for the first time. (Sec. 2) The bill also amends title XIX to eliminate federal financial participation in the Medicaid program for cosmetic purposes and for hair growth. (Sec. 3) The bill eliminates the requirement that a state Medicaid program provide a woman covered by title XIX with Medicaid coverage of tobacco cessation services through 2022. (Sec. 4) The bill eliminates the requirement that a state Medicaid program provide additional funding for the drug program for cosmetic purposes or hair growth. (Sec. 5) The Medicaid Improvement Fund is expanded to provide additional funding for FY2021 and FY2022.

Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to require a member of a reserve component who is ordered to report for military service for more than 90 days and who on the date of such order resides at real property that is occupied by the member or dependents of the member as the primary residence to not be required to pay rent under that lease for any period of such military service during which the member is assigned to duty at a location sufficiently distant from such property that the member is unable to reside at such property.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a refundable tax credit for lessors of real property used for the rental of a reserve component member.

Patent and Trademark Office Authorization Act of 2002 - Authorizes appropriations for the United States Patent and Trademark Office for FY 2003 through 2008, and for other purposes.

Requires the Director of the Office to develop an electronic filing and processing system for the filing and processing of patent and trademark applications that: (1) is user-friendly and includes the necessary infrastructure to allow examiners and applicants to send all communications electronically and allow the Office to process, maintain, and search electronically the contents and history of each application; and (2) is developed and implemented by the Director by December 1, 2004.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce to submit annual reports on the progress made in implementing the 21st Century Strategic Plan issued on June 3, 2002, and any amendments made to it.

Authorizes the third-party request for an appeal of a final decision favorable to patentability of any original or proposed amended or new claim of the patent and subject to certain conditions, including that the patent owner has a right of appeal.

Authorizes appeals from the Board of Patent Appeals and the Federal Circuit for inter part

Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend temporarily the duty on three-ring binders (a type of textile product designed to contain standard sheets of letter-sized paper measuring approximately 51 by 280 mm).

Wholesale Motor Fuel Fairness and Competition Restoration Act - Prohibits any owner or operator of a terminal facility from selling motor fuel from the terminal facility to a distributor or retailer at a price in excess of the price it charges any other distributor or retailer, including a distributor or retailer which it owns or with which it is affiliated. 
Authorizes the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to assess a civil penalty for violations of this Act.  Sets forth provisions regarding criminal penalties for knowingly violating this Act. 
Requires the FTC to issue regulations requiring full disclosure by refiners and distributors of their wholesale motor fuel pricing policies, including rebates, incentives, and market enhancement allowances. 
Requires the FTC to transmit to the Congress a report regarding whether ownership or operation by a refiner of a facility for the retail sale of motor fuel has anticompetitive effects on the price of motor fuel.

Foreign Medical School Accountability Fairness Act of 2013 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to repeal the requirement that at least 60% of applicants for a graduate medical school (GME) in the Caribbean region be non-U.S. nationals or permanent resident of Canada or U.S. nationals.  Extends the expiration date of the authority of a graduate medical school (GME) to participate in the federal student aid programs under title IV of the Act to the first July 1 following the enactment of this Act.  Allows a student who is enrolled at a GME on or before the date of enactment of this Act to continue to receive a loan under title IV while attending such GME in which the student was enrolled upon the date of enactment of this Act, subject to the student continuing to meet all applicable academic requirements, until the earliest of: (1) withdrawal by the student from the GME, (2) completion of the program of study at the GME, or (3) the fourth June 30 after such withdrawal.

Disclosure; and Encouragement of Verification, Innovation, Cleaning, and Efficiency Act of 2017 or the DEVICE Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require a manufacturer of a device to give the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) prior to any change to its design or reprocessing instructions that is marketed in interstate commerce.  The bill also requires a device manufacturer to report to the FDA within five days of a communication to the FDA relating to a change to its design, recommended reprocessing protocols, or safety concerns regarding the device. The bill requires a device manufacturer to also report to the FDA within five days of any communication to the FDA relating to a change to its recommended reprocessing protocols, if any, for the device, or a safety concern about the device. The bill requires a device manufacturer to report to the FDA within five days of any communication to the FDA relating to a change to its reusable device. The bill requires the FDA to publish a list of types of rapid assessment tests for which FDA reports must include validated instructions for use and validated data for the types of tests.

ESA Improvement Act of 2014 - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to prohibit the Secretary of the Interior from including in a list of endangered or threatened species any population of a species if the Secretary has approved a State Protective Action for such population in accordance with this Act.  Requires the Secretary to notify each state in which a population of the species occurs of the opportunity to submit a proposed State Protective Action for the species in that state, including specification of the criteria for approval of such an action.  Requires the Secretary to notify each state in which such a population occurs of the opportunity to submit a proposed State Protective Action for the species within specified time periods.  Authorizes each state to submit a proposed State Protective Action for the species in such state or states within the period specified by the Secretary for the submission of public comment regarding the inclusion of the species in the list.  Requires the Secretary to: (1) approve or disapprove a proposed State Protective Action by not later than 45 days after it is submitted, (2) approve such an action if the Secretary determines that it meets the criteria specified for approval in the notification, and (3) approve such an action if the Secretary determines that it meets the criteria

This bill authorizes the Coast Guard to exempt a passenger vessel of the United States having berth or fellow room accommodations for at least 50 passengers from certain fire-retardant standards if the vessel:  is constructed of fire-retardant materials; operates engines, boilers, main electrical distribution panels, fuel tanks, oil tanks, and generators that meet current Coast Guard regulations; operates boilers and main electrical generators that are contained within noncombustible enclosures equipped with fire suppression systems; and has multiple forms of egress off the vessel's bow and stern.  Before December 1, 2028, the Coast Guard is prohibited from disclaiming liability to a passenger or crew member for death, injury, or any other loss caused by fire due to the negligence of the vessel's owner or managing operator.  The Coast Guard must annually inspect any vessel exempted from such standards.

Health Care for Young Adults Act of 2005 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to provide for State option for providing State option for Medicaid and Medicare coverage of young adults (currently, only under SSA title XIX (Medicaid) with respect to children and under SSA title XXI (State Children's Health Insurance Program [SCHIP] with respect to individuals under SSA title XXI).

Provides for additional State allotments for providing coverage of optional young adults.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide for grants to States to implement expansions of eligibility for children and young adults their State medicaid plans under SSA title XIX (Medicaid) and State child health plans under SSA title XXI (SCHIP).

Lower Colorado River Multi-Species Conservation Program Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to implement the LCR MSCP in accordance with Program Documents.

Authorizes the Secretary to enter into an agreement with the states providing for the use of water from the Lower Colorado River for habitat creation and maintenance in accordance with the Program Documents.

Authorizes the Secretary to invest with the Secretary of the Treasury such portions of appropriations and any non-Federal contributions made pursuant to the Program Documents as are not required to meet current expenditures.

Requires that all amounts appropriated to and expended by the Secretary for the LCR MSCP be non-reimbursable and non-returnable.

Authorizes the Secretary to commence a civil action in U.S. district court to enforce a previous agreement entered into under this Act. Allows the U.S. or any agency to be named as a defendant in such actions.

Waives the sovereign immunity of the United States to claims for money damages, compensation, the provision of indemnity, or any claim seeking money from the United States.

Authorizes the United States or any agency to be named as a defendant in such actions.

Rocky Mountain National Park Wilderness Act of 1997 - Designates specified lands in Rocky Mountain National Park, Colorado, as wilderness and, together with such lands, shall be known as the Rocky Mountain National Park Wilderness. 
Requires the Secretary of the Interior to:  (1) file a map and a boundary description of the area so designated with the House Committee on Energy and Natural Resources and the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources; and (2) take all steps necessary to protect the rights reserved by this Act. 
Reserves a quantity of water sufficient to fulfill the purposes of that wilderness designation. 
Requires the priority date of the water rights reserved in this Act to be the date of enactment of this Act. 
Requires the Secretary and other appropriate U.S. officers to protect the rights reserved by this Act, including the filing by the Secretary of a claim for the quantification of such right in any present or future appropriate stream adjudication in the courts of the State of Colorado in which the United States has been or is hereafter properly joined in accordance with the McCarran Amendment. 
Deems such lands to be wilderness and reserves a quantity of water sufficient to fulfill the purposes of that wilderness designation.

Congenital Heart Futures Reauthorization Act of 2015 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to enhance and expand research and surveillance infrastructure to study and track the epidemiology of congenital heart disease. The CDC must plan, develop, implement, and submit one or more reports to Congress on a cohort study to improve understanding of the epidemiology of congenital heart disease across the lifespan. The CDC must establish and implement an awareness, outreach, and education campaign regarding congenital heart disease. The campaign must emphasize that congenital heart disease is the most prevalent birth defect and that it affects those diagnosed throughout their lives. The CDC must also: (1) coordinate research efforts related to congenital heart disease among multiple research institutions and (2) identify the areas of greatest need for such research. The CDC must report to Congress on its research efforts and the areas of greatest need for such research.

Small Business Lending to Entrepreneurs for Growth in Underserved Populations Act of 2011 or the Small Business Leg-Up Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer all unobligated funds in the Small Business Lending Fund to the Community Development Financial Institutions Fund.

Amends the Small Business Jobs Act of 2010 to require that: (1) all funds received by the Secretary in connection with purchases made pursuant to this Act, including principal, interest payments, dividend payments, and proceeds from the sale of any financial instrument, be transferred to the Fund; and (2) eligible community development financial institutions (i.e., financial institutions with assets of $10 billion or less) may apply to receive capital investments in an amount not exceeding 10% of total assets or such other percentage as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

Requires the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to carry out a Small Business Capital Investment Program to make capital investments in eligible community development financial institutions in order to increase the availability of credit for small businesses.

Authorizes the Administrator to issue regulations to carry out the Program.

Interstate Transport Act of 2018 This bill prohibits a person who is not otherwise prohibited by any federal law from transporting a knife for any lawful purpose from any place where the person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport the knife to any other place where the person may lawfully do so if: (1) in the case of transport by motor vehicle, the knife is not directly accessible from the passenger compartment of the motor vehicle or is contained in a locked container, and (2) in the case of a motor vehicle without a compartment separate from the passenger compartment, the knife is contained in a locked container.  A person may carry in the passenger compartment of a passenger aircraft a knife or tool: (1) the blades of which consist only of a blunt tipped safety blade, a guarded blade, or both, and that is specifically designed for enabling escape in an emergency by cutting safety belts; and (2) the blade that is specifically designed for enabling escape in an emergency by cutting safety belts, and that is contained in a locked container.  A person may not be required to secure such a knife in a locked container.  A person who is transporting a knife in compliance with this bill may not be arrested for the unlawful possession or transport of a knife

Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to grant an easement or right-of-way on the outer Continental Shelf or activities not otherwise authorized in such Act when such activities: (1) support exploration, development, production, transportation, or storage of oil, natural gas, or other minerals; (2) produce or support production, transportation, or transmission of energy from sources other than oil and gas; or (3) use facilities currently or previously used for activities authorized under such Act.

Requires the Secretary to establish reasonable forms of annual or one-time payments for any easement or right-of-way granted under such Act, including fees, rentals, or cash bonus payments.

Requires the Secretary to prescribe any necessary regulations to assure safety, protection of the environment, prevention of waste, and conservation of natural resources of the outer Continental Shelf.

Requires the holder of an easement or right-of-way granted under this Act to furnish a surety bond or other form of security as prescribed by the Secretary and to comply with such other requirements as the Secretary may deem necessary to protect the interests of the United States.

Directs the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to report to Congress: (1) a focused, in-depth Independent Safety Assessment of the design, construction, maintenance, and operational safety performance of the systems at the Indian Point Energy Center, Units 2 and 3, located in Westchester County, New York; and (2) a comprehensive evaluation of the radiological emergency plan for Indian Point Energy Center, Units 2 and 3, conducted by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's Independent Safety Assessment Team to conduct the system-level independent safety assessment of the Indian Point Nuclear Power Plant.

Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to monitor the system-level independent safety assessment by an observation group and a citizens' review team.

Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to enter into final determinations of whether to renew the operating licenses for Unit 2 or Unit 3 at the Indian Point Energy Center until the Commission has: (1) fully reported to the public on the Independent Safety Assessment of the system-level performance of the plants; and (2) accepted and implemented all recommendations of the Independent Safety Assessment.

Alaska Native Veterans Land Allotment Equity Act - Amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to provide that any person who qualifies for an allotment under the Act on land that is vacant, selected by, or conveyed to the State of Alaska by a Native Corporation or a native person who voluntarily relinquishes or conveys to the United States land for the allotment shall be eligible to receive such allotment within three years after such regulations are promulgated.

Authorizes an individual who qualifies for such an allotment on land within the boundaries of a right-of-way of the TransAlaska Pipeline or an inner or outer corridor of such a right-of-way to select an alternative allotment from land that is withdrawn or is not within a National Park.

Authorizes a person who qualifies for such an allotment on land that was originally conveyed to the individual to withdraw and reselect such land after enactment of this Act, if the land originally selected was not conveyed to the individual.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to issue a certificate of allotment as to the right of a person or entity to receive an allotment in the form of a private contest or protest if the applicant has an interest in the land that was originally conveyed to the applicant.

Clean Water Compliance and Ratepayer Affordability Act of 2015 This bill requires the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to carry out a pilot program to work with and facilitate the efforts of municipalities to develop and implement integrated plans to meet their wastewater and stormwater obligations under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (commonly known as the Clean Water Act) in a cost-effective and flexible manner. The EPA must select at least 15 municipalities to participate in the pilot program each fiscal year. The EPA must give priority to municipalities that are operating under an administrative order, administrative consent agreement, or judicial consent decree to comply with the requirements of the Clean Water Act. The EPA may give priority to a municipality seeking to develop and implement an integrated plan that includes adaptive approaches to account for changed or future uncertain circumstances. The EPA may also modify the implementation terms of a consent decree to: (1) extend the allowable national pollutant discharge elimination system permit term, (2) modify the implementation terms of a consent decree, and (3) provide additional regulatory flexibility in approving and implementing an integrated plan that includes adaptive approaches.

National Heroes Credit Protection Act - Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to authorize a member of a reserve component who serves on active duty outside the continental United States in support of a contingency operation to request that a consumer reporting agency include a military service deployment explanation for a credit or consumer report. Requires such an explanation to: (1) be included in the file of the member's active-duty service, and (2) be developed and maintained by the agency.

Requires a reseller of a servicemember to include in any report of the reseller on such member any such military service deployment explanation.

Requires any prospective user of a consumer credit report containing a military service deployment explanation to acknowledge such explanation.

Defines "eligible servicemember" as a member of a reserve component who serves on active duty outside the continental United States in support of a contingency operation in support of a call or order specifying a period of at least 180 days (or who enters such service under a call or order specifying a period of 180 days or less and who, without a break in service, receives orders extending the period of such service to a period of not less than 180 days.

EINSTEIN Act of 2015 This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to deploy, operate, and maintain capabilities to protect federal agency information and civilian information systems, including technologies to diagnose, prevent, and mitigate against cybersecurity risks.  DHS may: (1) access, and federal agency heads may disclose to DHS or a private entity providing assistance, information traveling to or from or stored on a federal civilian information system, regardless of from where the information or assistance is accessed, notwithstanding any other provision of law that would otherwise restrict or prevent federal agency heads from disclosing such information or assistance; (2) enter into agreements or requests to deploy, operate, and maintain technologies to protect federal civilian information systems; and (3) retain, use, and disclose information obtained through such activities only to protect federal agency information and federal civilian information systems from cybersecurity risks or in furtherance of the national cybersecurity and communications integration center's authority to investigate, prosecute, or respond to violations of the national cybersecurity and communications integration center's national cybersecurity and communications security reporting requirements.  DHS contracts or agreements shall include provisions barring: (1) the disclosure of information to any entity other than

Medicare Drug Formulary Protection Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise the prescription drug plan (PDP) formula to remove covered drugs from the PDP formula and impose restrictions or limitations on coverage.

Provides for an annual notice of changes in the formulary and other restrictions or limitations on coverage for covered drugs.

Rail Merger Reform and Customer Protection Act - Amends Federal transportation law to revise the Surface Transportation Board's jurisdiction and authority to review surface transportation board actions involving rail competition and alternative transportation methods.

Revises the Sherman Act exemption from antitrust laws for certain determinations made by the Board regarding the competitive use of rail by rail carriers.

Revises the scope of authority of the Board to exercise its antitrust laws remedies.

Prohibits a person proceeding against a rail carrier under Federal or State law, with respect to the same claim, from proceeding against the same rail carrier under other Federal or State law, with respect to the same claim.

Amends the Clayton Act to prohibit a person proceeding against a rail carrier under Federal or State law, with respect to the same claim, from proceeding against the same rail carrier under other Federal or State law, with respect to the same claim, with respect to the same rail carrier.

Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial 1-Cent Coin Redesign Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to issue one-cent coins in accordance with specifications for a reverse side bearing four different designs representing different aspects of the life of Abraham Lincoln.

Requires the reverse side of the coins to bear four different designs representing different aspects of the life of Abraham Lincoln.

Requires the Secretary to prescribe the number of one-cent coins to be issued with each of the four designs selected for each calendar quarter of 2009.

Requires the reverse side of the coins to bear an image emblematic of President Lincoln's preservation of the United States of America as a single and united country.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the original Victor David Brenner design for the one-cent coin was a dramatic departure from previous American coinage that should be reproduced, using the original form and relief of the likeness of Abraham Lincoln, on the one-cent coins issued in 2009.

Energy Efficient Buildings Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to establish a pilot program to award grants to businesses and organizations for new construction of energy efficient buildings, or major renovations of buildings that will result in energy efficient buildings, to demonstrate innovative energy efficiency technologies, especially those sponsored by the Department of Energy.

Requires the Secretary to give due consideration to proposals for buildings that are likely to serve low and moderate income populations.

Prohibits any single grantee from being eligible for more than 3 grants per year under this program.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on the total number and cost of grants awarded, as well as an estimate of aggregate cost and energy savings enabled by the pilot program.

Prosperous and Secure Neighbor Alliance Act of 2007 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to direct the President, acting through the Director of Foreign Assistance, to provide assistance to improve security and promote economic development in Mexico by: (1) professionalizing Mexican law enforcement personnel to prepare such law enforcement personnel to more effectively combat illicit drugs and drug-related violence and other criminal activities; (2) providing technology to assist Mexican law enforcement personnel to more effectively combat illicit drugs and drug-related violence; (3) strengthening the Mexican judicial branch through the training of judges and prosecutors; (4) supporting anti-corruption programs; and (5) reducing poverty through targeted funding to enhance social development.

Requires the President to conduct an annual evaluation of the results of the specific programs, projects, and activities carried out under this Act.

Authorizes appropriations.

Expresses the sense of Congress that, of the amounts appropriated pursuant to this Act: (1) $40 million should be made available to carry out this Act; (2) $50 million should be made available to carry out this Act; (3) $20 million should be made available to carry out this Act;

Social Security Lock-Box Act of 2005 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to make it out of order in the House of Representatives or the Senate to consider any concurrent budget resolution that sets forth totalities for any fiscal year with respect to the Social Security Trust Funds that are less than the totalities of the Social Security Trust Funds for that fiscal year as calculated in accordance with a current services baseline.

Provides that such prohibition shall not apply to the extent that a violation would result from an assumption in the budget, amendment, or conference report, as applicable, of an increase in outlays or a decrease in revenues and disbursements relative to the baseline underlying that budget resolution for social security reform legislation for any such fiscal year.

Provides that, if a concurrent budget resolution would be in violation of this prohibition because of an assumption of an increase in outlays or a decrease in revenues relative to the baseline, then that resolution shall include a statement identifying any such increase or decrease.

Provides that, for purposes of enforcing any point of order under this Act, the totals of the Social Security Trust Funds for a fiscal year shall be the levels set forth in the later of the report accompanying the concurrent budget resolution
Economic Recovery Through Responsible Ownership Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a refundable credit for the purchase of a residence in 2009 or 2010.

Creating Opportunities for Rural Economic Expansion Act or the CORE Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allocate a specified percentage of the new markets tax credit limitation to qualified coal community investment. Defines "qualified coal community investment" as any capital or equity investment in, or loan to, any qualified active distressed coal community business, the purchase from another community development entity of any loan made by such entity which is a qualified coal community investment, financial counseling and other services specified in regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury to businesses located in, and residents of, distressed coal communities, and any equity investment in, or loan to, any qualified community development entity in connection with qualified investments the proceeds of which are substantially used to make qualified coal community investments.

Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to certify to the Secretary of Commerce that: (1) a consignee of any imported foreign commodity will use the commodity for the purpose stated in the end-use certificate; and (2) the end-use certificates currently held by the consignee are relevant to the purpose of the transaction.
Requires the Commodity Credit Corporation (CCC) to provide a person with an opportunity for a hearing before suspending or debarming the person from participation in an agricultural trade program for using a foreign agricultural commodity in violation of the terms and conditions of the program.

Higher Education Accrediting Agency Responsibility Act of 2002 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to: (1) make the accrediting agencies responsible for providing comparative information about the quality of institutions of higher education; (2) eliminate the requirement that institutions of higher education be accredited by a accrediting agency; and (3) make title III institutions eligible for financial assistance under the Aid to Which Aid to Families with Dependent Children Act of 1996.Repeals title III provisions that require the National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity to disclose foreign gifts to institutions of higher education.Amends the HBCU Capital Financing Act to make HBCU capital financing eligible for title III financial assistance.Repeals the requirement that institutions of higher education (IHEs) be accredited by a accrediting agency.

Debt Relief and IMF Reform Act of 1999 - Amends the Bretton Woods Agreements Act to prohibit any U.S. officer, employee, or agent from providing any thing of value to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for the purpose of providing resources to the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility or other concessional lending facility of the IMF. 
Prohibits the IMF Director from using any IMF resources for debt relief, including the use of IMF residual proceeds for such purpose. 
Prohibits any IMF funds from being appropriated for the IMF until the IMF has cancelled all debts owed to the Fund by the eligible countries and has financed such debt cancellation from ongoing operations, procedures, and accounts of the Fund. 
Prohibits any IMF governor or alternate appointed to represent the United States at the IMF from voting for any proposal for any quota increase for the IMF, unless the IMF receives notice of the proposal and the position of the Executive Branch on it.

Directs the Election Assistance Commission to establish a program to make grants to participating states and local governments for carrying out a program to make backup paper ballots available in the case of the failure of a voting system or equipment or other emergency situation in the administration of the regularly scheduled general election for federal office held in November 2008.

Clean Slate for Kids Online Act of 2018 This bill amends the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 to require a website operator to: (1) notify a child over the age of 13 or a legal guardian of an individual over the age of 13 that the operator deletes personal information collected from or about the individual when the individual was a child; (2) provide a written confirmation of deletion to an individual or legal guardian of such individual who requested such deletion; and (3) provide to the extent necessary to respond to judicial process or to provide information to law enforcement agencies or for an investigation on a matter related to public safety that the personal information is only for the extent that it is necessary to respond to judicial process or to provide information to law enforcement agencies or for an investigation on a matter related to public safety that the personal information is only for the extent permitted under any other provision of law.

Access to Inpatient Rehabilitation Therapy Act of 2017 This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to include recreational therapy services among the therapeutic modalities that constitute an intensive rehabilitation therapy program in determining whether inpatient services in an inpatient rehabilitation facility are reasonable and necessary.

America's Cup Act of 2011 - Authorizes an eligible vessel, operating only in preparation for, or in connection with, the 34th America's Cup, to position competing vessels and may transport individuals and equipment and supplies utilized for the staging, operations, or broadcast of the competition from and around U.S. ports.

Prohibits an Eligibility Certification from being conclusive evidence to the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) of the Maritime Administration of the Department of Transportation (DOT) that a vessel is a competing vessel or a supporting vessel.

Subjects a vessel not in compliance with certain requirements for a vessel operating in the United States under the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Waterway System or the Alaska Waterway System to certain penalties.

Authorizes the coastwise endorsement for a vessel to carry natural gas, as defined by this Act.

Prohibits a vessel transported in Dry Dock #2 (state of Alaska registration AIDEA FDD-2) from being merchandise for purposes of certain requirements for certain vessels operating in Alaska.

Portable Fuel Container Safety Act of 2017 This bill requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to promulgate a final rule for flame mitigation devices in portable fuel containers that impedes the propagation of flame into a container, except as provided in this bill, that is designed to protect against accidental ignition of gasoline, kerosene, or diesel fuel. The rule shall be promulgated in accordance with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) aviation safety code and shall be treated as a consumer product safety rule under the Consumer Product Safety Act (CPSA). A rule shall not apply if the CPSA governing standard is not met. The bill also amends the Children's Gasoline Burn Prevention Act to require gasoline containers to be packaged in a manner that is designed to protect against accidental ignition of gasoline, kerosene, or diesel fuel.

Social Security Preservation through Individual Choice Enhancement Act - Amends the Tax Relief, Unemployment Insurance Reauthorization, and Job Creation Act of 2010 (TUJIL) to allow an individual to elect to take a specified payroll tax cut under TUJIL if the individual has a calendar year in which the individual's wages are in the range of $600 or more, and the individual's employer has a payroll tax holiday election in effect on such calendar year.

Allows an individual to revoke such election before or with the beginning of such calendar year.

Allows an individual to increase the retirement age for self-employment in connection with such election.

Directs the Secretary of the Air Force to carry out a demonstration program to assess the feasibility and advisability of permitting individuals with auditory impairments (including deafness) to access as officers of the Air Force.

Requires the total number of individuals with auditory impairments who may participate in the program to be no fewer than 15 individuals or more than 20 individuals.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) publicize the program nationally, including to individuals who have auditory impairments and would be otherwise qualified for officer training; (2) create a process whereby interested individuals can apply for the program; and (3) select the program participants from among the pool of applicants, based on the criteria in a specified manner.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) designate a special advisor to the program, (2) ensure that participants have the necessary auxiliary aids and services to fully participate, and (3) report to the appropriate congressional committees on the program.

Protect Children from Video Game Sex and Violence Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit the sale or rental of any video game that depicts nudity, sexual conduct, or other content harmful to minors. Establishes criminal penalties for knowingly violating such prohibition.

ED 1.0 Act - Establishes within the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) a four-year pilot program to award competitive grants to eligible institutions of higher education to develop digital and wireless networks for online educational programs of study within those institutions.

Gives priority to institutions serving communities in counties where: (1) at least 50% of the residents are members of a racial or ethnic minority; (2) there is a high unemployment rate; (3) there is a negative population growth rate; or (4) there are median family incomes of $32,000.

Hospital Price Reporting and Disclosure Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require hospitals and ambulatory surgical centers (ASCs) to report data on: (1) the frequency with which they perform certain services, such as hospital-wide blood pressure measurement, on an inpatient or outpatient basis; (2) the number of times they administer certain drugs, such as certain pain medications, during such periods; and (3) the average and median charge by the hospital for such services or drugs.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to: (1) provide hospitals and ASCs with publicly available data on such services and drugs; and (2) periodically post such data on the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) public Internet site.

Requires hospitals and ASCs to prominently post at each admission site a notice of the availability of the data reported on the Internet site.

Directs the Secretary to select the following: (1) 25 most frequently performed services in a hospital inpatient setting, 25 most frequently performed services in a hospital outpatient setting, 25 most frequently performed services in an ambulatory surgical center setting, and 50 the 25 most frequently

Nuclear Innovation Act This bill directs the Department of Energy (DOE) to carry out a program to enhance its capabilities to develop new reactor technologies through high-performance computation modeling and simulation techniques. DOE must consider supportive research activities to maximize the utility of its research facilities.  DOE must also carry out a program to enable the testing and demonstration of reactor concepts to be proposed and funded by the private sector.  DOE must leverage the technical expertise of relevant federal agencies and National Laboratories in order to minimize the time required to enable construction and operation of privately funded experimental reactors at DOE or other Department-owned sites while ensuring reasonable safety for persons working within these sites. DOE must report to Congress on its capabilities to authorize, host, and oversee privately funded fusion and advanced fission experimental reactors.

Oregon Coastal Land Conveyance Act This bill directs the Department of the Interior to complete a survey of the boundary lines to establish the boundaries of the federal land, including any improvements, located on the federal land, appurtenances to the federal land, and minerals on or in the federal land, including oil and gas.  Interior shall: (1) file a map and legal description of the federal land with the congressional defense and appropriations committees, and (2) identify any land owned by the Oregon and California Railroad that is conveyed under this bill.  Interior shall identify public domain land that: (1) is approximately equal in acreage and condition, and (2) is located within the planning area.  Interior shall identify public domain land that: (1) is approximately equal in acreage and condition, and (2) is located within the planning area.  Interior shall reclassify any land reclassified as public domain as land owned by the Oregon and California Railroad.

Department of Environmental Protection Act - Redesignates the Environmental Protection Agency as the Department of Environmental Protection (the head of the Department) and makes the responsibilities of the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Secretary of the department responsible for the functions, powers, and duties of the Administrator and the Administrator's functions, powers, and duties as described above.

Transfers the functions, powers, and duties of the Administrator of EPA to the Department.

Authorizes the Secretary to delegate any functions, powers, or duties, including the promulgation of regulations, to such EPA officers and employees as they may designate.

Deems any reference in any other Federal law, executive order, rule, regulation, reorganization plan, or delegation of authority to the EPA to refer to the Department of Environmental Protection.

Requires all orders, determinations, rules, regulations, permits, grants, contracts, certificates, registrations, and other administrative actions which relate to the functions of the EPA actions to continue in effect until modified, terminated, superseded, set aside, or revoked in accordance with law by the President, the Secretary, or other authorized official.

Declares that this Act shall not affect any proceeding, proposed rule, or

Fighting Medicare Payment Fraud Act of 2009 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to extend from 6 months to 365 calendar days the period during which the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) may require a Medicare claims denial or denial of a claim to be filed with a particular category of providers of services or suppliers if there is a likelihood of fraud, waste, or abuse involving a particular category of providers of services or suppliers.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) engage in heightened scrutiny of claims during such period; and (2) report recommendations to the Secretary and the Inspector General of HHS regarding the application of this Act and any changes to it.

Integrated Public Alert and Warning System Modernization Act of 2008 - Amends the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to direct the President, through the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), to: (1) modernize the integrated public alert and warning system of the United States to ensure that it can alert and warn governmental authorities and the civilian population in areas endangered by disasters; and (2) implement the public alert and warning system.

Requires the Director to: (1) assign to the National Continuity Programs Directorate or its successor responsibility for advising the Director on the modernization and implementation of the public alert and warning system; (2) establish or adopt common alerting and warning protocols, standards, terminology, and operating procedures for the public alert and warning system; (3) include in the public alert and warning system the capability to adapt the distribution and content of communications on the basis of geographic location, risks, or personal user preferences; (4) include in the public alert and warning system the capability to alert and warn individuals with disabilities and individuals with limited English proficiency; and (5) ensure the conduct of training, tests, and exercises for the public alert and warning system.

Requires the public

Medicare Assurance of Rx Transitional Assistance Act of 2004 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide that part D eligible individuals who are full-benefit dual eligible individuals or who are recipients of supplemental security income benefits to be treated as being: (1) subsidy eligible individuals; and (2) medically eligible for Medicare prescription drug benefits.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) enroll such individuals automatically in Medicare drug discount programs; and (2) determine that such individuals are transitional assistance eligible individuals without requiring any self-certification or subjecting such individuals to any verification.

Small Business, Family Farms, and Constitutional Protection Act - Prohibits the use of Federal funds to propose or issue rules, regulations, decrees, or orders or to be used to propose or issue rules, regulations, decrees, or orders to implement the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change before the date on which the Senate gives its advice and consent to ratification of the Kyoto Protocol.

Amends the Defense Production Act of 1950 to reauthorize and extend the Defense Production Review Act (DPRA) through FY2015.

Revises the Committee for the Airborne Recovery and Recovery Operations (CERO) to require the Chairperson of the Committee to be the head of the agency to which the President has delegated primary responsibility for government-wide coordination of the authorities in such Act.

Revises the DPRA's authority to make recommendations for legislation actions to support the effective use of the priorities and allocations authorities.

Revises the criteria for approval of a plan for contingency planning.

Revises the criteria for the review of a plan for the effective use of the priorities and allocations authorities.

The bill also amends Medicare part D (Supplementary Medical Insurance) to provide for Medicare coverage of addiction treatment for opioid-use disorder.

Territorial Economic Growth and Recovery Act of 2016  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the tax on distilled spirit sales. Urban Recovery and Growth Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2010 the recovery zone economic development bonds issued by certain U.S. cities for purposes of extending economic development extension bonds for recovery zones.

National Spaceport Act - Establishes within the Department of Transportation a National Spaceport Office. 
Requires the Office to:  (1) administer the application and assistance program under the National Airports Act; and (2) establish procedures for the competitive awarding of Federal-aid grants and the transfer of excess Federal property to commercial spaceports.

Delphi Pensions Restoration Act of 2012 - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to require revenues of, and proceeds from the sale of troubled assets purchased under such Act, or from the sale, exercise, or surrender of warrants or senior debt instruments acquired under such Act to be paid into the general fund of the Treasury for reduction of the public debt.

Establishes in the Treasury the Delphi Retired Employees Fund to be used by the Secretary of the Treasury in making payments to eligible separated employees who are not covered by any agreement between the General Motors Corporation (General Motors) and the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) that provide for payment of nonforfeitable benefits to such employees.

High School Data Transparency Act of 2011 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to collect, annually, data from each coeducational secondary school receiving federal financial assistance that has an athletics program, to be publicly available for the school year following its receipt of such assistance.

Requires the school to make such information available to students and potential students, upon request, and to the public, on an annual basis.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) ensure that all schools are informed of their right to request such information; and (2) not later than 180 days after enactment of this Act notify schools of their availability for such information and issue guidance to schools on how to collect and report such information.

Recapture Excess Profits and Invest in Roads (REPAIR) Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax on any applicable taxpayer for taxable years beginning in 2008 or 2009 for 25% of the windfall profit of such taxpayer for any taxable year beginning during 2003-2007. Encroachment on Military Bases Prevention Act - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to prohibit the Secretary of the Interior from designating as a critical habitat any lands or other geographical areas owned or controlled by the Department of Defense (DOD) or designated for its use, that are subject to an integrated natural resources management plan prepared under the Sikes Act, if the Secretary determines that such plan addresses special management considerations or protection.

Amends the National Park System General Authorities Act to require the Secretary of the Interior to provide written notice to the Secretary of Defense of the exact military lands to be covered by a study that includes, or the study will be expanded to include, the consideration of any military lands.

Requires the Secretary of Defense, upon receipt of such notification, to: (1) evaluate the existing environmental protections for such lands and the importance of such lands to military readiness and preparedness; and (2) make the determination required by the Secretary of the Interior, and transmit the notice to the Secretary of the Interior, before the end of the 90-day period beginning on the date on which the Secretary receives the written notice of a study that covers military lands.

Statewide PTV Access Act of 2009 - Amends Federal telecommunications law to provide for secondary transmissions of noncommercial educational broadcast stations (NCEs) within a state-wide network of NCEs that are licensed to a single state, political, educational, or special purpose subdivision of a state, or a single public agency.

Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to authorize a state, political, educational, or special purpose subdivision to carry the signals of a television broadcast station outside its local market if the station is a part of a network of three or more NCEs that are licensed to a single state, political, educational, or special purpose subdivision, or a single public agency.

Authorizes a satellite carrier to carry the signals of a network of three or more NCEs that are licensed to a single state, political, educational, or special purpose subdivision, or a single public agency, if the satellite carrier retransmits the secondary signal only to its subscribers located in any county within that state that is located outside that station's local market and not served by another noncommercial educational broadcast station.

Highway Fairness and Reform Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to carry out a direct federal-aid highway program in accordance with the requirements of this Act.

Requires the Secretary to accept an election to have a State waive its right to receive certain Federal-aid highway program payments for FY2011.

Requires the Secretary to accept an election to have a State continue to suballocate funds to urbanized areas and other areas using the formulae and rules under the Federal-aid highway program for urbanized projects and programs funded under this Act.

Requires a State that makes such a election to continue to suballocate funds to urbanized areas and other areas using the formulae and rules under the Federal-aid highway program for urbanized projects and programs funded under this Act to report annually to the Secretary on the use of funds received and on the report available to the public in an easily accessible format.

Declares that nothing in this Act, or in the Higher Education Act of 1965 (HEA), shall be construed to limit or otherwise alter the authorizations of appropriations for title IV programs or the duration of certain title IV programs.

Energy Savings Through Public-Private Partnerships Act of 2014 - Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require federal energy managers to provide an explanation regarding any life-cycle cost-effective measures that have not been implemented in their energy management programs.  Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to authorize federal agencies to enter into contracts with private entities for the modernization or replacement of energy-hungry facilities.  Authorizes federal agencies to sell or transfer energy savings and apply the proceeds of such sale or transfer to fund a contract under the Energy Conservation Program.  Authorizes federal agencies to apply for and receive federal energy conservation contracts.  Authorizes federal agencies to pay the costs of energy savings programs.

Childrens' Internet Protection Act - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to exclude elementary and secondary schools and libraries that fail to provide the certification required by this Act from eligibility for universal service assistance. 
Requires elementary and secondary schools and libraries that have been certified to be effective filters for computers with Internet access to install and use such technology within 30 days of the date of enactment of this Act. 
Provides that a school, library, or other authority responsible for making such a certification shall make such a certification within 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act. 
Directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), within 120 days after this Act's enactment, to adopt rules implementing this Act within 120 days of this Act's enactment.

Provides alternative retirement pay rates for members of the Armed Forces who are veterans with a combat-related disability.

Provides alternative wartime disability compensation rates for veterans with a covered service-connected disability.

Intergovernmental Law Enforcement Information Sharing Act of 2001 - Directs the Attorney General to: (1) expeditiously carry out security clearance investigations for the persons identified in this Act; and (2) grant appropriate security clearances to all such persons who qualify for clearances under applicable laws and executive orders.Requires the Attorney General to ensure that information systems are configured to allow efficient and effective sharing of information among appropriate Federal, State, territorial, and local officials and agencies.

Mobile Workforce State Income Tax Fairness and Simplification Act - Prohibits the wages or other remuneration earned by an employee who performs employment duties in more than one state from being subject to income tax in any state other than: (1) the state of the employee's residence; and (2) the state within which the employee is present and performing employment duties for more than 30 days during the calendar year.

Allows an employer to rely on an employee's determination of the time an employee will spend in the states in which he or she will perform such duties absent actual knowledge of fraud by the employee or collusion between the employer and the employee to evade tax.

Allows an employer to maintain a time and attendance system which tracks where an employee performs duties on a daily basis.

Provides that an employer may rely on an employee's determination of the time an employee will spend in the states in which he or she will perform such duties absent actual knowledge of fraud by the employee or collusion between the employer and the employee to evade tax.

SIG TARP Small Business Awareness Act of 2009 - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 (EESA) to require the Special Inspector General (SIG) of the Office of the Secretary of the Treasury to examine the effects of the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) on small financial institutions and small businesses.

Requires the SIG to report quarterly on the activities of the Secretary and any financial institutions receiving financial assistance to include and utilize minorities (as defined by the Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery, and Enforcement Act of 1989) and women, and minority- and women-owned businesses, in any solicitation or contract, including any contract to asset managers, servicers, property managers, and other service providers or expert consultants.

King Cove Road Land Exchange Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the state of Alaska the 131 acres of federal land located within the Refuge in Alaska, which shall be used for the road corridor along which the road is to be constructed.

Requires the federal land to be conveyed to the state for the purposes of: (1) designating a road corridor through the Refuge; and (2) constructing a single-lane gravel road along the road corridor.

Requires the federal land to be conveyed to the state for the purposes of: (1) designating a road corridor through the Refuge; and (2) constructing a single-lane gravel road.

Requires the federal land and non-federal land to be exchanged for the same amount or to be equalized if not equal.

Requires the state to adopt a certain alternative to the alternative 2-Land Exchange and Southern Road Alignment (i.e., the alternative 3-Land Exchange and Southern Road Alignment) in the final environmental impact statement for the construction of the road.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) reduce estate and gift taxes; (2) increase the exclusion from gifts to $10 million; and (3) increase the annual gift tax exclusion to $50,000.
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through June 30, 1999, the duty on certain HIV-related substances.

Veterans Serving Veterans Act of 2018 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the VA Choice and Quality Employment Act to establish a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Recruiter Database to be known as the Departments of Defense and Veterans Affairs Recruiting Database.  The database shall: (1) maintain a searchable database of military occupational specialties of current and former veterans, (2) include information about each qualified member of the Armed Forces, and (3) include information about the date on which a member is expected to be discharged and released from active duty.  The VA shall: (1) hire qualified members of the Armed Forces who apply for positions listed in the database without regard to the provisions of the veterans' benefits program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and (2) implement a program to train and certify veterans to work as intermediate care technicians in the VA.  The VA shall also establish a center at VA medical facilities to carry out the intermediate care technician training program. No additional funds are authorized to carry out this bill.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the exclusion from gross income for gain from certain small business stock held by a corporation; (2) allow an increased exclusion for incentive stock options; and (3) increase the holding period from five to three years.

Highway Infrastructure Privatization Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt certain qualified highway infrastructure projects from the excise tax on bonds issued to finance certain pilot projects for the construction or reconstruction of highways and the improvement of public transportation.

National Telecommuting and Air Quality Act - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to a nonprofit private entity that is knowledgeable on matters relating to air quality for the purpose of developing a design for the proposed pilot program.  Requires the Secretary to carry out this Act in collaboration with the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency and the Secretary of Energy. 
Requires the Secretary to ensure that the proposed pilot program includes recommendations for:  (1) evaluating and developing for calculating reductions in emissions of ozone precursors that can be achieved as a result of reduced VMTs by telecommuting employees of participating employers; (2) estimating such reductions for the periods of time involved; (3) issuing emission credits to such employers; (4) establishing a commercial trading and exchange forum for trading and exchanging emission credits; (5) obtaining emission credits through such forum; (6) facilitating the transfer of emission credits between participating employers and regulated entities; and (7) conducting a study and report to Congress and the Secretary on the potential significance of the pilot program as an incentive for expanding telecommuting and reducing VMTs in the geographic areas for which the pilot program is developed. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Cyber Preparedness Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to include within the definition of "cybersecurity information" information that is "attributed" to a person or entity that is an entity that has been or is acting as a person that is acting to protect the public interest or the public health or safety of the United States. (Sec. 3) The bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to include within the definition of "cybersecurity risk" that is "attributed" to a person or entity that is an entity that has been or is acting as a person that is acting to protect the public interest or the public health or safety of the United States. (Sec. 4) The bill expresses the sense of Congress that to facilitate the dissemination of homeland security information related to cyber threats, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) should work to share actionable information related to cyber threats in an unclassified form.

Veterans' Access to Child Care Act (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide child care assistance to a veteran for any period that the veteran: (1) receives covered health care services at a VA facility; and (2) is required to return to and stay at the VA facility for the receipt of such care.  (Sec. 3) The VA shall provide child care assistance to a veteran who: (1) is the primary caretaker of a child or children; and (2) is receiving covered health care services from the VA or in need of such care services, but for lack of child care services, would receive such care from the VA.  (Sec. 4) The VA shall extend through FY2026: (1) the authorization of appropriations for the VA's mental health care and other intensive health care services program; and (2) the requirement that a veteran return to and stay at the VA facility for the receipt of such care.

Federal Agency Anti-Lobbying Act - Prohibits the use of appropriated funds by any federal agency for any activity (including the preparation, publication, distribution, or use of any kit, pamphlet, pamphlet, public presentation, news release, radio, television, or film presentation, video, or other written or oral statement) that is intended to promote public support or opposition to any legislative proposal (including the confirmation of a public official or the ratification of a treaty) on which congressional action is not complete.

Defines "federal agency" to include executive agencies, private corporations created by the Congress for which appropriations are made, and any private corporation created by a law of the United States for which the Congress appropriates funds.

Public Good IRA Rollover Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income distributions from individual retirement accounts (IRAs) made directly by the trustee of a qualified charity to a qualified charity (as defined by this Act) that is maintained on or after age 70 1/2 and that has attained age 59 1/2.

Solar Stimulus for Job Creation and Energy Independence Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a refundable energy investment tax credit for the purchase of certain solar energy equipment.

Amends the Energy Policy Act of 2005 to authorize the Department of Energy (DOE) to contract for the production of solar energy.

Workforce Training Enhancement Act of 2016 This bill amends the Trade Act of 1974 to authorize a state to use funds provided under the Trade Adjustment Assistance Program (TAA) to reimburse the costs of providing training to a worker before he or she is approved for training under the TAA.  The conditions for reimbursement are met if the worker is covered by a state certification for eligibility under the TAA, and the costs of which are being reimbursed: (1) commenced after the date on which the total or partial separations of the group of workers covered by the certification for eligibility began or threatened to begin, and (2) meets the requirements for approval of training.

Right of Passage Community Service Act - Amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to establish a national service after-school and summer program for students to serve in their communities after school and during the summer after school and summer program. Includes among the program's eligibility requirements: (1) the opportunity to perform service in their communities; (2) the opportunity to participate in activities that would provide training in leadership development, public speaking, conflict resolution, team-building, and other critical skills; (3) service-learning curricula linked to academic goals; and (4) the opportunity to work with older AmeriCorps members who can organize service projects and act as mentors.

Requires such program to be carried out with assistance provided under the National and Community Service Act of 1990.

Requires such program participants to agree to participate in the program for at least 160 hours during a period of at least two months and not more than one year.

Requires such program participants to receive an education award of $500 for such participation.

Health Care Liability Reform Act - Allows punitive damages to be awarded against a manufacturer or product seller of a product involved in a civil action if the claimant establishes by clear and convincing evidence that the harm suffered was the result of conduct which was not the result of actual malice, unless: (1) the manufacturer withholds from the Food and Drug Administration or from a patient, information relevant to the performance of the product and causally related to the harm suffered by the plaintiff, is withheld; or (2) the product seller withholds from the Food and Drug Administration or from a patient, information relevant to the performance of the product and causally related to the harm suffered by the plaintiff, is withheld.

Requires the amount of punitive damages that may be awarded for a claim in any civil action to be: (1) three times the amount awarded to the claimant for the economic injury on which such claim is based; or (2) $250,000, whichever is greater.

Prohibits joint ownership of the product by the manufacturer or product seller involved in such action.

Securing Protections for the Injured from Limitations on Liability Act - Amends the Death on the High Seas Act to revise provisions concerning the recovery of damages for a seamen's death, including provisions regarding the recovery for loss of care, comfort, and companionship.

Repeals the limitation on the liability of the U.S. Secretary of the Treasury for debts incurred by the U.S. government arising out of the oil pollution and environmental damage caused by the sinking of ships.

Amends the Oil Pollution Act of 1990 to prohibit the Secretary from selling or leasing significant property of the estate of a debtor who is liable under any law for a claim for wrongful death, personal injury, or property damage arising from an incident (as defined by such Act) that gives rise to liability under such Act.

Prohibits the Secretary from selling or leasing, other than in the ordinary course of business, significant property of the estate (or, to the extent that the court has or can obtain jurisdiction over any affiliate of the debtor, significant property of such affiliate) unless creditors holding at least two-thirds in amount and more than one-half in number in such claims consent to such sale or lease.

Unemployment Assistance Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income any qualified unemployment distribution from the gross income of individuals who are unemployed for two years or less.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax on the importation of petroleum products.  Defines "petroleum product" to include: (1) crude oil, and (2) refined petroleum products. 
Imposes an excise tax on the first sale within the United States of such petroleum products. 
Provides for the tax deduction for such products for foreign countries.

Psychological Kevlar Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement a plan to incorporate evidence-based preventive and early-intervention measures, practices, or procedures that reduce the likelihood that personnel in combat will develop post-traumatic stress disorder or other stress-related psychopathologies (including substance use conditions) into: (1) basic and pre-deployment training for enlisted members, noncommissioned officers, and officers; (2) combat theater operations; and (3) post-deployment service.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) conduct and fund the necessary research; (2) develop and implement a training program to educate and promote understanding and awareness about the signs and risks of combat stress; (3) educate commissioned and non-compositional officers and their families to recognize signs of combat stress; (4) establish a new Peer-Reviewed Research program within the Defense Health Program's research and development function to conduct and develop evidence-based preventive measures, practices, or procedures that reduce the likelihood that personnel in combat will develop post-traumatic stress disorder or other stress-related psychopathologies; and (5) submit a report to Congress on the status of research and the expected implementation timeline.

Amends the Agricultural Act of 1949 to permit the grazing of reduced acreage, acreage devoted to a conservation use, and acreage diverted from production under a land diversion program (land diversion) to wheat and other grains.  Prohibits the Secretary of Agriculture from excluding irrigated or irrigable acreage not planted to alfalfa when exercising the authority of the Secretary under this Act.

Artists' Contribution to American Heritage Act of 1999 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that the fair market value of donated literary, musical, artistic, or scholarly compositions, or the copyright thereon (or both), but only if:  (1) such property was created by the taxpayer's personal efforts no less than 18 months before such contribution; (2) the taxpayer has received a qualified appraisal of its fair market value; (3) the donee is a taxpayer organization; (4) the use of the property by the donee is related to the taxpayer's exemption from excise tax on the sale of personal property for tax purposes; and (5) the written appraisal includes evidence of the extent to which the property was owned, maintained, and sold by the taxpayer and the donee. 
Sets forth a maximum dollar limitation for such charitable contributions.

Superfund Research, Development, and Demonstration Act of 1999 - Amends the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA) to authorize the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to enter into agreements with persons, public entities, and nonprofit private entities to use other sites appropriate for carrying out hazardous substances research, testing, evaluation, development, and demonstration projects.

African Free Trade Initiative Act - Amends the African Growth and Opportunity Act to direct the President to develop a plan for negotiating and entering into one or more free trade agreements with all sub-Saharan African countries.

Requires the plan to identify the 15 countries or groups of countries that are most ready for such a free trade agreement.

Requires the plan to include for each such country the following: (1) the steps such country needs to be equipped and ready to enter into such a free trade agreement, including the development of a bilateral investment treaty; (2) milestones for accomplishing each such step; (3) a description of the resources required to assist each country in accomplishing each milestone; and (4) the extent to which such steps may be accomplished through regional or subregional organizations in sub-Saharan Africa, including the East African Community, the Economic Community of West African States, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa, and the Economic Community of Central African States.

Requires the President to report to Congress on the plan.

Diamond-Blackfan Anemia Research and Care Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to expand and intensify research activities regarding Diamond-Blackfan anemia, which is a rare genetic bone marrow failure disorder.

Requires the Director to make grants to, or enter into contracts with, public or private entities to support a comprehensive research initiative to study, develop better treatments for, and ultimately find a cure for Diamond-Blackfan anemia.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to maintain and expand the Diamond-Blackfan Anemia Registry.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Director of the CDC, to establish a comprehensive clinical care center for Diamond-Blackfan anemia where a majority of the patients with the disease are examined, treated, and tracked through the Registry, by experts in the disease.

Prohibits interment in any National Cemetery System cemetery of a person convicted of a capital offense (i.e., murder) or of a person who has committed a heinous act (i.e., a war criminal) that results in death or serious bodily injury.

Denies burial in any military cemetery or funeral honor for a person convicted of a capital offense or of a person who has committed a heinous act that results in death or serious bodily injury.

Requires the Secretary of the Army to remove the remains of Russell Wayne Wagner from Arlington National Cemetery.

Requires the Secretary to arrange for the internment or inurnment of the remains in a public or private cemetery or, if requested, relinquish the remains to the next-of-kin of record.

Economic Fairness for Seniors Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, the American Recovery and Reinvestment Tax Act of 2009, and the Consumer Price Index (CPI)-Elderly Survey to revise requirements for the premium for 2010 for Medicare part B (Supplementary Medical Insurance) for individuals 65 and over.

Amends the American Recovery and Reinvestment Tax Act of 2009 to extend through 2010 the requirement that the Secretary of the Treasury disburse annually specified actuarial rates for the 15-year period beginning with the enactment of this Act.
