Colombian Temporary Protected Status Act of 2002 - Expresses the sense of Congress that, in view of the recent escalation of the current civil war in Colombia, Colombia qualifies for designation under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) as if it had been designated pursuant to which Colombian nationals would be eligible for temporary protected status (TPS) in the United States.

Provides that for a one-year period, TPS shall apply to Tists who: (1) have been continuously physically present since the date of enactment of this Act; (2) are admissible as immigrants and are not ineligible for TPS; and (3) register for TPS in a manner that the Attorney General shall establish.

Directs the Attorney General to give prior consent to travel abroad to an alien granted TPS pursuant to this Act, if the alien establishes to the satisfaction of the Attorney General that emergency and extenuating circumstances beyond the control of the alien require the alien to depart for a brief, temporary trip abroad.

Authorizes the Secretary of Defense to prescribe the following schools for the provision by the National Guard of training in drug interdiction and counter-drug activities:  (1) the NICI (Northwestern Institute for National Defense) in San Luis Obispo, California; (2) the Multi-Jurisdictional Counterdrug Task Force Training in St. Petersburg, Florida; (3) the Midwest Counterdrug Training Center in Meridian, Mississippi; (4) the Regional Counterdrug Training Academy in D.C.; and (5) the Northeast Regional Counterdrug Training Center in Fort Indiantown Gap, Pennsylvania. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the Carl D. Perkins Vocational and Technical Education Act of 1998 to define "Indian student count" as the total number of Indian students enrolled in each tribally-controlled postsecondary vocational and technical institution. 
Requires the Indian student count to be determined on the basis of the enrollments of Indian students as in effect at the conclusion of the third week of the fall term and the third week of the spring term. 
Provides for the counting of students without secondary school degrees in the determination of the Indian student count. 
Provides for the inclusion of such credits in the calculation of the sum of all credit hours of the student.

Veterans TRICARE Choice Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a TRICARE-eligible individual to elect at any time during a special enrollment period (usually 12 months) to be ineligible to enroll in the TRICARE program. Allows such individual to later elect to enroll in the program.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to ensure that a TRICARE-eligible individual who makes such a election may efficiently enroll in the program.

Requires the Secretary to submit to the Commissioner of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) the name of, and any other information that the IRS may require with respect to each TRICARE-eligible individual who makes such a election, not later than 90 days after such election.

American Worker Mobility Act of 2014 - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to grant a relocation subsidy to an eligible individual who is unemployed and has exhausted all rights to regular compensation under state or federal law with respect to a benefit year (excluding any benefit year ending before July 1, 2008).  Defines "eligible individual" as an individual who is unemployed and has exhausted all rights to regular compensation under state or federal law and has not received a relocation subsidy in the two-year period preceding such date of application.  Directs the Secretary to issue regulations to prevent fraud or abuse relating to the program.

Native American Commercial Driving Training and Technical Assistance Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to provide grants, on a competitive basis, to certain tribal colleges or universities to support programs providing training and certificates leading to the licensing of Native Americans with respect to commercial vehicle driving.

Gives priority to grant applications that: (1) propose training that exceeds minimum standards for training tractor-trailer drivers of the Department of Transportation (DOT); (2) propose training that exceeds entry level truck driver certification standards; and (3) propose an education partnership with a private trucking firm, truck driver certification standards, or similar entity in order to ensure the effectiveness of the grant program.

Prescription Drug Labeling Promotion Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a working group to develop and promulgate guidance constituting best practices on access to prescription drug labeling for the visually impaired.

Requires the working group to consider: (1) the use of Braille, auditory means, and large font labels; (2) enhanced visual means, such as large font labels or large font "duplicate" labels that are affixed or matched to a prescription drug container; and (3) factors unique to pharmacies with 20 or fewer retail locations which may fundamentally impact the ability of such pharmacies to implement the best practices.

Directs the Comptroller General to conduct a review of the guidance, the extent to which pharmacies are complying with such best practices, and the extent to which barriers to accessible prescription drug labeling for blind and visually-impaired individuals continue.

Religious Liberty and Charitable Donation Protection Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to prohibit a transfer of a charitable contribution to a qualified religious or charitable entity or organization from exceeding 15 percent of the gross annual income of the debtor for the year in which the contribution is made.

Brownfields Housing and Community Renewal Development Act - Amends the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to establish a program to make grants to assist in carrying out redevelopment activities for brownfield (i.e., unutilized industrial, commercial, or housing structure) sites and abandoned, idled, and underutilized industrial, commercial, or housing structures located in brownfield sites.

Taiwan Airpower Modernization Act of 2011 - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) a critical element to maintaining peace and stability in Asia in the face of China's two-decade-long program of military modernization and expansion of military capabilities is ensuring a militarily strong and confident Taiwan; (2) Taiwan that is confident in its ability to deter Chinese aggression will increase its ability to proceed in developing peaceful relations with China in areas of mutual interest; (3) the cross-Strait military balance between China and Taiwan has clearly shifted in China's favor; (4) China's military expansion poses a clear and present danger to Taiwan, and this threat has very serious implications for U.S. foreign and national interests in East Asia; (5) the United States has a statutory obligation under the Taiwan Relations Act to provide Taiwan with additional advanced multirole fighter aircraft; (6) the proposed sale of F-16C/D multirole fighter aircraft to Taiwan would have significant economic benefits to the United States economy; and (7) the United States must provide Taiwan with such aircraft, as well as significant upgrades to Taiwan's existing fleet of multirole fighter aircraft.

Purchase Card Waste Elimination Act of 2006 - Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to issue guidelines to assist the heads of executive agencies in improving the management of the use of the Governmentwide commercial purchase card for making micropurchases.

Requires the Administrator of General Services to: (1) continue efforts to improve reporting by financial institutions that issue the Governmentwide commercial purchase card so that the General Services Administration (GSA) has the data needed to identify opportunities for achieving savings; and (2) pursue point-of-sale discounts with major vendors accepting the purchase card so that any federal purchaser using the purchase card can benefit from such point-of-sale discounts.

Alisa's Law of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to withhold 1% of the amount authorized to be apportioned to a state for each of specified fiscal years if the state has not enacted and is not enforcing a law requiring the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence.

Foreign Investment Transparency and Security Act of 2006 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to authorize foreign governments to acquire, own, or manage U.S. critical infrastructure (i.e., any entity in which a foreign government owns a majority interest, or otherwise controls or manages the entity) only through the establishment or operation of a foreign-owned general business corporation.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to promulgate regulations to implement this Act.

Makes a foreign government-controlled entity that owns or controls or manages any U.S. critical infrastructure on effective date of this Act 180 days or less.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on the implementation of a scanning system for 100% of the inbound maritime containers.

Bond Financing Renewal Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase from $10 to $20 million the maximum amount of qualified small issue bonds authorized for certain principal-related businesses.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the cost-of-living adjustment to such increased amounts; (2) require the cost-of-living adjustment to such increased amounts to be based upon the cost of the facility for which the bond is issued; and (3) require the cost-of-living adjustment to such increased amounts to be based upon the net proceeds of the issue of such bonds.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) allow the acquisition of interest-expensing obligations of financial institutions for small issue bonds; and (2) allow the acquisition of interest-expensing obligations of non-financial institutions for such bonds.

Freedom and Human Rights for the Enclaved People of Cyprus Act - Directs the President to: (1) inform the United Nations (U.N.), foreign governments, and appropriate U.S. agencies of the restrictions on the freedom and human rights of the enclaved people of Cyprus; (2) enlist U.N. and foreign government assistance to end such restrictions; and (3) establish U.S. government programs of assistance to the enclaved.

Directs the President to use funds allocated to the government or ethnic community participating directly or indirectly in the imposition of such restrictions to assist such people or to undertake efforts for the alleviation and elimination of such restrictions.

Requires the President to: (1) use such funds to eliminate specific aspects of such restrictions; and (2) establish a foreign assistance program for the enclaved.

(U.N.); and (2) urge the head of such government to cease such participation and to work to eliminate such restrictions.

Meat Promotion Act of 2005 - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a voluntary program of country of origin labeling for covered meat products.

Prohibits a person from: (1) designating a covered meat product as having the United States as the country of origin unless the covered meat product is derived exclusively from an animal born and raised in the United States; or (2) having a meat product from an animal born and raised in Alaska or Hawaii slaughtered in the United States.

Prohibits the Secretary from making or guaranteeing a loan to a borrower who: (1) was restructured with a write-down under the Act; or (2) is current on payments under a confirmed reorganization plan. PTSD/TBI Guaranteed Review For Heroes Act - Directs the Secretary of Defense to establish within the Office of the Secretary of Defense a special review board to review the discharge or dismissal of a former member of the Armed Forces who: (1) was deployed in support of a contingency operation; (2) was discharged or dismissed from the Armed Forces under a general or other than honorable condition; and (3) has been diagnosed by a health care professional with post-traumatic stress disorder or traumatic brain injury.

Authorizes the Secretary to refer such a member for evaluation by a physical evaluation board if the board determines that the member is unfit to perform the duties of the member's office.

Amends the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act of 1996 to prohibit a person from holding a gun show unless:  (1) the person is licensed to do so; and (2) at least 30 days have elapsed since the person, using a form prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury, has notified the Secretary and the chief law enforcement officer of the post-alabama gun show and the dates and times at which the gun show is to be held. 
Requires a licensed person to submit to the Secretary an application which contains a certification by the applicant that:  (1) the applicant meets certain requirements; and (2) any gun show to be conducted under the license is not prohibited by State or local law, and will be conducted in accordance with State and local law. 
Requires the Secretary to:  (1) approve an application submitted within 60 days of its receipt; and (2) issue to the applicant a license which entitles the licensee to hold gun shows in interstate or foreign commerce during the three-year period beginning with the date the license is issued.

Obamacare Marriage Penalty Elimination Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code, with respect to the tax credit for health insurance coverage, to: (1) eliminate the tax penalty for married individuals filing a joint tax return, (2) reduce the amount of such penalty for taxpayers with incomes over $250000, and (3) allocate such credit to dependents of the taxpayer based on their family size.

Canyon Mountain Land Conveyance Act of 2013 - Transfers approximately 17,826 acres of federal land in the Coos Bay District, Eugene District, Medford District, Salem District, and Klamath Falls Resource Area of the Lakeview District (the federal lands) to the Coos Bay Band of the Umpqua Tribe of Indians for use as a tribal lands reserve.  Requires the Secretary of the Interior to complete a survey of the boundary lines to establish the boundaries of the federal lands taken into trust.  Requires the Secretary to file a map and legal description of such federal lands with the congressional agriculture and natural resources committees.  Prohibits the sale or other disposition of any federal land or interest in land until the Secretary has identified: (1) any Oregon and California Railroad land conveyed under this Act, and (2) public domain land that is approximately equal in acreage and condition to the land identified.  Directs the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of the Interior to identify any land owned by the Oregon and California Railroad.  Requires the Secretary to reclassify any such land as federal lands owned by the Oregon and California Railroad.

Election Jamming Prevention Act of 2006 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit the use of the following communications to annoy, abuse, threaten, or harass any person at the called number or who receives the communications: (1) the intent to annoy, abuse, threaten, or harass any person at the called number or who receives the communications; (2) the prevention or obstruction of the broadcast or exchange of election-related information; or (3) the impair or obstruct of any other telecommunications device from being used to engage in communications containing election-related information.

Allows private actions for injunctive or declarative relief in any court of competent jurisdiction, including in U.S. district court.

Healthy Maternity and Obstetric Medicine Act or the Healthy MOM Act This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to provide for a special enrollment period for pregnant women, beginning on the date on which the pregnancy is reported to the health insurance company. The bill amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require a group health plan to permit an employee who is eligible, but not enrolled, for coverage under the terms of the plan (or a dependent of such an employee if the dependent is eligible, but not enrolled, for such coverage under such terms) to enroll for coverage under the terms of the plan upon pregnancy, with the special enrollment period beginning on the date on which the pregnancy is reported to the group health plan.
Continuity of Congress Act of 2003 - Authorizes the legislature of each State to fill a vacancy in the House of Representatives or the Senate.

Earmark Reform and Federal Spending Transparency and Accountability Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit any earmark beneficiary from making more than $5,000 a candidate for such earmark during the period beginning on January 1 of an odd-numbered year and ending on December 31 of the next even-numbered year.

Defines "earmark beneficiary" as any person who specifically requests and benefits from a congressionally directed spending item, a limited tax benefit, or a limited tariff benefit (as so defined) which was enacted into law during the period beginning on January 1 of an odd-numbered year and ending on December 31 of the next even-numbered year.

Supporting Emergency Responders Volunteer Efforts Act of 2009 or the SERVE Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a bona fide volunteer member of a qualified volunteer emergency response organization a tax credit for $1,000 of the cost of providing such services. Defines "bona fide volunteer member of a qualified volunteer emergency response organization" as an individual who has served as a volunteer performing qualified services for more than six months in a taxable year and provided more than 40 hours of such service.

Fuel-Efficient Fleets Act of 2006 - Amends Federal transportation law to require federal passenger automobiles purchased, or leased for at least 60 consecutive days, by executive agencies following enactment of this Act to achieve a minimum fuel economy of at least 15 miles per gallon for vans, 20 miles per gallon for minivans, 36 miles per gallon for pickup trucks, and 45 miles per gallon for passenger automobiles.

Requires at least 25% of such automobiles to achieve the minimum fuel economy for vans and minivans, 50% for pickup trucks, and 75% for passenger automobiles.

Requires at least 100% of such automobiles to achieve the minimum fuel economy for sport utility vehicles, minivans, and passenger automobiles.

Requires the Secretary of Energy to annually evaluate the fuel economy standards under this Act, and increase such standards if significant technological improvements make it feasible to achieve higher fuel economy.

Taxation of Minor Children Simplification Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose a tax on the net unearned income of minor children (children under age 21) who are taxpayers for purposes of determining the tax of the taxpayer's income for purposes of determining the gross income of the taxpayer.

Expands the parental election to allow a child to claim income of the parent who is not entitled to certain benefits for the child's tax deduction.

Strengthening Child Welfare Response to Trafficking Act of 2014 - Amends the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to report to Congress on the specific type and prevalence of severe form of trafficking in persons to which children who are identified for services or intervention under the child welfare (CWA) programs have been subjected as of the date of enactment of this Act. Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on the practices and protocols utilized by states to identify and serve: (1) children who are victims of trafficking; and (2) children who are at risk of becoming victims of trafficking. Requires the Secretary to specify any barriers in federal laws or regulations that may prevent identification and assessment of such children.

Health Care COBRA OffSet Tax Savings Act of 2005 or the Health Care COSTS Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual taxpayer who receives COBRA continuation coverage under a group health plan a refundable credit equal to 50 percent of the amount of the premium which would be required to be paid by such individual during the taxable year for COBRA continuation coverage.

Requires the Secretary of Labor to prescribe regulations permitting such an individual to assign such credit to the administrator of the plan under which COBRA continuation coverage is being provided.

Enhanced Emergency and Enforcement Authority Act This bill amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Company Act of 1940, and the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 to expand the authority of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to conduct and enforce securities laws in U.S. district court.  The bill also expands the authority of the SEC to conduct and enforce securities laws in foreign courts.
Safe Medications for the Elderly Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of certain pharmaceutical care services furnished by a pharmacist.

Elgin Stafford Mental Illness Information Disclosure Act of 2012 or Elgin's Law - Requires a health care professional, in the case of a minor child, an uninsured adult, or an adult under age 26 who is being treated for mental illness, to disclose to a parent any information regarding the mental illness and treatment for mental illness as may be useful for the appropriate involvement of the parent with respect to the treatment.

Exempts such a professional from such requirement in exceptional circumstances as the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) may provide where the involvement of the parent would be counter-productive to the treatment involved.

Requires the Secretary to post information on the requirements of this Act on Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) websites.

Energy Savings Through Public-Private Partnerships Act of 2013 - Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require an energy manager of an agency to consider: (1) implementing any energy-saving or conservation measure that the agency identified in an evaluation that was conducted under this Act that is life cycle cost-effective, and (2) bundling individual measures of varying paybacks together into combined projects. Requires the energy manager to provide reasons for not implementing any such measure. Requires the federal agency to consider using energy savings performance contracts or utility energy service contracts to implement energy-saving or conservation measures. Requires the federal agency to submit to the Secretary information regarding progress made by the agency towards achieving the goal of entering into energy savings performance contracts or utility energy service contracts equal to $1 billion in each year during the five-year period beginning on January 1, 2014.

Drunk Driving Repeat Offender Prevention Act of 2015 This bill requires a state to enact and enforce a law that requires the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence. A state may not use the device if it requires a breath sample prior to starting the vehicle.

Small Business Expansion and Job Creation Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2010: (1) increased limitations on the expensing of depreciable business assets, and (2) an extension of the special allowance for depreciable business property.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2010: (1) the increased expensing allowance for depreciable business assets, and (2) the special allowance for depreciable business property for which the expensing allowance is extended.

Great Lakes Navigation System Sustainability Act of 2013 - Directs the Secretary of the Army, acting through the Chief of Engineers, to manage and allocate funding for all of the federally authorized commercial and recreational navigation projects in the Great Lakes Navigation System as components of a single, comprehensive system recognizing the interdependence of the projects. Sweetgrass Hills Protection Act of 1995 - Establishes the Sweetgrass Hills Natural Area within the Bureau of Land Management's Sweetgrass Hills Area of Critical Environmental Concern. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to make minor revisions in the boundary of the natural area to promote management effectiveness and efficiency in the furtherance of this Act. 
Directs the Secretary to acquire lands or interests within the boundaries of the natural area necessary to carry out the purposes of this Act by donation, purchase with donation or appropriated funds, or exchange. 
Prohibits the Secretary from issuing any lease under the Federal Mining Laws or the Materials Act of 1947 for lands within the natural area. 
Prohibits disposal of mineral materials under the Act of July 31, 1947, for any location or claim made in the natural area. 
Prohibits mining or mining related activities within the natural area. 
Prohibits the use of any surface disturbance of lands or waters within such area, including through subsistence, in connection with any mining or mining related activities. 
Directs the Secretary to examine all unpatented mining claims within the natural area.

Hiring Heroes Tax Incentive Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers a business-related tax credit of 15% of the wages of employees who are either: (1) a Ready Reserve-National Guard employee, or (2) a recently-separated veteran. Defines "Ready Reserve-National Guard employee" as an employee who is a member of the Ready Reserve or the National Guard and who is: (1) a veteran; and (2) a member of the Ready Reserve or the National Guard.

Prohibits the President from providing economic, military, or arms transfers to the Government of Sudan unless the President certifies to Congress that such Government has taken appropriate action to eliminate chattel slavery in Sudan, including: (1) the enactment of anti-slavery laws that provide appropriate punishment for violators of such laws; and (2) the rigorous enforcement of such laws.

Prohibits the President from providing economic assistance, military assistance or arms transfers to the government of any foreign country that participates, or is otherwise involved, in the establishment or conduct of slavery originating from Sudan, directly or indirectly.

Directs the President to instruct the U.S. representative to pursue the passage of any resolution by the United Nations Security Council that enhances the cooperation of other countries in the application of the spirit and intent of sanctions against Sudan and in any other Act.

Under the system, established providers must demonstrate that at least 90% of claims for payment for items and services furnished by such providers or suppliers for which a review was conducted are eligible for payment or partial payment.  A provider is eligible to qualify as an established provider for a period with respect to a reporting period (as specified by the CMS) for which an electronic system for the submission of claims by established providers is established. Clean Up Earmarks Act of 2010 or the CUE Act of 2010 - Directs the Comptroller General to submit an audit of 5% of Senate earmarks for the current fiscal year chosen at random.

Arapaho-Roosevelt National Forests Land Exchange Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to exchange certain land owned by Grand Creek, LLC, in Clear Creeks County, Colorado, for certain land owned by Grand Creek, LLC, in the Arapaho-Roosevelt National Forests in Colorado.

Requires the Secretary to adjust the boundary of the National Forests to reflect the land exchange.

Guaranteed Health Coverage for Pre-Existing Conditions Act of 2014 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit a group health plan or health insurance issuer offering group health insurance coverage from imposing any preexisting condition exclusion with respect to such plan or coverage. Defines "preexisting condition exclusion" as a limitation or exclusion of benefits relating to a condition based on the fact that it was present before the date of enrollment in the plan or for coverage, whether or not any medical advice, diagnosis, care, or treatment was recommended or received before such date. Makes such provisions applicable to coverage offered to individuals by a health insurance issuer in the individual market. Requires each health insurance issuer offering health insurance coverage in the group market to accept every individual in a group that applies for such coverage. Allows an issuer to restrict enrollment in coverage to open or special enrollment periods. Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to treat any reference of the word "employer" in such provisions as a reference to the term "individual."

Workplace Integrity Act This bill prohibits federal employees from being granted official time in connection with any matter covered by federal law.  Official time may be granted to: (1) an employee representing an exclusive representative, but only for a purpose allowable under this bill; or (2) an employee in a unit represented by an exclusive representative, but only for a purpose allowable under this bill.  Official time may not be granted to any employee, except to: (1) allow such employee to present a grievance on behalf of an employee in a unit represented by the exclusive representative, or (2) be present during a grievance proceeding involving an employee in a unit represented by the exclusive representative.  Official time may not be granted to any employee, except to allow such employee to present a grievance on the employee's own behalf under a negotiated grievance procedure, or to attend an impasse proceeding, or to solicit membership, elections of labor organization officials, and collection of dues.  The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) shall report to Congress on the use of official time.

Responsible Debt Relief and Democracy Reform Act - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to authorize the President to cancel or reduce amounts owed to the United States by foreign countries as a result of concessional or nonconcessional loans only if certain additional requirements are met, including that the requirements are satisfied.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the President should instruct the U.S. Executive Director at each international financial institution to which the United States is a member to use the U.S. vote to urge that the cancellation or reduction of debt owed to such institution may be provided only if the country meets certain requirements.

21st Century Federal Pell Grant Plus Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to provide that, in the case of a student who is eligible under the Act and who is pursuing a degree with a major in, or a certificate or program of study relating to, engineering, mathematics, science (such as physics, chemistry, or computer science), or a foreign language, the amount of the Federal Pell Grant shall be the amount calculated for the student under specified circumstances for the academic year involved, multiplied by 2.

Veterans' Employment Transition Support Act of 2005 or the VETS Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a military service personnel employment tax credit for: (1) hiring a veteran who served in a combat zone or a hazardous duty area; and (2) having a disability that has been determined to be service-connected and that is rated as 10% or more disabling. Defines "qualified wages" as wages attributable to service rendered during the one-year period beginning with the day the individual begins work for the employer.

United States Mariner and Vessel Protection Act of 2009 - Authorizes the Commandant of the Coast Guard to deploy a maritime safety and security team to deter, protect against, and respond to acts of piracy against U.S.-flag vessels in international waters.

Directing Dollars to Disaster Relief Act of 2015 (Sec. 3) This bill directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to develop and implement an integrated plan to control and reduce administrative costs for major disasters, which shall include: (1) steps the agency will take to reduce administrative costs; (2) milestones needed for accomplishing such reduction; (3) strategic goals for the average annual percentage of administrative costs of major disasters for each fiscal year; (4) the assignment of clear roles and responsibilities, including the designation of officials responsible for monitoring and measuring performance; and (5) a timetable for implementation. (Sec. 4) FEMA must report to Congress on the plan's development and implementation.

Children First Act of 2010 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to exclude child care assistance from the definition of "temporary assistance" for families receiving TANF.

Increases funding for child care.

Subjects child care assistance expenditures for which TANF is provided in the aggregate to the individual and case data reporting requirements of the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990.

Personal Exemption Fairness Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for a multiplicative adjustment to the dollar amounts of individual income tax exemptions for individuals residing in a metropolitan statistical area that is not within a metropolitan statistical area.

Amends the Defense Base Closure and Realignment Act of 1990 to extend through FY 2007 the closure of Department of Defense (DOD) and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) military installations in Iraq and Afghanistan.

Amends the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2002 to extend through FY 2007 the closure of DOD and DHS military installations in Iraq and Afghanistan.

Directs the President to submit to Congress a two-year progress report on the closure of military installations in Iraq and Afghanistan.

Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection Advisory Board Enhancement Act - Amends the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 to direct the Director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) to establish a Small Business Advisory Board to: (1) advise and consult with the CFPB in the exercise of its functions under federal consumer financial laws, and (2) provide information on emerging practices of small business concerns that provide eligible financial products or services, including regional trends, the effect that decisions by the CFPB have on rural areas, concerns, and other relevant information.

Declaration of Official Language Act of 1997 - Makes English the official language of the U.S. Government.  Directs the U.S. Government to promote and support the use of English for communications among U.S. citizens.  Requires that all U.S. citizens be encouraged to read, write, and speak English to the extent of their physical and mental abilities. 
Repeals provisions of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 which require that English be the language of instruction in the schools. 
Repeals provisions of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 which require that bilingual election requirements be inapplicable to:  (1) religious purposes; (2) training in foreign languages for international communication; or (3) use of non-English terms of art in government documents.

Child Immunization Incentive Act of 1993 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to deny TANF benefits to any child who has not attained the age of six years, unless the State agency has received from one or more physicians:  (1) verification that the child has been examined by a physician at least every six months since the child was born; and (2) that the child has been immunized in accordance with recommendations issued by the Surgeon General of the Public Health Service. 
Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act to require that providers of child care services require certificates signed by a physician who verifies that the child has been immunized in accordance with recommendations issued by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. 
Requires the Surgeon General of the Public Health Service to issue, and revise, TANF immunization recommendations from time to time.

Home Energy Savings Incentives Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to revise the tax credit for energy efficiency upgrades. Allows a $10 credit for the cost of 85% (currently, 100%) of a qualified energy efficiency expenditure, and a $0.65 credit for each kilowatt hour of certified electricity savings. Limits the lifetime credit to $5,000.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to prescribe the manner and method for the certification of such expenditures.

Federal Computer Security Act - Requires the Inspector General of each federal agency operating a federal computer system that provides access to classified information or personally identifiable information to report to the Comptroller General and appropriate congressional committees information collected from the agency regarding the use of such information and related information processing services.

Requires the Comptroller General to report to Congress on any impediments to agency use of effective security software and devices.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from the payroll tax on earnings attributable to the hiring of qualified individuals by employers in 2010 any wages paid by such employers after February 3, 2010, and before January 1, 2011, in furtherance of their tax exemptions.

Allows employers to elect to have this exemption not apply.

Amends the Federal Employees' Retirement System (FERS) to exempt from the payroll tax on wages paid by employers in 2010 any amounts paid or incurred to a qualified individual during the one-year period beginning on the hiring date of such individual by a qualified employer (FERS employer) unless such employer makes a election not to have this exemption.

Increases the business tax credit for retained workers with respect to which this Act applies.

Department of Homeland Security Data Framework Act of 2018 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to develop a data framework to integrate existing DHS databases and systems for access by authorized personnel in a manner consistent with relevant legal authorities and privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties policies and protections.  DHS must ensure that the data framework is accessible to DHS employees who:   have an appropriate security clearance, are assigned to perform a function that requires access to information in the framework, and are trained in applicable standards for safeguarding and using such information.   DHS may exclude information from the framework if inclusion of such information may:   jeopardize the protection of sources, methods, or activities;  compromise a criminal or national security investigation;  be inconsistent with other federal laws or regulations; or be duplicative or not serve an operational purpose if included in such framework.   DHS shall incorporate into the framework systems capabilities for auditing and ensuring the security of information included in the framework.  DHS shall notify Congress at least every 60 days on component use of the framework to support operations that disrupt terrorist activities and incidents in the homeland.

Veterans Health Care Budget Reform and Transparency Act of 2009 - Authorizes the two-fiscal year budget authority provided in an appropriations Act for the appropriations accounts of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to include new discretionary budget authority for such accounts that first become available for the first fiscal year after such fiscal year.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on the adequacy and accuracy of the budget projections made by the Enrollee Health Care Projection Model, its equivalent, or other methodologies as utilized for the purpose of estimating and projecting VA health care expenditures with respect to the fiscal year involved and the subsequent four fiscal years.

Native American Housing Enhancement Act of 2005 - Amends the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996 to provide for a program of residential assistance to federally recognized Indian tribes (or their instrumentalities) that exercise powers of self-government.

Provides that federally recognized Indian tribes that exercise powers of self-government shall comply with title II of the Indian Civil Rights Act (the Act) when receiving assistance under the Act.

Provides that title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and title VIII of the Civil Rights Act of 1968 shall not apply to tribes covered by the Act or to tribes acting under such Act.

Amends the Cranston-Gonzales National Affordable Housing Act to provide that an Indian tribe, tribally designated housing entity, or other agency primarily serving Indians shall be eligible for Youthbuild grants under the Act.

Veterans Conservation Corps Authorization Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to establish a veterans conservation corps to: (1) provide training and employment to eligible veterans; (2) assist eligible veterans in the transition from service in the Armed Forces to civilian life; and (3) assist the federal government in maintaining federal land and water.

Authorizes the Secretary to establish a program in the corps for the short-term employment of eligible veterans that is attending institutions of higher education.

Requires each eligible veteran employed under the corps to be assigned to a work project that: (1) furthers such purposes; and (2) falls within one or more of specified categories of such work projects.

Requires the Secretary and the Secretary of Commerce to identify additional project categories that the Secretary and the Secretary of Commerce consider appropriate to further such purposes.

Requires the Secretary and the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, and the Secretary of Commerce to use existing facilities of the federal government to provide the education and training necessary to enable eligible veterans to carry out the work projects assigned to them.

State Health Care Flexibility Act of 2011 - Permits a qualifying state to opt out of the application of any or all of the provisions of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) with respect to health insurance coverage within such state.

Senior$afe Act of 2015 This bill prohibits a state financial regulatory agency, each of the federal financial institutions regulatory agencies, or a law enforcement agency, from providing training to a senior citizen officer or employee of a covered financial institution regarding the identification and reporting of the suspected exploitation of a senior citizen to such officer or employee if the individual: (1) served as a supervisor, compliance officer, or legal advisor for the covered financial institution; and (2) made the disclosure in good faith and with reasonable care. A covered financial institution shall not be liable, including in any civil or administrative proceeding, for a disclosure made by an individual if the individual was employed by the covered financial institution at the time of the disclosure and before the time of the disclosure, the covered financial institution provided the training to each officer or employee of the covered financial institution, and before the time of the disclosure, the covered financial institution provided training to each officer or employee.

Manufacturing Advisory Council Establishment Act of 2004 - Establishes the President's Council of Advisors on Manufacturing to advise the President on policy matters affecting the domestic manufacturing sector.

Fair Trade in Grain Act of 1993 - Amends the Agricultural Trade Act of 1978 to prohibit the importation of foreign grain unless the importer presents an end-use certificate that complies with specified requirements.

Directs the Secretary to initiate a countervailing duty and antidumping duty investigation with respect to the subsidies provided by Canada in connection with the exportation of wheat to the United States.

Master Teacher Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Education to: (1) conduct a demonstration project under which the Secretary shall award competitive grants to local educational agencies (LEAs) to increase teacher salaries and employee benefits for teachers who enter into contracts with such LEAs to serve as master teachers; and (2) report to Congress on the project results and recommendations.

Tax Reduction and Economic Growth Act of 1995 - Authorizes the President to declare temporary tax reductions upon receipt of a Secretary of Labor's declaration that economic growth is less than 1.5 percent and the rate of national unemployment is greater than 6.5 percent. 
Provides that any such reduction or surtax shall not be considered for purposes of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act).

Children's Products Safety Act of 2007 - Amends the Consumer Product Safety Act to require manufacturers of children's products subject to a consumer product safety standard under the Act or a rule declared by a specified Commission declaring a consumer product a banned hazardous product to issue a certificate which certifies that such product conforms to such consumer product safety standard or is not a banned hazardous product and specifies such standard or rule.

Requires any testing program on the basis of which a certificate is issued to be conducted by a nongovernmental independent third-party qualified to perform such tests or testing programs.

Defines "children's product" as a toy or other article intended for use by a child under 60 months of age that is introduced into the interstate stream of commerce.

Directs the Consumer Product Safety Commission to prescribe a rule for children's products which is added by this Act.

Choice in Welfare Tax Credit Act of 1995 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer to elect a credit for up to $100 ($200 for joint returns) of cash contributions to a qualifying charity whose primary activity is assistance to the poor.  Requires such charity to provide copies of annual returns for inspection.

Flat Alternative Individual Return Tax Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual to elect to be subject to the tax imposed by this Act on the alternative tax imposed by the Internal Revenue Service on individuals who are making an election to avoid a tax imposed by the Internal Revenue Service on the alternative tax. 
Declares that it shall not be in order in the House of Representatives or the Senate to consider any bill, joint resolution, amendment, or conference report thereon that includes any provision that increases the FAIR tax rate, creates any additional FAIR income tax rate, or reduces the FAIR standard deduction.  Allows this Act to be waived or suspended in the Senate only by an affirmative vote of three-fifths of the Members, duly chosen and sworn.

National Whale Conservation Fund Act of 1998 - Amends the National Fish and Wildlife Establishment Act to authorize the Foundation for National Whaling Conservation to establish a national whale conservation endowment fund to be used to support research, management, or educational programs that contribute to the protection, conservation, or recovery of whale populations. 
Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to transfer to the Foundation for deposit in the endowment fund any amount (or portion thereof) received by the Secretary under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 as a civil penalty assessed by the Secretary under such Act; or any amount received by the Secretary as a settlement or award for damages in a civil action or other legal proceeding relating to damage of natural resources. 
Requires the Directors of the Board of Trustees of the National Marine Fisheries Service to ensure that any transferred amounts are deposited in the endowment fund in accordance with this Act. 
Requires the Board to give priority to any project that addresses the conservation of populations of whales that the Foundation determines are the most endangered or that are most likely to benefit from research and educational activities that may be funded with amounts made available from the endowment fund.

Justice for Public Safety Officers Act - Amends the Federal criminal code to impose a fine and/or prison term of up to 30 years for the killing of federally funded or Federal law enforcement officers (or attempting or conspiring to kill such officers) or for a manslaughter offense if the officer was at the time of the offense, engaged in carrying out a program authorized by federal law or regulation that is executed in whole or in part by non-federal public safety officers.

Imposes a fine and/or prison term of up to 15 years for the killing of a former federally funded or Federal law enforcement officer (or attempting or conspiring to kill such officer) on account of the past performance of official duties as such.

Imposes a fine and/or prison term of up to 10 years for the flight to avoid prosecution for killing federally funded public safety officers.

Secure Fence Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to take all actions necessary and appropriate to achieve and maintain operational control over the entire international land and maritime borders of the United States, including: (1) systematic surveillance of U.S. land and maritime borders through more effective use of technology and physical infrastructure, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), ground-based sensors, satellites, radar coverage, and cameras; and (2) physical infrastructure enhancements to prevent unlawful entry by aliens into the United States and facilitate entry by Customs and Border Protection (CBP).

Emergency Unemployment Compensation Amendments of 1993 - Amends the Emergency Unemployment Compensation Act of 1991 to extend through October 2, 1993, the emergency unemployment compensation program. 
Terminates such program after June 1993.

Ban Poisonous Additives Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require that a food intended for children three years of age or younger, or for a baby bottle or cup that is three years old, be made of bisphenol A (BPA).

Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to: (1) prohibit the use of BPA in baby food and infant formula containers; and (2) require that a bisphenol A-containing container of baby food or formula be: (1) composed of bisphenol A; and (2) notched (covered by the requirement that a bisphenol A-containing container of baby food or formula come into contact with the infant formula powder).

Family Farmer Bankruptcy Clarification Act of 2017 This bill allows a governmental unit to file a claim for a tax return that arises after the filing of a bankruptcy case concerning the disposition of property used in a farming operation.  A governmental unit may file a proof of claim for such a claim that arises after the filing of the petition.  A claim may be allowed under the same bankruptcy procedures as a claim arising immediately before the filing of a bankruptcy case.

Commit to Opioid Medical Prescriber Accountability and Safety for Seniors Act or the COMPASS Act This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to identify outlier prescribers of opioids in Medicare-eligible individuals enrolled in prescription drug plans (PDPs) or Medicare Advantage (MA) plans based on certain criteria, including that the outlier prescriber has been so identified and that the criteria for identifying an outlier prescriber is the same criteria used to identify other opioid-prescription prescribers. The CMS must use National Provider Identifiers (unique provider identification numbers for Medicare drugs) to identify outlier prescribers. The CMS may exclude certain individuals and prescribers from the analysis.

Desert Community Lands Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the town of: (1) the surface estate of approximately 4,630 acres of land in California, in the form of a Conveyance to Town of Apple Valley, for the purpose of allowing the town to use the conveyed land to provide a suitable location for the establishment of a centralized off-road vehicle recreation park, the public with opportunities for off-road vehicle recreation, and a designated area and facilities that would discourage unauthorized use of off-highway vehicles in areas containing environmentally sensitive land; and (2) the surface estate of the land generally depicted as "Proposed Conveyance to Twentynine Palms" in California, for the purpose of allowing the city of Twentynine Palms, California, to use the conveyed land for the purpose of providing a suitable location for the establishment of a centralized off-road vehicle recreation park, the public with opportunities for off-road vehicle recreation, and a designated area and facilities that would discourage unauthorized use of off-highway vehicles in areas containing environmentally sensitive land.

Alcohol Advertising Accountability Act of 1996 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report annually to the Congress on alcohol advertising, its profile and effects. 
Requires the Secretary to establish a panel made up of individuals in the Department of Health and Human Services or any other Federal agency to review alcohol advertising in all media, including broadcast and cable television, other electronic means, and print and outdoor advertising and review promotional activities undertaken to promote the sale of alcoholic beverages. 
Requires the report of the Secretary to include:  (1) an identification of the media used by alcohol advertising to reach children; (2) the total expenditures for alcoholic beverage advertising in each media and in promotions; (3) the extent to which media program audiences are under the age of 21; (4) an identification of the types and themes of alcohol advertising in all media (especially in broadcast) and other electronic means, any graphics, slogans, children's characters, and techniques that are used and that appeal to youth; (5) a determination of the extent to which young people are exposed to alcohol advertising and promotions of alcoholic beverages; (6) an evaluation of the relationship between alcohol advertising practices and underage drinking, drunk driving, and related public health
Mortgage Cancellation Relief Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer to discharge an individual's indebtedness from gross income, subject to limitations.

Local Zoning Decisions Protection Act of 2017 This bill prohibits the use of federal funds to design, build, maintain, utilize, or provide access to a federal database of geospatial information on community racial disparities or disparities in access to affordable housing.  The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) shall jointly consult with state officials, local government officials, and officials of public housing agencies to develop recommendations to further the purposes and policies of the Fair Housing Act. HUD shall publish a draft report describing the recommendations.  The bill requires the report to identify that consensus was not reached and describe: (1) the areas and issues with regard to which consensus was reached, (2) the areas and issues of continuing disagreement that resulted in the failure to reach consensus, and (3) the reasons for the continuing disagreements. HUD may include a recommendation in the draft report only if consensus has been reached. HUD shall make the draft report available for public review and comment for a period of not fewer than 180 days. HUD shall prepare a final report describing the results of the consultation process.

Honorable Stephanie Tubbs Jones College Fire Prevention Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to establish a demonstration program to award grants for installing fire sprinkler systems, or other fire suppression or prevention technologies, in student housing and dormitories owned or controlled by such entities.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to entities that demonstrate the greatest financial need.

Requires the Secretary to award: (1) at least 10% of the cost of the activities for which assistance is sought; and (2) not less than 10% of the reserved amounts for use by other eligible entities.

Requires grantees to provide (directly or through donations from public or private entities) not less than 50% of the non-federal matching funds.

Prohibits the use of grant funds for administrative expenses.

Makes grant applications, negative determinations, or statements of reasons for the determination inadmissible as evidence in any court, agency, board, or other entity.

Exempts such applications, determinations, or statements as evidence from such admissibility requirements.

Food Sharing Act of 2017 This bill amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to authorize the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to make grants to assist public food program service providers, tribal organizations, or private nonprofit entities that have experience in providing food to individuals in low-income communities or engaging in efforts to reduce food insecurity to develop new resources and strategies to help reduce food insecurity and prevent food insecurity in low-income communities. USDA may also give preference to projects designed to develop new resources and strategies to help reduce food insecurity and prevent food insecurity in low-income communities that are the subject of such projects by:   developing creative food resources, or  coordinating food services with park and recreation programs, and other community-based activities to reduce barriers to access to food.  USDA may also share information concerning projects and issues related to the grant, including information about activities funded with the grant and the degree of success in improving the long-term capacity of the low-income community served by the project to address food and agriculture problems related to hunger or access to healthy food in such community.

Social Security COLA Limitation Act of 1994 - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to reduce the increases applied to higher primary insurance amounts. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to require the Secretary of the Treasury to provide for the application of such amendments to the preceding provisions of the Social Security Act as to have the same effect on the OASDI provisions as in effect in December 1978 and applicable in accordance with this Act.

HOPE VI Green Building and Technical Assistance Act of 2007 - Amends the United States Housing Act of 1937 to prohibit the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development from making a grant to an applicant to carry out a revitalization plan unless the applicant's revitalization plan complies with the following requirements: (1) the revitalization plan complies with the green communities criteria checklist of the national Green Communities program; and (2) the revitalization plan complies with the other nonmandatory items of the green communities criteria checklist so as to result in a cumulative number of points attributable to the nonmandatory items of the criteria checklist of at least 25 points.

Requires the Secretary to verify, or provide for verification, sufficient time to ensure that each revitalization plan complies with the requirements and that the revitalization program is carried out in accordance with such requirements and plan.

Requires the Secretary to use at least two percent of the amount appropriated pursuant to the HOPE VI grant program for any fiscal year for grants to potential applicants and applicants for grants to carry out revitalization programs.

State Temporary Economic Priority (STEP) Act - Authorizes a State to transfer or consolidate funds under certain transportation, education, and job training programs after experiencing economic growth at an annual rate of less than 1% for two calendar quarters.

Requires transferred or consolidated funds to be used in accordance with statutory and regulatory requirements applicable to such programs.

Authorizes States to transfer or consolidate funds from the Highway Trust Fund (HTF) to apportion and allocate amounts for specified programs authorized by title II (No Child Left Behind) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (ESEA), title IV (Improving Academic Achievement for All Children), title V (Innovative Programs for the Next Generation of Scholars), title VI (Improving Academic Achievement for the Next Generation of Scholars, and School Dropouts Prevention), title VII (Improving the Academic Achievement of the Next Generation of Scholars), title VIII (Improving the Academic Achievement of the Next Generation of Scholars and the School Dropout Prevention Program), title IV (Safe and Drug-Free Schools and Communities), title V (Innovative Programs for the Next Generation of Scholars and School Improvement Programs), title VI (Improving Academic Achievement for the Next Generation of Scholars and School Improvement Programs), title VII (Improving Academic Achievement for the

Drunk Driving Repeat Offender Prevention Act of 2009 - Amends federal transportation law to direct the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to withhold 1% of the amount authorized to be apportioned to a state that does not meet the requirements of this Act if the state has not enacted and is not enforcing a law requiring the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence.

Directs the Secretary to withhold 3% of the amount authorized to be apportioned to a state that does not meet the requirements of this Act if the state does not meet the requirements of this Act.

Directs the Secretary to withhold 5% of the amount authorized to be apportioned to a state that does not meet the requirements of this Act.

Requires any funds withheld from apportionment to remain available for apportionment to the state until the end of the third fiscal year following the fiscal year for which the funds are authorized to be appropriated.

Opioid Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to one or more states to carry out a one-year pilot project to develop a standardized peer review process and methodology to review and evaluate prescribing and pharmacy dispensing patterns, through a review of prescription drug monitoring programs (PDMP) in the states receiving such grants. Requires the recipients to develop a systematic, standardized methodology to identify and investigate questionable or inappropriate prescribing and dispensing patterns of substances on schedule II or III under the Controlled Substances Act. Requires the grant recipients to: (1) develop a systematic, standardized methodology to identify and investigate questionable or inappropriate prescribing and dispensing patterns of substances on schedule II or III under the Act; and (2) conduct patient screening, brief interventions, and referral to treatment as needed, with the appropriate state regulators and health profession boards.  Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary to award five-year grants to eligible entities to facilitate training in order to increase the capacity of health care providers to conduct patient screening, brief interventions, and referral to treatment as needed, such as in health care settings to prevent the abuse of prescription drugs, heroin, and other controlled substances.

Kids 2000 Act - Directs the Attorney General to make grants to the Boys and Girls Clubs of America for the purpose of funding effective after-school technology programs, such as PowerUp, to provide: (1) constructive technology-focussed activities that are part of a comprehensive program to provide access to technology and technology training to youth during after-school hours, weekends, and school vacations; (2) supervised activities in safe environments for youth; and (3) full-time staffing with teachers, tutors, and other qualified personnel. 
Requires the Boys and Girls Clubs of America to make subawards to local boys and girls clubs authorizing expenditures associated with providing technology programs, including the hiring of teachers and other personnel, procurement of goods and services, including computer equipment, or such other purposes as are approved by the Attorney General. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Joe Testaverde Adult Stem Cell Research Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to expand, intensify, and coordinate the activities of the National Institutes of Health regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Requires the Director to make grants and contracts to public or nonprofit private entities to pay the costs of planning, establishing, improving, and providing basic operating support for centers of excellence regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Requires the Director to provide for coordination of information among centers and to ensure regular communication between such centers and the Director.

Requires the Director to provide for the establishment of not less than five centers.

Requires the Director to provide for a program under which samples of tissues and genetic materials that are of use in qualifying adult stem cell research are donated, collected, preserved, and made available for such research.

Solar Fuels Innovation Act  (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Energy Policy Act of 2005 to direct the Department of Energy (DOE) to carry out a research initiative to expand theoretical and fundamental knowledge of solar chemistry, electrochemistry, and materials science useful for the practical development of experimental systems to convert solar energy to chemical energy. DOE must leverage expertise and resources from the Basic Energy Sciences Program and the Office of Science, and the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, as provided under this Act.  DOE must organize activities under the initiative to include multidisciplinary teams, which shall pursue aggressive, milestone-driven basic research goals.  DOE must provide sufficient resources for those teams to achieve those goals over a period of time.  The Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy shall support basic research to pursue distinct lines of scientific inquiry, including the production of hydrogen and oxygen from water, and the sustainable reduction of carbon dioxide to fuel products.  DOE must review the program activities to determine the achievement of technical milestones.  DOE must conduct a program to support research needed to replicate natural photosynthetic processes by use of artificial photosynthetic components and materials.  DOE must conduct a program to support research needed to replicate natural synthesis processes by use of artificial photosynthetic components

This bill requires the Director of National Intelligence (DNI) to make publicly available on an Internet website all captured documents related to intelligence activities conducted in Afghanistan and Iraq.  The DNI may review a captured document before making it publicly available.  The DNI may not be required to make a captured document publicly available if it meets certain criteria.  The DNI must report to Congress on each captured document.  The DNI must make a copy of each captured document available for review upon request.  The DNI must report on the progress in making captured documents publicly available.

Iran Sanctions Enhancement Act of 2007 - Amends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 to expand sanctions to include refined petroleum.

Directs the President to impose specified sanctions, including economic sanctions, if the President determines that a person has, with actual knowledge: (1) made an investment of $20 million or more; or (2) provided Iran with refined petroleum resources or engaged in an activity that could contribute to the enhancement of Iran's ability to import refined petroleum resources.

Directs the President to report to the congressional defense and appropriations committees every six months on any person who has provided Iran with refined petroleum resources or any activity that could contribute to the enhancement of Iran's ability to import refined petroleum resources.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Cultural Resource Programs at the National Park Service (NPS), to: (1) facilitate the development of guidelines and a program of technical assistance and grants that will set priorities for the preservation of the Route 66 corridor; and (2) designate officials of the NPS to perform the functions of the Cultural Resource Programs. 
Directs the Secretary to: (1) support efforts of State and local public and private persons and entities interested in the preservation of the corridor; (2) act as a clearinghouse for communication among Federal, State, and local agencies, nonprofit Preservation Organizations, Indian tribes, State historic preservation offices, and private persons and entities interested in the preservation of the corridor after programs are terminated; and (3) assist States in determining the appropriate form of and establishing and supporting a non-Federal entity or entities to perform the functions of the Cultural Resource Programs. 
Requires the Secretary to provide assistance in the preservation of the corridor in a manner that is compatible with the idiosyncratic nature of the corridor. 
Requires the Secretary to: (1) develop a program of technical assistance in the preservation of the corridor and interpretation of the corridor; and (2) coordinate a program of historic
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a limited credit for certain stage 3 aircraft modification property.

Taking Account of Institutions with Low Operation Risk Act of 2015 or the TAILOR Act of 2015 This bill requires the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the National Credit Union Administration, and the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection to tailor any regulatory action that occurs subsequent to enactment of this bill to: (1) the risk profile and business models of the various institutions or classes of institutions subject to the regulatory action, (2) the necessity, appropriateness, and impact of applying such action, and (3) the tailoring of such action in a manner that limits the regulatory compliance impact, cost, liability risk, and other burdens as is appropriate for the risk profile and business model involved. The bill requires the Federal financial institutions regulatory agencies to: (1) report to Congress on the specific actions taken to tailor their regulatory actions, and (2) publish reports on the extent to which such actions result in differential regulation of similarly-situated institutions of diverse charter types with respect to comparable regulations and the reasons for such differential treatment.

Holding Salaries in Escrow  (Sec. 3) This bill requires the Chief Administrative Officer of the House of Representatives, the Chief Administrative Officer of the Senate, and the Office of the Secretary of the Treasury to: (1) determine that the President's budget is not in compliance with the congressional budget resolution due on April 15, 2017, and (2) notify the chairpersons of the congressional budget and appropriations committees within 3 days of the notification.  The bill prohibits appropriations for FY2018 from being made available to the Director of OMB, the Deputy Director of OMB, and the Deputy Director for Management of OMB during any period of noncompliance determined by the Inspector General of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) under this Act.  The bill prohibits the Director of OMB, the Deputy Director of OMB, and the Deputy Director for Management of OMB from receiving pay for any period of noncompliance determined by the Inspector General of OPM after the end of that period. Technological Resource to Assist Criminal Enforcement (TRACE) Act - Amends the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act to require a licensed manufacturer or importer of firearms to: (1) test fire manufactured or imported firearms as specified by the Attorney General; (2) prepare ballistics images of the fired bullet and cartridge casings; (3) make the records available to the Attorney General for entry into a computerized database; and (4) store the fired bullet and cartridge casings.Requires the Attorney General to assist firearm manufacturers and importers in complying with such requirements by: (1) acquiring, installing, and upgrading ballistics equipment and bullet and cartridge casing recovery equipment to be placed at or near the sites of licensed manufacturers and importers; (2) hiring or designating sufficient personnel to develop and maintain a database of ballistics images of fired bullets and cartridge casings; (3) providing education about the role of ballistics as part of a comprehensive firearm crime reduction strategy; (4) providing for the coordination among Federal, State, and local law enforcement and regulatory agencies and the firearm industry to curb firearm-related crime and illegal firearm trafficking; and (5) conducting mandatory ballistics testing of all firearms obtained or in the possession of their respective agencies.Requires

Buy America Update Act - Amends Federal transportation law to revise requirements for the duty-free treatment of imported rolling stock.

Revises requirements for the duty-free treatment of imported steel and iron to require that the cost of components and subcomponents produced in the United States be more than 60% of the cost of all components of the rolling stock.

Directs the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to: (1) review regulations to determine whether manufactured products other than those containing steel and iron should be considered for purposes of domestic content preferences; (2) initiate a rulemaking to develop audit procedures for the agency to review offeror and recipient compliance with domestic content provisions; (3) initiate a rulemaking to develop standards for measuring the percentage value of a component relative to the entire procurement; (4) initiate a rulemaking to further develop standards for measuring the percentage value of a component relative to the entire procurement; and (5) initiate a rulemaking to submit a survey of suppliers to determine whether they provide a supplier who can provide the compliant products for which a waiver will be sought.
