Directs the Secretary of Education to discharge or cancel specified types of student loan indebtedness of spouses, surviving spouses, and parents of individuals who died or became permanently and totally disabled as a result of injuries suffered in the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

Eating Healthy at School Act of 2010 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to study and report to Congress on: (1) the effectiveness and efficiency of administrative review systems to ensure the compliance of local educational agencies (LEAs) participating in the school lunch and breakfast programs; (2) alternative processes and procedures that may improve the effectiveness and efficiency of such systems; and (3) the optimal frequency for carrying out reviews of such systems.

Requires the Secretary to submit a report that describes the study results and recommendations.

Authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations as may be necessary to implement the processes or procedures identified for establishing an effective and efficient administrative review system.

Heavy Truck, Tractor, and Trailer Retail Federal Excise Tax Repeal Act of 2017 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the excise tax on new heavy trucks, tractors, and trailers sold or installed in new highway construction and operation.

Rape Survivor Child Custody Act - Directs the Attorney General to make grants to states that have in place a law that allows the mother of any child conceived through rape to seek court-ordered termination of the parental rights of the rapist with regard to that child. Limits grant amounts to 10% of the average of the total amount of funding of the three most recent awards that the state received under the following grant programs: (1) Part T of title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968; (2) Section 41601 of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994; and (3) the Sexual Assault Services Program.

Women and Alcohol Research Equity Act of 1996 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Director of the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism to obligate at least $43,997,080 for the purpose of carrying out specified research projects on alcohol abuse and alcoholism among women. 
Authorizes appropriations for such projects.

Airline Passenger Fairness Act - Amends Federal transportation law to require the Secretary of Transportation to report on certain certificated air carrier violations, including violations of the prohibition against unfair or deceptive practices in the airline industry.

HSA Accessibility and Portability Act of 2006 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to authorize a health insurance issuer to elect to meet certain requirements for coverage of small employers in the small group market and individual market by requiring an election to guarantee continuation of coverage to the individual after the individual no longer qualifies as an eligible individual of such employer, through issuance of individual health insurance coverage, at a rate that does not exceed 150% of the standard individual rate applicable to such coverage in the state in which the policy was initially issued.

Requires the issuer to guarantee continuation of coverage to the individual after the date the individual no longer qualifies as an eligible individual of such employer, through issuance of individual health insurance coverage, at a rate that does not exceed 150% of the standard individual rate applicable to such coverage in the state in which the policy was initially issued.

Requires the issuer to furnish to the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) information on any such election, including information relating to: (1) the rejection rate of small employers who are denied coverage under this Act; (2) premium rates charged for coverage offered under such election; and (3) the rates charged for coverage offered

Greater Sage Grouse Protection and Recovery Act of 2016 This bill prohibits the Department of the Interior from making a finding under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (ESA) with respect to the Greater Sage grouse in a state that does not have an existing state management plan by September 30, 2026. Until such date, the conservation status of the grouse shall remain not warranted for listing under the ESA.  Interior and the Department of Agriculture (USDA) may not exercise authority under the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (FLapotard) to make, modify, or extend any withdrawal, or amend or otherwise modify any federal resource management plan (fap) to be consistent with the state management plan.  Interior and USDA shall report annually to Congress regarding their implementation and effectiveness of systems to monitor the status of the Greater Sage grouse on federal lands.

Safe, Convenient, Reliable, Efficient, Effective, Next-Generation, Functional, and Secure TSA Act of 2016 or the SCREEN FAST Act This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to establish a pilot program at three airports to: (1) configure and install security systems that increase efficiency and reduce vulnerabilities in airport terminals, and (2) develop and test prototypes of screening security systems and security checkpoint configurations to expedite the movement of passengers by deploying a range of technologies including passive and active systems, new types of security baggage and personal screening systems, and new systems to address passenger and baggage anomalies. The TSA shall establish a pilot program at three airports to: (1) test and evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of the screening and voucher program for airport security system (ASAS) products and services, and (2) accept and provide monetary gifts or bequests to the greatest extent practicable.

Fort Stanton and Rio Bonito Corridor Vegetation Management Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior, in managing land within Fort Stanton and the Rio Bonito Corridor under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior, to solicit competitive bids for and enter into vegetation sales contracts for the purpose of using livestock grazing as a vegetation management tool.  Requires that any such contracts entered into with respect to the land before the date of enactment of this Act are ratified. 
Requires management of Fort Stanton and the Rio Bonito Corridor to be consistent with any applicable land and resource management plan under the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976. 
Provides for distribution and use of proceeds from such sales contracts.

Pay Accountability Act - Requires the payroll administrator of a House of Congress, if a government shutdown is in effect or the public debt limit is reached, to withhold from the payments otherwise required to be made for compensation of Members of Congress who serve in that House an amount equal to the product of one day's worth of pay under the annual rate of compensation for such Members and the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown is in effect or the public debt limit is reached.  Requires the payroll administrator of a Senate chamber to withhold from the payments otherwise required to be made for compensation of the Vice President or the President an amount equal to the product of one day's worth of pay under the annual rate of compensation for such Members and the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown is in effect or the public debt limit is reached.  Requires the Secretary of the Treasury, if a President or Vice President is or is not in office, to withhold from the payments otherwise required to be made for compensation of the President or Vice President an amount equal to the product of one day's worth of pay under the annual rate of compensation for such Members and the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown

Agricultural Credit Expansion Act - Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to deem certain limited liability companies (limited liability companies) and certain other legal entities as eligible for farm loan insurance.

Breast Cancer Patient Education Act of 2012 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide for the planning and implementation of an education campaign to inform breast cancer patients regarding the availability and coverage of breast reconstruction, prostheses, and other options.

Requires such campaign to include dissemination of breast reconstruction, prostheses, and other options.

Prohibits the campaign from specifying or being designed to limit the health care providers available to patients.

Judicial Transparency and Ethics Enhancement Act of 2006 - Amends the federal judicial code to establish for the judicial branch of the government the Office of Inspector General for the Judicial Branch.

Requires the head of the Office to be the Inspector General (IG) appointed by the Chief Justice after consultation with the majority and minority leaders of the Senate and the minority leader of the House of Representatives.

Directs the IG to: (1) conduct investigations of matters pertaining to the Judicial Branch; (2) conduct and supervise audits and investigations; (3) prevent and detect waste, fraud, and abuse; and (4) recommend changes in laws or regulations governing the Judicial Branch.

Grants the IG other powers, including the authority to: (1) make investigations and reports; (2) obtain information or assistance from any federal, state, or local governmental agency, or other entity, including all information kept in the course of business by the Judicial Conference of the United States, the judicial councils of circuits, the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, and the U.S. Sentencing Commission; (3) require attendance and testimony of such witnesses and the production of such records; (4) administer to or take from

Cormorant Management and Natural Resources Protection Act - Amends the Migratory Bird Treaty Act to grant the Secretary of the Interior authority to regulate the importation of cormorants into a State.

Directs the Secretary to conduct educational and informational activities for the owners and operators of aquaculture facilities to improve their efforts to prevent cormorants from consuming aquatic species being reared in such facilities.

Tax Relief for Victims of Disasters Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make the term "qualified federally declared disaster individual" (a taxpayer who resides in a federally declared disaster area and was displaced by reason of a federally declared disaster, or who performed substantially all employment services in the disaster area, and was so employed on the applicable date) inapplicable to a disaster occurring after December 31, 2010; and (2) allow a tax deduction for the loss of taxpayer income attributable to a disaster displaced individuals.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) allow the tax deduction for the tax deduction for housing furnished to displaced individuals in a disaster-affected area; and (2) allow an additional tax deduction for the housing furnished to such individuals.

Hospice Evaluation and Legitimate Payment Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise the criteria for determining whether a hospice physician, nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist, or physician assistant (PASS) has a face-to-face encounter with an individual who is terminally ill and has a continued eligibility determination for hospice care prior to the first 60-day period and each subsequent recertification. (Currently, such an individual must have such an encounter within 60 days of entering into such a recertification.) Revises the criteria for determining whether a Medicare hospice payment methodology revision would adversely affect access to quality hospice care for beneficiaries. Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a Medicare Hospice Payment Reform demonstration program to test the revisions. Requires the Secretary to: (1) conduct an evaluation of the program, and (2) submit recommendations for legislation and administrative action. Requires the Secretary to ensure that revisions implemented as part of the program result in the same estimated amount of aggregate payments as would have been made if the hospice programs had not participated in the demonstration program. Requires the Secretary to submit to Congress

National Neurological Diseases Surveillance System Act of 2010 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to: (1) enhance and expand infrastructure and activities to track the epidemiology of neurological diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease; and (2) incorporate information obtained through such activities into a National Neurological Diseases Surveillance System (NDSSS).

Requires the Secretary to ensure that the NDSSS is designed in a manner that facilitates further research on neurological diseases.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) provide for the collection and storage of information on the incidence and prevalence of neurological diseases in the United States; (2) to the extent practicable, to provide for the collection and storage of other available information on neurological diseases, such as information concerning demographics and other information associated or possibly associated with neurological diseases, such as age, race, ethnicity, sex, geographic location, and family history; (3) may provide for the collection and storage of information relevant to analysis on neurological diseases, such as information concerning the epidemiology of neurological diseases, the natural history of neurological diseases, the prevention of neurological diseases, and the detection, management

Millennium Challenge Compact Improvement Act (MCIA) - Amends the Millennium Challenge Act of 2003 to extend the duration of five-year Millennium Challenge Compacts (MCCs) to five years.

Authorizes the United States and the recipient country to enter into more than one MCC at any given time.

Authorizes concurrent and subsequent MCCs.

Authorizes the assistance of countries and entities, structures, or other arrangements established by two or more eligible countries in connection with a regional Compact to develop and implement a compact.

Authorizes the Chief Executive Officer of the United States to suspend or terminate assistance to one or more countries, as appropriate, based on a determination consistent with this Act.

Amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to require the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to: (1) deny payments to a person or legal entity determined to be ineligible for benefits or payments under the Farmers' Home Loan Program (PHPP) for a period not less than five years; and (2) require the Secretary to submit to the Administrator of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) a determination as to whether the average adjusted gross income, adjusted gross farm income, and adjusted gross nonfarm income of the person or legal entity are within the applicable limitations established under the PHPP.

Allows a person or legal entity to request a reconsideration of a denial of benefits under the PHPP.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for $1,200 of the cost of care provided to an eligible caregiver for a period of at least 180 consecutive days and a portion of which occurs within the taxable year. Defines "applicable individual" as an individual who has been certified by a physician as having long-term care needs that are at least 180 consecutive days, and who is unable to perform, without reminding or cuing assistance, at least three activities of daily living.

Chickasaw National Recreation Area Land Exchange Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey all right, title, and interest in and to the Chickasaw National Recreational Area lands and interests therein, identified as Tract 102-25 on the map, to the Chickasaw Nation.

Requires the fair market values of such land and non-federal land to be determined by an appraisal acceptable to the Secretary and the Chickasaw Nation.

Provides that if the fair market values of such land and non-federal land are not equal, the values may be equalized by the payment of a cash equalization payment by the Secretary or the Chickasaw Nation.

Provides that if the land exchange is not executed within a specified time frame, the items included in the Preliminary Exchange Agreement among the City of Sulphur, the Chickasaw Nation, and the National Park Service may not apply.

Requires the Secretary to revise the boundary of Chickasaw National Recreation Area to reflect that exchange.

Immigration Anti-Discrimination Improvement Act of 1993 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to provide for the application of civil penalties collected under the Act to the appropriation to be used in carrying out such Act. 
Authorizes appropriations for FY 1994 for activities of regional offices of the Special Counsel for Immigration-Related Unfair Employment Practices within the Department of Justice. 
Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Comptroller General to report annually to the Congress on the pervasiveness of unfair immigration-related employment practices and enforcement with respect to such practices. 
Directs the Special Counsel to provide for agreements with Federal and State agencies involved with enforcement of laws relating to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of national origin under which such agencies would receive charges respecting unfair immigration-related employment practices and otherwise forward such charges to the Special Counsel. 
Directs the Attorney General to provide technical assistance to States and local governments concerning the prohibition against employment by aliens in a manner that is discriminatory. 
Directs the Attorney General to establish a monitoring panel to monitor the application of the anti-discrimination provisions in the Immigration and Nationality Act and to report to the Attorney General and the Congress on implementation.

Satellite Home Viewer Protection Act of 1996 - Amends Federal Communications Commission law to require a satellite carrier that makes secondary transmissions of a primary transmission made by a network station to provide the subscriber with a written statement describing and quoting the territorial restrictions of such station.  Requires such statement to describe the circumstances under which a subscriber may not be eligible for satellite service of a particular station. 
Requires a satellite carrier, upon a challenge by a network station regarding whether a subscriber is an unserved household within the predicted grade B contour of the station, to:  (1) inform the subscriber of the station of the challenge; and (2) offer the subscriber the option of conducting a measurement of the signal intensity of the subscriber's household to determine whether the household is an unserved household.  Requires the subscriber, upon request, to be notified of the measurement. 
Authorizes a satellite carrier to negotiate the terms and conditions of the signal intensity measurement.  Requires arbitration if the parties are unable to agree to the terms and conditions of the measurement within 30 days after this Act's enactment.

Ronald Reagan Memorial Act of 2000 - Authorizes the Ronald Reagan Memorial Commission to establish the Ronald Reagan Memorial in accordance with this Act on Federal lands administered by the National Park Service in the District of Columbia.

Requires the National Capital Memorial Commission and the Secretary of the Interior to assist the members of the Commission: (1) in the preparation of a recommendation to the Congress of a permanent location for the memorial; and (2) in carrying out its responsibilities.

Establishes the Ronald Reagan Memorial Commission to raise necessary funds from private sector sources to design, construct, and maintain the memorial.

Requires the Commission to: (1) raise necessary funds from private sector sources to design, construct, and maintain the memorial; (2) select a design for the memorial from proposals solicited and accepted from qualified American architects; and (3) issue a report to the Congress and the President on its activities every six months after its first meeting.

This bill directs the Department of the Interior to sell specified federal land in Mohave County, Arizona, to a qualified entity, which shall convey to the entity all remaining U.S. rights to the covered land.  Interior shall convey to the entity all remaining U.S. rights to the covered land.  Interior shall determine the fair market value of the covered land to be conveyed.

Bodegas as Catalysts for Healthy Living Act - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to carry out a program under which the Administrator makes grants to: (1) locally-based organizations that represent small business concerns; (2) local redevelopment agencies that are chartered, established, or otherwise sanctioned by a state or local government; and (3) local health centers that are chartered, established, or otherwise sanctioned by a state or local government.

Requires a small business to work in collaboration with one or more community-based organizations in expanding that inventory.

Amends title XVIII (Medicare) and title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to cover additional primary and preventive services relating to obesity treatment and prevention, supervised exercise sessions, stress testing, lifestyle modification education, and culinary arts education for promoting proper nutrition.

Border Enforcement Security Task Force Reauthorization Act of 2017 This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to revise the authority of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to establish units for border security and port security best units.  The bill revises the criteria for an "advance unit" for purposes of the DHS homeland security strategic priorities and objectives, including: (1) whether the unit will advance DHS homeland and border security strategic priorities and related objectives; and (2) whether DHS joint cross-border initiatives would be enhanced, improved, or otherwise assisted by the unit.  The bill also revises the reporting requirements for DHS units for border security and port security best units.

Clean Energy Technology Manufacturing and Export Assistance Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish a Clean Energy Technology Manufacturing and Export Assistance Program to: (1) promote policies to reduce production costs and encourage innovation, investment, and productivity among U.S. businesses that produce or export clean energy technologies or related services; (2) implement a national strategy with respect to the exportation of clean energy technologies and related services from the United States; and (3) ensure that U.S. businesses that produce or export clean energy technologies or related services have the necessary information and assistance to be competitive and to create and maintain clean energy technology jobs in the United States.

Medicare Certified Registered Nurse First Assistant Direct Reimbursement Act of 2001 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000, to provide for Medicare coverage of surgical first assisting services of a certified registered nurse first assistant.

Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to extend through December 31, 2007, the Medicare prescription drug plan (PDP) initial enrollment periods. Suspends the late enrollment penalty through December 31, 2007.

Allows a prescription drug plan (PDP) sponsor to remove a covered part D drug from the PDP formulary or impose a restriction or limitation on the coverage of such a drug during the first 12 months of enrollment.

Prohibits the Secretary of Health and Human Services from removing or modifying a covered part D drug formulary or imposing a restriction or limitation on the coverage of such a drug during the period beginning on the date of enrollment and ending on December 31 of the immediately succeeding year.

Requires the PDP sponsor of a PDP to provide an annual notice of any changes in the formulary or other restrictions or limitations on coverage of a covered part D drug.

Waco Mammoth National Monument Establishment Act of 2011 - Establishes the Waco Mammoth National Monument in Texas as a unit of the National Park System.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to complete a general management plan for the Monument.

Terminates designation of the Monument as a unit of the System if federal funding is required to operate and maintain the Monument.

Methane Hydrate Research and Development Amendments Act of 2015 This bill amends the Methane Hydrate Research and Development Act of 2000 to revise the program of methane hydrate research and development.  The program is expanded to include research on methane hydrate as a commercially viable source of energy, exploration and development of methane hydrate resources, and research and development of technologies to reduce the risks of drilling through methane hydrates.  The Department of Energy (DOE) must conduct a long-term environmental monitoring program to study the effects of production from methane hydrate reservoirs.

Local Emergency Health Services Reimbursement Act of 2002 - Amends the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 to reauthorize appropriations for FY 2003 through 2007 for the Federal Emergency Health Services Fund.Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to use specified amounts of such funds to compute an allotment for each of the 17 States with the highest number of undocumented aliens.

Student Credit Card Transparency Act of 2009 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to require each creditor to submit an annual report to the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System containing the terms and conditions of all business, marketing, and promotional agreements and college affinity card agreements with an institution of higher education (IHE), or an alumni organization or foundation affiliated with or related to such IHE, for any college student who is a full-time or a part-time student attending an IHE.

Requires the Comptroller General to review such reports and report to Congress on the impact that such agreements have on credit card debt.

Small Business Jobs Act of 2015 Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a small employer hiring a minimum 2 or more employees a business-related tax credit for the cost of up to 5 employees. Defines "covered employee" as an employee who: (1) first begins work for the employer for services performed by the employee in a trade or business of such employer or in the case of a qualified small employer exempt from tax, in furtherance of the activities related to the purpose or function constituting the basis of the employer's exemption and that is employed on average at least 30 hours per week; and (2) is employed on average at least 30 hours per week, but not more than 5, in any week.

Gas Price and Refinery Capacity Relief Act of 2013 - Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to revise the requirement that the Administrator of the Energy Information Administration (EIA) review and analyze information on refinery outages and unplanned refinery outages to determine whether such scheduling may substantially affect the price or supply of refined petroleum products. Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to study and report to Congress on the costs and benefits of creating a national strategic refined petroleum products reserve.

School-Based Respiratory Health Management Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to give additional preference to a State that: (1) certifies that it has the necessary training and that requires that each public elementary and secondary school in the State: (2) has in place a plan for having on the premises of the school a school nurse or one or more individuals trained personnel who are trained in helping students with allergies and reversible lower airway disorders to identify such students, identify students with a diagnosis of such allergies and reversible lower airway disorders, identify students with such allergies and reversible lower airway disorders education, and provide rescue medications; and (3) has in place a comprehensive school-based allergy and reversible lower airway disorders management program that includes an action plan for each student with a diagnosis of such allergies and reversible lower airway disorders, including an individual student allergies and reversible lower airway disorders education plan.

USDA Civil Rights Resolution Act of 2000 - Amends the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1999 to permit a complainant of a complaint to petition the Civil Rights Division of the Department of Justice (DOJ) to review the complaint and make recommendations to the Department to resolve the complaint within 270 days after the complaint has been investigated by the Department.

Amends the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 to repeal the zero mortality goal for commercial fishing.

Modifies the goal of take reduction plans to require that the plan reduce, within five years after its implementation, the incidental mortality or serious injury of marine mammals incidentally taken in the course of fishing operations.

New Economy Workforce Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to allow certain family-sponsored immigrants to be eligible for a work visa or a work exemption if they do not have a bachelor's degree or higher degree only if there is no qualified individual to whom such a visa or work visa may be made available under the respective paragraph who has such a degree or higher. Includes as a qualifying degree the degree of a foreign student who has successfully completed elementary or secondary school study abroad in the United States or a high school diploma or equivalent.

Requires the Secretary of State to verify the authenticity of any foreign educational credential proffered by an alien.

Requires the Secretary of State to promulgate regulations regarding the allocation of immigrant visas, including to family-sponsored immigrants, pursuant to this Act.

Preserving Access to Manufactured Housing Act of 2013 - Amends the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act to: (1) make the definition of "manufactured housing mortgage" for purposes of the Act inapplicable to a retailer of manufactured or modular homes or its employees unless such retailer or its employees receive compensation or gain for engaging in certain activities that are in excess of any compensation or gain received in a comparable cash transaction; and (2) make the definition of "high cost mortgage" in the Act inapplicable to a retailer of manufactured or modular homes or its employees unless such retailer or its employees receive compensation or gain for engaging in certain activities that are in excess of any compensation or gain received in a comparable cash transaction that is for less than $50,000. Prescott Marine Mammal Rescue Assistance Grant Program to provide grants to eligible stranding network participants for the recovery or treatment of marine mammals, the collection of data from living or dead marine mammals for scientific research regarding marine mammal health, and facility operation costs that are directly related to those purposes.

Drug Price Competition Act of 2009 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to provide that the first applicant for a drug that is approved for human use shall be eligible to receive patent infringement approval no later than 505A (FFCA) days after the drug is approved.

Voluntary Protection Program Act - Directs the Secretary of Labor to establish a program of entering into cooperative agreements with employers to: (1) encourage establishment of comprehensive safety and health management systems that include requirements for systematic assessment of hazards, comprehensive hazard prevention, mitigation, and control programs, and active and meaningful management and employee participation in such systems; and (2) encourage excellence and recognize its achievement in both the technical and managerial protection of employees from occupational hazards.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) establish a voluntary protection program to encourage excellence and recognize its achievement in both the technical and managerial protection of employees from occupational hazards; and (2) take necessary steps for the orderly transition from Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) cooperative agreements and voluntary protection programs carried out before enactment of this Act to agreements and programs authorized under this Act.

Olympic Commemorative Coins Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to issue commemorative one-dollar coins in each six-month period beginning in 1997 to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the founding of the United States Olympic Association and the 40th anniversary of the Summer and Winter Olympic Games.

Bridge Ice and Snow Prevention Pilot Program Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish and implement a pilot program to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of the use of technologies to prevent ice, snow, and other adverse weather effects associated with freezing temperatures on National Highway System bridges.

Strategic Deterrent Sustainment Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to report to the congressional defense and appropriations committees on the capabilities of the U.S. industrial base to achieve specified goals, including: (1) maintaining, modernizing, and sustaining the Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) system until at least 2030; and (2) replacing such system with a follow-on land-based strategic deterrent system after 2030.

Requires the Comptroller General to report to such committees on the consistency of the budget of the President for FY2009, as submitted to Congress pursuant to this Act.

Television Violence Reduction Through Parental Empowerment Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require that television programming be blocked by the blocking apparatus (i.e., a television picture screen) at least 13 inches in size, measured diagonally. 
Prohibits the importation of any such blocking apparatus into the United States. 
Prohibits the selling of such blocking apparatus without trading it. 
Directs the Federal Communications Commission to promulgate rules to implement this Act within 180 days.

Jobs Now Act of 2017 This bill amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to direct the Department of Labor to carry out a two-year pilot program to award competitive grants to general local government or community-based organizations to retain, employ, or train employees providing a public service for their units and for the organizations that provide such services. Helping Individuals Return to Employment Act or the HIRE Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to eligible entities in specified areas to hire unemployed individuals to perform work to benefit communities.

Second Chance Voting Rights Act of 2006 - Grants the right of an individual who is a U.S. citizen to vote in any election for federal office to be denied or abridged because that individual has been convicted of a criminal offense.

Authorizes a person aggrieved by a violation of this Act to provide written notice of the violation to the chief election official of the state involved.

Provides that this Act shall not be construed to prohibit States enacting any state law which affords the right to vote in any federal election on terms less restrictive than those established by this Act.

Requires the grantee to use all grant funds received under this Act to support activities related directly to the recruitment, selection, training, and support of teachers.

Jason's Law - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to implement a pilot program to address the shortage of long-term parking for commercial motor vehicles on the National Highway System (NHS).

National Fab Lab Network Act of 2013 - Establishes the National Fab Lab Network to facilitate the creation of a national network of local fab labs and serve as a resource to assist stakeholders with the effective operation of such labs. Drinking Water Affordability Act of 2016 This bill amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to require the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to promulgate a new national primary drinking water regulation that shall be promulgated in accordance with the Safe Drinking Water Act.  The bill also amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to require the EPA to exempt a public water system that receives financial assistance pursuant to a federal program that is as stringent as the federal program for federal water pollution control to receive a loan or grant from the state for which the loan or grant is being assessed. The bill exempts a public water system from federal cross-cutting requirements if the EPA determines that the state in which the public water system is located has a requirement that is as stringent as the federal cross-cutting requirement. The bill also requires the Government Accountability Office to report to Congress on the results of a study of cost-effective and economically feasible rehabilitation or replacement of drinking water infrastructure to meet the goals of the Safe Drinking Water Act.

Consumer Credit Card Protection Act of 2005 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to prohibit a creditor from using any adverse information concerning a consumer's credit card information as the basis for increasing any annual percentage rate of interest (APR) or decreasing the introductory APR applicable to such account, for reasons other than actions or omissions that are directly related to such account.

Requires the credit card issuer to provide the consumer with: (1) a clear and conspicuous disclosure of the minimum monthly payment required to be made on the account; (2) a table of the number of months it would take to pay the entire balance of the account if the consumer pays only the required minimum monthly payments; and (3) a notice of the required minimum payment period before the beginning of the billing cycle and of any increase in the APR or fee required.

Prohibits an increase in any APR or fee before the end of the 30-day period beginning on the date the obligor receives a specific notice of the imposition of such fee.

Requires the consumer to be provided with an explanation of the imposition of such a fee or any reason for its imposition.

American Textile Technology Innovation and Research for Exportation (ATTIRE) Act - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish a competitive grant program to fund textile research and innovation and to promote increased textile exports. Requires the funds authorized to be appropriated for the grant program to be used for research and development activities that achieve at least one of the following goals: (1) to build and sustain innovation, competitiveness, and best practices in the U.S. textile industry; (2) to contribute to transforming the U.S. textile industry into a highly flexible supply chain, capable of responding to rapidly changing market demands, including shifts to technologically advanced textile production; (3) to design and develop new materials and innovative and improved manufacturing and integrated systems, essential to the success of a modern textile industry; (4) to train personnel, establish industrial partnerships, and create transfer mechanisms to ensure the utilization of technologies developed; and (5) to strengthen the Nation's textile research and educational efforts by uniting diverse experts and resources in unique collaborative projects. Veterans Benefits Network Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make grants to a state or local government, a regional council of governments, or a private entity to establish or expand a regional technology system to provide an active database and enrollment system that can be used by a coordinated network of private, public, and nonprofit entities to assist veterans and their family members in applying for benefits and services offered by such entities that participate in the network.

Counseling in Shelters Act of 2002 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Assistant Secretary for the Administration on Children, Youth, and Families, to make grants to eligible entities for the purpose of providing on site mental health and substance abuse counseling and referral services.

Community-Based Overweight and Obesity Prevention Program - Amends the Individuals with Disabilities Improvement and Assistance Act of 1996 to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a community-based overweight and obesity prevention program to award grants and contracts to: (1) plan evidence-based programs for the prevention of overweight and obesity among children and their families through improved nutrition and increased physical activity; or (2) implement such programs.

Requires grant or contract recipients to demonstrate community support and to include a broad cross-section of stakeholders, including health care providers, universities, local educational agencies, state, local, and tribal health departments, state, local, and tribal park and recreation departments, employers, and health insurance companies.

Requires grant or contract recipients to: (1) establish a steering committee to provide input on the assessment of, and recommendations on improvements to, their programs funded through the grant or contract; and (2) have input on the overweight and obesity problem in their communities.

Emergency Mortgage Loan Modification Act of 2008 - Requires a servicer of a residential mortgage loan to: (1) act in a manner consistent with the duty to maximize, or to not adversely affect, the recovery of total proceeds from pooled residential mortgage loans; and (2) act on behalf of the securitization vehicle in the best interest of all investors and holders of beneficial interests in the loans, in the aggregate, if for a loan that is in default or for which payment default is imminent or reasonably foreseeable.

Makes a servicer of a residential mortgage loan that acts in a manner consistent with this Act, under the best interest of all investors and holders of beneficial interests in the loans, ineligible for entering into a qualified loan modification or workout plan, to: (1) any person, based on that person's ownership of a residential mortgage loan or any interest in a pool of loans or in securities that distribute payments out of the principal, interest, and other payments in loans on the pool; (2) any person who is obligated pursuant to a derivatives instrument to make payments in reference to any loan or any interest; or (3) any person that insures any loan or any interest.

International Commerce Enhancement Act - Amends the Arms Export Control Act to increase the authorization of appropriations for the Secretary of Defense for FY 2004 and 2005 for: (1) the transfer to Japan of certain defense articles and services; (2) the transfer to any other country of certain military exports to such country; (3) the transfer to any other country of certain loans to any other country; and (4) the transfer to any other country of certain license applications for commercial sales of military equipment and other products.

Increases the authorization of appropriations for the Secretary for FY 2005 for: (1) the transfer to any other country of certain military exports to such country; (2) the transfer to any other country of certain loans to any other country; and (3) the transfer to any other country of certain license applications for commercial sales of military equipment and other products.

Rush Hour Congestion Relief Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish and implement a traffic incident management program to assist states and localities in: (1) regional traffic incident management program planning; and (2) mitigating the effects of traffic delays resulting from accidents, breakdowns, and other non-recurring incidents on highways.

Authorizes the use of funds apportioned to a State under this Act to: (1) develop regional traffic incident management plans; (2) purchase or lease telecommunications equipment for first responders as part of the development of a regional traffic incident management program; (3) purchase or lease equipment to support the clearance of traffic incidents; (4) rent vehicle storage or staging areas immediately adjacent to roadways as part of a regional traffic incident management program; (5) traffic service patrols as part of a regional traffic incident management program; (6) enhance hazardous materials incident response; (7) traffic management systems in support of traffic incident management; (8) traffic incident management training; (9) crashes investigation equipment; (10) other activities under a regional traffic incident management plan; and (11) statewide incident reporting systems.

Requires the Secretary to develop a regional traffic incident management plan

Safer Trucks and Buses Act of 2015 This bill requires the Department of Transportation to ensure that certain motor carrier data it collects and analyzes is not made available to the public. The bill terminates that effect on the date on which the Department submits to Congress the report required under this Act. The bill requires the Department to enter into an agreement with the National Academy of Public Administration to have the Academy study the compliance, safety, accountability initiative of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA). The Academy must conduct a study on how to improve the FMCSA's compliance, safety, accountability initiative. The National Academy must report on the results of the study and certify that the study is complete.

Colorectal Cancer Detection Act of 2018  This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide Medicare coverage for a year's worth of screening blood-based tests for the early detection of colorectal cancer.

Infertility Research Centers Act of 2002 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Director of the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development to make grants to, or enter into contracts with, public or nonprofit private entities for the development and operation of centers to conduct activities for the purpose of improving methods of preventing infertility.Requires the Director to provide for the establishment of two centers with respect to infertility prevention.Authorizes each center to use funds provided under this Act to provide stipends for health and allied health professionals enrolled in clinical trials.Requires the Director to provide for the coordination of information among the centers.Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a program of entering into agreements with qualified health professionals under which such health professionals agree to conduct research with respect to infertility prevention.

Amends the Forest Service Administrative Review Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a pre-decisional administrative review process for Forest Service actions involving land and resource management plans.

Federal Reserve Accountability Act of 2009 - Authorizes the Comptroller General (GAO) to review the accounting, financial reporting, and internal controls of credit facilities established by the Federal Reserve Board or any federal reserve bank, including when such activities are carried out by or on behalf of the board or any official of a federal reserve bank.

Requires the Comptroller General to report to Congress on each such review, including with respect to the audit of credit facilities.

Prohibits the Comptroller General from disclosing to any person or entity, including to the Congress, the names or identifying details of specific participants in any of the audited facilities or identifying details regarding assets or collateral held by, under, or in connection with any of the audited facilities and any report provided under this Act.

Requires the Comptroller General to release a nonredacted version of any reports on specific credit facilities, one year after the termination of the relevant facility.

Requires the board to place on its website a link to a repository of information made available to the public for a reasonable period of time, not less than six months following the date of release of the relevant information, including: (1) the reports prepared by
Cures Can Be Found Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a personal credit for qualified stem cell research, storage, and donation.

Regulatory Integrity Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill requires each executive agency to make publicly available in a prominent location either on the agency website or in its rulemaking docket the following information regarding any agency regulatory action: (1) the date on which the agency first began to develop or consider the agency regulatory action, (2) the status of the agency regulatory action, (3) an estimate of the status of the action, (4) a brief description of the agency regulatory action, (5) if applicable, a list of agency regulatory actions that duplicate or overlap with the agency regulatory action, and (6) any public communication with respect to the pending agency regulatory action.  The agency must publish such information within 24 hours after a public communication relating to a pending agency regulatory action is issued and maintain the public availability of such information not less than five years after the date on which the pending agency regulatory action is finalized.  Any public communication issued by an agency that refers to a pending agency regulatory action must specify whether the agency is considering alternatives, accepting or will be accepting comments, and disclosing the information to the intended recipients.  The agency must report to Congress on the number of public communications issued by the agency during the fiscal

Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop and issue public service announcements that advertise and promote the pharmacist profession, highlight its advantages and rewards, and encourage individuals to enter the profession.

Directs the Secretary to award grants to entities to support State and local advertising campaigns through appropriate media outlets to promote the profession, highlight its advantages and rewards, and encourage individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds to enter it.

Requires the Secretary to establish a demonstration project to enhance the participation of pharmacists in the National Health Service Corps Loan Repayment Program.

Requires the Secretary to report to specified congressional committees on the project.

Knife Owners' Protection Act of 2017 This bill provides that any person who is not otherwise prohibited by federal law from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a knife or knives shall be entitled to transport a knife or knives from any place where such person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport such a knife or knives to any other place where such person may lawfully do so if: (1) in the case of transportation by motor vehicle, the knife or knives are not directly accessible from the passenger compartment or, in the case of a motor vehicle without a compartment separate from the passenger compartment, the knife or knives shall be contained in a locked container, glove compartment, or console; or (2) in the case of transportation by other means (including any conveyance over land, on or through water), the knife or knives are contained in a locked container.  A person who is transporting a knife or knives in compliance with this bill may not be arrested or otherwise detained for violation of any federal law related to knife possession, transportation, or carrying of knives, unless there is probable cause to believe that the person is not in compliance with at least one of the requirements of this bill.
