Child Modeling Exploitation Prevention Act - Amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to prohibit employers from employing a child model in exploitive child modeling. 
Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit anyone from making a financial gain by displaying or offering to provide the image of an individual engaged in exploitive child modeling. 
Provides that whoever, in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce, with the intent to make a financial gain thereby: (1) displays or offers to provide the image of an individual engaged in exploitive child modeling; and (2) does so with a serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value is subject to criminal penalties.

Presidential Transition Act of 2000 - Amends the Presidential Transition Act of 1963 to revise the presidential transition process by requiring the Office of Government Ethics to study and report on improvements to the financial disclosure process for Presidential nominees required to file reports under the Ethics in Government Act of 1978.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to transfer specified land within the Standing Rock Indian Reservation of North Dakota to the Secretary of the Interior for the benefit of the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the state of North Dakota all interest of the United States in and to the covered property.

Declares that the transfer of land to the state shall not interfere with any of the authorized purposes of the Oahe Dam and Reservoir Project, any project of the Pick-Sloan Missouri River Basin Program, or any applicable law.

Requires the Secretary of the Army to retain any right of property interests necessary to carry out authorized purposes of the Oahe Dam and Reservoir Project or any project of the Pick-Sloan Missouri River Basin Programs.

Requires the Secretary of the Army to retain any land, structures, easements or other property interests necessary to carry out authorized purposes of the Oahe Dam and Reservoir Project or any project of the Pick-Sloan Missouri River Basin Programs.

Requires the Secretary of the Army to prepare a map of the transferred land.

Requires the tribe to be responsible for the payment of all costs and administrative expenses associated with the transfer and the state of North

International Remittance Services Enhancement and Protection Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Credit Union Act to include among authorized federal credit union disclosures: (1) any fees to be charged to the recipient, including exchange rate or currency conversion fees; (2) a final itemization of all costs; and (3) the exact amount of foreign currency to be received by the recipient in the foreign country.Requires the appropriate federal banking agencies to prescribe regulations requiring any financial institution or money transmitting business initiating an international money transfer on behalf of a consumer to provide specified disclosures to the consumer before the transaction's completion.
Animal Agriculture Environmental Incentives Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer to elect an income tax credit for 25 percent of the costs of animal feeding operations.

Provides that a health care provider shall not be considered to be in noncompliance with specified requirements of title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act and related regulations for electronic transactions and codes of health care practices before October 16, 2003.  Requires a health care provider or, subject to specified requirements, a health care clearinghouse to comply with such requirements without regard to such requirements.

Protection from Sexual Predators Act of 1997 - Expresses the sense of the Congress that States should more seriously consider the relatively high recidivism rate of sexual offenders when deciding whether to plea bargain with a first-time sexual offender and whether to grant parole to sexual offenders, and States should review their treatment and parole supervision programs for sexual offenders to assure that these programs are fulfilling their goals, if they are not. 
Amends the Federal criminal code to provide that a State is not eligible for a grant under the Truth in Sentencing in Criminal Law Grants Act unless the State has provided assurances to the Attorney General that such State has in effect laws which allow the court to impose a sentence of life in prison without parole on a defendant who is convicted of a State offense for conduct that:  (1) is an offense under the Federal criminal code or a State code; or (2) would have been an offense under either of such laws if the offense had occurred in the special maritime or territorial jurisdiction of the United States. 
Amends the Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act of 1994 to make a State ineligible for a grant under such Act unless it has provided assurances to the Attorney

Meat and Poultry Products Traceability and Safety Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Meat Inspection Act to require the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a traceability system for all stages of production, processing, and distribution of meat and meat food products that are produced through the slaughter of animals.

Prohibits the Secretary from: (1) prohibiting entry into any slaughtering establishment inspected under this Act of any cattle, sheep, swine, goats, or horses, mules, or other equines not identified as prescribed by the Secretary; or (2) restricting entry into any slaughtering establishment inspected under this Act of any poultry not identified as prescribed by the Secretary.

Prohibits any person, firm, or corporation from: (1) falsifying or misrepresenting to any other person, firm, or corporation any information as to any premises at which any cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules, or other equines, or the carcasses thereof were held; or (2) altering, detaching, or destroying any records or other means of identification.

Veterans Timely Access to Health Care Act - Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to prescribe an appropriate standard for access to care, determined from the date on which a veteran contacts the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) seeking an appointment until the date on which a visit with a primary-care provider is completed, that is 30 days long.

Requires the Secretary to periodically review the performance of VA health-care facilities in meeting the standard.

Authorizes the Secretary, in any case in which unable to meet such standard, to use the Secretary's authority to furnish health care and services for that veteran in a non-VA facility.

Requires the Secretary to report annually to the congressional veterans' committees on the experience of the VA with respect to waiting times for veterans seeking appointments with a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) health-care provider.

Historically Women's Public Colleges or Universities Historic Building Restoration and Preservation Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to make grants to historically women's public colleges or universities for the preservation and restoration of historic buildings and structures on their campuses. 
Subjects such grants to the condition that the grantee agree, for the period of time specified by the Secretary, that: (1) no alteration will be made in the property with respect to which the grant is made without the concurrence of the Secretary; and (2) reasonable public access for interpretive and educational purposes be permitted by the grantee for interpretive and educational purposes. 
Authorizes the Secretary to obligate funds made available for FY 2001 for a building or structure listed on the National Register of Historic Places, designated as a National Historic Landmark, or located within a designated historic district, only if the grantee agrees to provide for activities under the grant, from funds derived from non-Federal sources, an amount equal to 50 percent of the costs of the grant. 
Authorizes in addition to cash outlays and payments, in-kind contributions of property or personnel services by non-Federal interests, to be used for the non-Federal share of costs required by this Act.

Global Investments in America's Cities Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require specified numbers of EB-5 (intracompany visa) visas for qualified immigrants seeking to invest in a new commercial enterprise in an economically distressed urban area.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to set aside specified amounts of capital for such an enterprise.

Requires the Government Accountability Office to submit a report to Congress on the EB-5 Visa Program.

Small Business Expansion and Hiring Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business tax credit for the retained worker credit, which is the aggregate of the lesser of $4,000 ($6,000 for a long-term unemployed individual) or 6.2% of wages paid to such employee during the 52-week period following their employment in the taxpayer's business. Defines "retained worker" as an individual who: (1) is employed by the taxpayer on any date during the taxable year in which the taxpayer ends the 60-day period during which the individual was employed by the taxpayer; and (2) certifies that the individual has not been employed for 40 hours or more per week during the 60-day period ending on the date the individual begins such employment.

Making Education Affordable Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award grants to institutions of higher education (IHEs) that carry out a dual or concurrent enrollment program or an early college high school program that enables students to earn college credits while in high school.

Gives grant priority to IHEs serving students from low-income families, students from rural communities, or students who are the first in their family to receive postsecondary education.

Requires IHEs to provide teachers, principals, and other school leaders with professional development activities that enhance or enable the provision of such programs.

Allows grantees to use grant funds for the costs associated with carrying out such programs, including the costs of: (1) tuition and fees, books, and required instructional materials; and (2) transportation to and from the program.

Helping Responsible Homeowners Act - Requires the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to carry out a program under which mortgages they insure are refinished or refienned on their own property through a refinancing mortgage.

Requires the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation to: (1) provide for the refinancing of mortgages on single-family housing owned by such enterprises; and (2) require each servicer of a mortgage owned or guaranteed by such enterprises to inform each borrower of such mortgage of the refinancing program.

Prohibits the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation from charging the mortgagee any up-front fee beyond the standard guarantee fee for the refinancing of the mortgage.

Terminates such programs after one year after enactment of this Act.

Requires the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation to inform each borrower of any second lien for a mortgage they refuse to resubordinate.

Women's Human Rights Protection Act of 1993 - Directs the Secretary of State to report to the Congress on the steps taken to create the position described in this Act and to make certain determinations regarding the ratification of CEDAW.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) expand the definition of "infrastructure property" for purposes of the tax deduction for depreciation of such property; (2) expand the definition of "publicly traded partnership" for purposes of the tax deduction for income from related improvements; (3) allow an exception for income from publicly traded partnerships; (4) allow the treatment of infrastructure property as five-year property for purposes of the depreciation deduction for related improvements; and (5) allow the treatment of infrastructure property as a like-kind exchange for purposes of the tax deduction for exchange of property held for productive use or investment.

Independent Pharmacy Protection Act of 2006 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require each contract entered into with a Medicare Advantage (MA) sponsor for a prescription drug plan (PDP) to provide for: (1) direct deposit payments; (2) increased dispensing fees for generic drugs; and (3) payment of dispensing fees to each participating pharmacy for covered drugs dispensed through the participating pharmacy.

Requires the payment of dispensing fees to encourage use of generic drugs.

Provides for a non-disputed claim for a covered drug that is therapeutically equivalent and bioequivalent to a brand name drug that is a covered drug.

Return of Talent Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish the Return of Talent Program to permit eligible aliens to temporarily return to their country of citizenship in order to make a material contribution to that country if the country is engaged in post-conflict or natural disaster reconstruction activities, for a period not exceeding 24 months, unless an exception is granted under specified circumstances.

Authorizes an alien who participates in the Program to return to the alien's country of citizenship with the alien and reenter the United States with the alien.

Defines: (1) "eligible immigrant" as an immigrant who: (1) has been lawfully admitted to the United States for permanent residence; (2) demonstrates an ability and willingness to make a material contribution to the post-conflict or natural disaster reconstruction in the alien's country of citizenship; and (3) is a U.S. citizen who is a citizen of a country in which the U.S. armed forces are engaged, or have engaged in the 10 years preceding such determination, in combat or peacekeeping operations.

Lifelong Improvements in Food and Exercise (LIFE) Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to carry out a national program to conduct and support activities regarding individuals who are overweight or obese in order to make progress toward the goal of significantly reducing the number of cases of obesity among individuals in the United States.

Directs the Secretary to carry out such activities with respect to individuals who are overweight: (1) training health professionals to recognize that patients are overweight and to recommend prevention activities regarding such condition, including educating patients on the relationship between such condition and cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and on proper nutrition and regular physical activities; (2) educating the public with respect to the condition of being overweight; and (3) developing and demonstrating intervention strategies for use at worksites and in community settings such as hospitals and community health centers.

SOAR to Health and Wellness Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a pilot program to provide training to health care providers and other related providers on human trafficking to enable such providers to:   identify potential human trafficking victims,  implement proper protocols and procedures for working with law enforcement to report and facilitate communication with such victims,  implement proper protocols and procedures for referring victims to social or victims service agencies or organizations,  provide such victims care that is coordinated, victim centered, culturally relevant, comprehensive, evidence based, gender responsive, age appropriate, and trauma informed, and   consider the potential for integrating such training with existing training programs for victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking, child abuse, child neglect, child maltreatment, and child sexual exploitation.   The pilot program shall terminate on October 1, 2022. HHS must collect data on the number of facilities operating under the pilot program and the number of health care providers and other related providers trained through the program during FY2018-FY2022.

Seniors Financial Fraud Prevention Act of 2010 - Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to establish a separate office within the FTC to prevent fraud targeting seniors and to assist with: (1) oversight; (2) consumer education; (3) means of referring complaints; and (4) procedures to log and acknowledge the receipt of complaints by individuals who certify that they have a reasonable belief that they have been the victim of fraud in connection with the conduct of mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud.

Community Health Center Volunteer Provider Protection Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to include volunteer practitioners in the definition of "volunteer physician" for purposes of the liability protections for physician practitioners.

Directs the Comptroller General to study the adequacy of funding for liability coverage through the program under the Public Health Service Act for: (1) public or nonprofit private entities receiving Federal funds for health centers under such Act; and (2) volunteer practitioners serving such health centers.

Dru's Law - Directs the Attorney General to: (1) make public in a registry from information contained in the National Sex Offender Registry, via the Internet, all information regarding convicted persons who are: (1) victims of sexual or violent predator offenses; or (2) sexually violent predators.

Requires the public registry to provide to the Attorney General: (1) the name and any known aliases of the person; (2) the date of birth and physical description; (3) the current address and photograph; (4) a physical description and current photograph; (5) the nature of and date of commission of the offense; (6) the date on which the person is released from prison or placed on parole, supervised release, or probation; and (7) any other information the Attorney General considers appropriate.

Requires a State that provides for a civil commitment proceeding to: (1) notify the attorney general of the impending release of any person incarcerated who is a sexually violent predator or who has been deemed by the State to be at high-risk for recommitting any sexually violent offense or criminal offense against a minor; and (2) intensively monitor any such person who has been unconditionally released by the State and

Gerardo Hernandez Airport Security Act of 2014 - Directs the Assistant Secretary of Homeland Security (Transportation Security Administration) (TSA) to conduct outreach to all U.S. airports at which the TSA performs, or oversees the implementation and performance of, security measures, and provide technical assistance as necessary, to verify such airports have in place individualized working plans for responding to security incidents inside the airport, including active shooters, acts of terrorism, and incidents that target passenger-screening checkpoints.  Authorizes the Assistant Secretary to: (1) provide to Congress an analysis of how the TSA can use cost savings achieved through efficiencies to increase over the next five fiscal years the funding available for checkpoint screening law enforcement support reimbursementable agreements; and (2) conduct a review of the interoperable communications capabilities of the law enforcement, fire, and medical personnel responsible for responding to a security incident at all U.S. airports at which the TSA performs, or oversees the implementation and performance of, security measures.

Stock Option Accounting Reform Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to require all publicly traded securities to show in their annual reports on their fair value that are issued or terminated after December 31, 2004, to a named executive officer of the issuer of securities granted after such date.

Requires the Commission on Stock Option Accounting Reform to review and report to the Congress on mandatory expensing of all employee stock options.

Livestock Concentration Report Act - Directs the Commissioner on Concentration in the Livestock Industry to report to the President, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, and the President pro tempore of the Senate on the study of concentration in the red meat packing industry. 
Directs the Commission to:  (1) determine whether the study adequately examined and identified specified procurement markets for slaughter cattle in the continental United States, analyzed the effects that slaughter cattle procurement practices have on the purchasing and pricing of slaughter cattle by beef packers, examined the use of captive cattle supply arrangements by beef packers and the effects of such arrangements on slaughter cattle markets, examined the economics of vertical integration and of coordination arrangements in the hog slaughtering and processing industry, reviewed the pricing and procurement by hog slaughtering plants operating in the Eastern corn belt, reviewed the pertinent research literature on issues relating to the structure and operation of the meat packing industry, and represents the current situation in the livestock industry compared to the situation reflected in specified data; (2) request the Attorney General to report on the application of the antitrust laws and the operation of Federal laws applicable to the concentration and vertical integration in the procurement and pricing of slaughter cattle and of slaughter hogs by meat packers; (3) review

Law Enforcement Protection Act of 1997 - Amends the Federal criminal code to authorize an individual to carry a concealed firearm if that individual is:  (1) a qualified law enforcement officer or a qualified former law enforcement officer; and (2) carrying appropriate written identification. 
Exempts qualified current and former law enforcement officers from State and local laws prohibiting the carrying of a firearm on Federal property, installations, buildings, bases, or parks. 
Gives Congress the right to enter into interstate compacts or agreements for cooperative effort to enable individuals to carry concealed weapons.

Art-in-Architecture Act of 1993 - Requires that not less than one percent of the funds made available for new construction, building purchase, acquisition, or prospectus-level repair and alteration projects shall be made available for art projects for the building. 
Authorizes the Administrator of the General Services Administration to increase the percentage of such funds for a project warranting more artwork, such as a building with exceptional public space whose architectural character and scale would accommodate and be significantly enhanced by large-scale, high-quality artwork. 
Provides that the Administrator shall commission works of art by living American artists to be placed in Federal buildings. 
Directs the Administrator to commission works of art based upon their artistic merit, estimated value, and scope of work. 
Requires the Administrator to establish procedures for commissioning of art. 
Exempts Commissioning of art from Federal property and Administrative Services Act requirements. 
Requires the Administrator to maintain and preserve the works of art in a state of high quality. 
Requires the fine arts officer of the agency to maintain a registry of portfolios and statements of qualifications for artists interested in being considered for art projects.

Promoting Self-Reliance for the World's Poorest Act of 2002 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to authorize the Administrator of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) to make grants to eligible recipients for programs under which 50 percent or more of the clients are initially very poor.

Requires the Administrator to: (1) develop poverty measurement methods to measure the level of poverty of clients of sustainable poverty-focused programs; and (2) implement poverty measurement methods in accordance with this Act, with a specified interim methodology.

Requires grant assistance to be targeted assistance to the very poor if at least 50 percent of the clients of the program or service are among the very poor as described in this Act.

Northern Yukon-Arctic International Wildlife Refuge Act - Establishes the Northern Yukon-Arctic International Wildlife Refuge in order to permanently commemorate the long-existing relationship of peace and good will between the people and the Governments of Canada and the United States. 
Establishes the United States portion of the Refuge in order to protect the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR) administered under the National Wildlife Refuge System Administration Act of 1966. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Bright Idea Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to initiate a project to establish technical standards for general service lamps.

Requires the initial technical standards established to be standards that enable those lamps to provide levels of illumination equivalent to those provided by general service lamps generally available in 2007, but with a level of 30-watt and 45-watt lumens per watt ratings that are at least 30 by calendar year 2013 and 45 by calendar year 2018, respectively.

Requires the Secretary to consult with interested parties and make necessary technical and market research and development actions.

Authorizes the Secretary to carry out a lighting technology research and development program to: (1) support the research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of lamps and related technologies sold, offered for sale, or otherwise made available in the United States; and (2) assist manufacturers of general service lamps in the manufacturing of general service lamps that achieve the lumens per watt ratings established by this Act.

Directs the Secretary to carry out a comprehensive national program to educate consumers about the benefits of using light bulbs that have improved efficiency

Traveler Redress Improvement Act of 2017 (Sec. 2) This bill requires the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to ensure that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Traveler Redress Inquiry Program (DHS TRIP) is available to adjudicate inquiries for individuals who: (1) are U.S. citizens or aliens lawfully admitted for permanent residence, (2) have been given enhanced screening at an airport passenger security checkpoint more than three times in any 60-day period, and (3) believe they have been falsely identified as being a threat to aviation security.  The TSA shall ensure that the DHS TRIP is implemented to ensure that the program is in place to adjudicate such inquiries.  The TSA shall report to Congress on the implementation of the program and on any privacy impact review and update.  The TSA shall review and update the Privacy Impact Assessment for Secure Flight programs to ensure that it is accurate.  The TSA shall review and update the Privacy Impact Assessment for the Secure Flight programs to ensure that it is accurate.  The TSA shall review and update the risk analysis for the Secure Flight programs.  The TSA shall review and update the risk analysis for the Secure Flight

Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend temporarily the duty on certain isomers of isomers of 3-butylamine, 3-isomer of isomers of 3-butylamine, and 3-isomer of isomers of 3-butylamine.

Teacher Tax Credit Act of 2007 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 50% of the expenses of a kindergarten through grade 12 classroom teacher, instructor, counselor, aide, or principal in an elementary or secondary school on a full-time basis for an academic year ending during a taxable year. Defines "qualified elementary and secondary education expenses" as expenses for books, supplies, computer equipment, and other equipment, and supplementary materials used by such a teacher in the classroom. Defines "qualified professional development expenses" as expenses for tuition, fees, books, supplies, equipment, and transportation required for the enrollment or attendance of an individual in a qualified course of instruction.

This bill requires the United States to: (1) take all necessary and appropriate steps to ensure the safety of the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya (the former Camp Ashraf refugee camp in Iraq); (2) provide all necessary and appropriate assistance to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees to process applications by the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya for refugee status and to secure their orderly resettlement in safe locations outside of Iraq, including in the United States for any such residents who express such a desire; and (3) timely admit as refugees the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya in the United States and in doing so shall not delay or bar such resettlement.

(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on May 22, 2003. The summary of that version is repeated here.) Basic Pilot Program Extension and Expansion Act of 2003 - Amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to extend the basic immigration and immigrant registration program through December 1, 2004. Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to expand the operation of the basic immigration and immigrant registration program to all 50 States by December 1, 2004. Requires the Secretary to report to the Congress on the processing priority under the pilot immigration program for regional centers to promote economic growth. (Currently, such priority applies only to petitions for alien admission to the United States.) Amends the Departments of Commerce, Justice, and State, the Judiciary, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1993 to extend the authority of the Secretary of Homeland Security to give priority to immigrant visa issuance under the pilot program to certain foreign nationals seeking to gain U.S. citizenship. (Currently, such priority applies only to petitions for alien admission to the United States.) Directs the General Accounting Office to report to Congress on

Enhancing Nutrition in Medical Education Act of 2004 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to award grants to accredited schools of medicine to integrate innovative curricula on nutrition into medical education.

Directs the Secretary to ensure that innovative curricula on nutrition developed and implemented under this Act focus on preventive health measures, including: (1) education on the causes, treatment, and prevention of obesity; (2) office education and counseling to ensure appropriate diet for mostly healthy people; (3) prevention and treatment of common nutritional deficiencies; (4) appropriate and inappropriate use of herbs and supplements; and (5) office recognition and treatment of common eating disorders.

Requires schools receiving such grants to establish a multidisciplinary planning committee to develop the curricula.

Witness Security and Protection Grant Program Act of 2011 - Directs the Attorney General to make competitive grants to eligible state, tribal, and local governments to establish or maintain witness protection programs that provide protection or assistance to witnesses in: (1) court proceedings involving homicide or involving a serious violent felony or serious drug offense; and (2) court proceedings involving gangs or organized crime.

Requires the Attorney General to: (1) direct the appropriate offices within the Department of Justice (DOJ) to provide technical assistance to the extent the Attorney General determines such assistance is needed to establish or maintain such a program; and (2) develop best practice models to assist states and other relevant entities in addressing witness protection and assistance issues.

Oil Industry Merger Antitrust Enforcement Act - Amends the Clayton Act to require the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the Department of Justice (DOJ) to jointly review and revise enforcement guidelines and policies, including the Horizontal Merger Guidelines issued April 2, 1992, and the Non-Horizontal Merger Guidelines issued June 14, 1984, and modify those guidelines to ensure that they will prevent any merger and acquisition in the oil industry when the effect of such a merger or acquisition may be to substantially lessen competition or to tend to create a monopoly. 
Requires the FTC and DOJ to review and revise enforcement guidelines and policies, including the Horizontal Merger Guidelines, to specifically address mergers and acquisitions in oil companies and among companies involved in the production, refining, distribution, or marketing of petroleum, oil, natural gas, or products derived from petroleum, oil, or natural gas and to ensure that the application of such guidelines will prevent any merger and acquisition in the oil industry when the effect of such a merger or acquisition may be to substantially lessen competition or to tend to create a monopoly.

Amends the Clean Air Act to define "renewable biomass" as materials, pre-commercial thinnings, or invasive species from National Forest System land and public lands that: (1) are byproducts of preventive treatments that are removed to reduce hazardous fuels, to reduce or contain disease or insect infestation, or to restore ecosystem health; (2) would not otherwise be used for higher-value products; and (3) are harvested in accordance with applicable law and land management plans and requirements.

Defines "renewable biomass" as: (1) materials, pre-commercial thinnings, or invasive species from National Forest System land and public lands that are byproducts of preventive treatments that are removed to reduce hazardous fuels, to reduce or contain disease or insect infestation, or to restore ecosystem health; (2) any organic matter that is available on a renewable or recurring basis from non-federal land or land belonging to an Indian or Indian tribe that is held in trust by the United States or subject to a restriction against alienation imposed by the United States; or (3) any organic matter that is available on a renewable or recurring basis from nonfederal land or land belonging to an Indian or Indian tribe that is held in trust by the United States that is held in accordance with applicable

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (ESEA) to require local educational agencies (LEAs) receiving assistance under the Act to provide, upon a request made by a military recruiter or an institution of higher education, access to the name, address, and telephone listing of each secondary school student served by the LEA, unless the parent of such student has submitted the prior consent request.

Authorizes a parent of a secondary school student to submit a written request to the LEA that the student's name, address, and telephone listing not be released for purposes of this Act without prior written parental consent.

Requires the LEA to notify parents of the option to make such request.

Requires the LEA to determine whether the LEA is failing to comply with this Act and, upon determining that it is not failing, to impose a penalty or enforce a remedy available for violations of this Act.

American Freedom Agenda Act of 2007 - Repeals the Military Commissions Act of 2006, authorizes the President to establish military commissions for the trial of war crimes only in places of active hostilities against the United States, and prohibits the President from detaining any individual indefinitely as an enemy combatant absent substantial evidence that the individual has engaged in active hostilities against the United States, provided no U.S. citizen shall be detained as an enemy combatant.

Prohibits any federal agency from gathering foreign intelligence in contravention of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.

Declares that no federal tribunal shall admit as evidence statements extracted from the defendant by torture or coercion.

Prohibits any federal officer or agent from kidnapping, imprisoning, or torturing any person abroad based solely on the President's belief that the subject of the kidnapping, imprisonment, or torture is a criminal or enemy combatant, provided that kidnapping is permitted if undertaken with the intent of bringing the kidnapped person for prosecution or interrogation to gather intelligence before a tribunal that meets international standards of fairness and due process.

Defines "criminal law" to mean the law that imposes penalties for crimes against the United States or against the nation

Creating Opportunities for Military Members to Use Transportation Efficiently Act of 2014 or the COMMUTE Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Defense (DOD), acting through the Director of the Office of Economic Adjustment, to establish a Military Community Infrastructure Program under which the Secretary may provide grants to eligible entities for transportation infrastructure improvement projects in military communities.  Grants may be used for: (1) the construction of roads, the construction of mass transit and parking facilities, the construction of, or upgrades to, pedestrian access and bicycle access, and the upgrades to public transportation systems; and (2) the construction of, or upgrades to, pedestrian and bicyclist access and bicycle access improvements.  Grants may be used to: (1) improve access to a military installation, and (2) address transportation problems caused by military installation growth. Directs the Secretary to conduct a traffic impact study for any urbanized area that expects a significant increase in traffic related to a military installation.

Amends the San Luis Rey Indian Water Rights Settlement Act to revise the conditions under which the Secretary of the Interior shall arrange for the development of supplemental water supply (by an amount not more than 16,000 acre-feet per year) for the benefit of the San Luis Rey Indian Water Authority and the local entities. 
Requires the Secretary to provide for the development of at least 16,000 acre-feet of supplemental water from public lands within the boundaries of California outside the service area of the Central Valley Project.

Broadband Internet Regulatory Relief Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit an incumbent local exchange carrier from being subject to requirements for facilities and equipment used exclusively to provide advanced service. 
Provides for pricing flexibility and for the availability of alternative service providers. 
Prohibits the Commission from subjecting an incumbent local exchange carrier to requirements for the provision of advanced service, in any State in which 70 percent of the carrier's loops in its service territory are DSL-capable, as determined by that State. 
Provides that the rates, terms, and conditions of any advanced service by an incumbent local exchange carrier shall not be subject to regulation if the Commission determines that advanced service is being offered by an unaffiliated provider in competition with the incumbent local exchange carrier within a geographic area served by a central office. 
Provides that the rates, terms, and conditions of advanced service offered by an incumbent local exchange carrier or its affiliate are not subject to regulation in any geographic area in which that carrier, its successor, or assigns was not the local incumbent exchange carrier on February 8, 1996.

Protecting Domestic Violence and Stalking Victims Act This bill amends the federal criminal code to expand the definition of "immediate partner" to include a dating partner or former dating partner. It also expands the exceptions to the prohibition against possessing or receiving a firearm from an intimate partner or child.

Insider Trading Prohibition Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to make it unlawful for a person to purchase, sell, or enter into, any security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement while in possession of material, nonpublic information relating to such security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement if such person knows or recklessly disregards that such information has been obtained wrongfully, or that such purchase, sale, or entry would constitute a wrongful use of such information.

Makes it unlawful for any person whose own purchase or sale of a security, security-based swap, or entry into a security-based swap agreement would violate this Act: (1) the other person who purchases, sells, or causes the purchase or sale of any security or security-based swap or entry into a security-based swap agreement to any other person; (2) to communicate the information to another person who makes or causes such a purchase, sale, or entry while in possession of such information; and (3) to make or cause such a purchase, sale, or entry while in possession of such information if the other person or the other person's communication is reasonably foreseeable.

Desalination Energy Consumption Reduction Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to make incentive payments to the owners of qualified desalination facilities to encourage the utilization of the best available technology to reduce the consumption of electrical energy in the desalination process.

Prohibits the Secretary from making any payment to the facility owner or operator under this Act unless, within fiscal year 2018, the Secretary enters into a written agreement with the owner or operator to make such payment.

Sets forth payment periods.

Requires the Secretary to establish a formula for making incentive payments to owners of qualified desalination facilities producing potable water from source waters ranging from 1,000 to 35,000 milligrams per liter total dissolved solids or more.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to any application for a project that: (1) uses innovative technologies to reduce the energy demand of the project; (2) uses renewable energy supplies in the desalination process; (3) provides regional water supply benefits; (4) provides a secure source of new water supplies for national defense activities; (5) reduces the threat of a water supply disruption as a result of a natural disaster or acts of terrorism; (6) uses technologies that minimize

Customs Training Enhancement Act - Directs the Commissioner of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to establish and carry out educational seminars at U.S. ports of entry to improve the ability of CBP and CBI Customs and Border Protection personnel to classify and appraise articles imported into the United States in accordance with U.S. customs laws, including to improve the ability of CBP and CBI personnel to identify and prevent the mislabeling and transshipment of articles.  Authorizes the Commissioner to establish and carry out fewer than 15 such seminars each year.  Requires the instruction and related instructional materials at each such seminar to be subject to the approval of the Commissioner.  Directs the Commissioner to establish a process to solicit, evaluate, and select interested parties for providing instruction in such seminars.

Seeds for the Future Act - Amends the Competitive, Special, and Facilities Research Grant Act to require the Secretary of Agriculture to ensure that not less than $50 million is used for competitive research grants that support the development of public cultivars.

Amends the Department of Agriculture Reorganization Act of 1994 to direct the Under Secretary of Agriculture for Public Culture and Research to appoint a coordinator within the Research, Education, and Extension Office that reports to coordinate research activities at the Department relating to the breeding of public cultivars.

Requires the coordinator to: (1) coordinate plant breeding research activities funded by the Department relating to the development of public cultivars; (2) develop a strategic plan that establishes targets for public cultivar research investments across the Department to ensure that a diverse range of crop needs are being met in a timely and transparent manner; (3) convene a working group to carry out such coordination functions comprised of individuals responsible for the management, administration, or analysis of public breeding programs within the Department from individuals who are responsible for the management, administration, or analysis of public breeding programs from genetic resource conservation centers, land-grant colleges and universities, Hispanic-serving institutions, Native American-serving nongovernmental organizations, public and private plant breeders

Patient Access to Durable Medical Equipment Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to extend the transition period from June 30, 2016, to June 30, 2017, under the Medicare program for durable medical equipment (DME) furnished to patients. (DME is a medical equipment that is not compatible with current Medicare payment plans and is intended to be used for long-term care services.) HHS must extend the transition period from June 30, 2016, to June 30, 2017, under the Medicare program for DME furnished to patients. HHS must also: (1) solicit and take into account stakeholder input, and (2) take into account the highest bidder bid by a winning supplier in a competitive acquisition area and a comparison of each of the following with respect to non-competitive acquisition areas and competitive acquisition areas. HHS must report on the results of the monitoring of access of Medicare beneficiaries to durable medical equipment and of health outcomes for DME. Organic Farmer and Consumer Protection Act of 2017 This bill amends the Organic Foods Production Act of 1990 to authorize appropriations for the National Organic Program (NOPP) for FY2018-FY2023.  The bill also amends the Act to direct the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to modernize international trade tracking and data collection systems of the NOPP.  The bill also amends the Act to authorize the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to share confidential business information with federal and state government officers and employees and certifying agents involved in the NOPP.  The bill authorizes the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to issue regulations to limit the types of operations excluded from certification under NOPP and any other specified regulations.  The bill requires USDA to: (1) have oversight and approval authority over any NOPP certifying agent operating in a foreign country, and (2) require an annual authorization for each agent that intends to operate in any foreign country.

Survivor Benefits Improvement Act of 2013 - Amends federal veterans' benefits provisions to extend the initial period for increasing dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses of former service members who remarry after age 55. Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide to any surviving spouse of a veteran who has remarried after age 55 the health care, vocational training, and rehabilitation, and monetary assistance to help pay for such care and treatment to which such spouse is entitled under the veterans' benefits program. Allows the Secretary to provide to any surviving spouse of a veteran who has remarried after age 55 the same benefits and assistance as a surviving spouse of a veteran who has remarried before age 55. Directs the Secretary to carry out a pilot program at a specified number of Veterans Health Administration (VHA) facilities to assess the feasibility and advisability of providing grief counseling services in group retreat settings to surviving spouses of veterans who die while serving on active duty.

Veterans Tobacco Trust Fund Act of 1998 - Establishes in the Treasury the Veterans Tobacco Trust Fund to be credited to the Fund from amounts received by the United States pursuant to a law enacted to allocate funds for programs to reduce use of tobacco products by minors and for health-care research, rehabilitation, and health systems research.

Medicaid Directory of Caregivers Act or the Medicaid DOC Act This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require states to update their medical assistance plans on an annual basis. A provider is: (1) in the case of a provider of a provider type for which the state agency requires the enrollment of the provider with the state agency, a provider that is enrolled under the state plan as of the date on which the directory is published or updated (as applicable) under this bill, and (2) in the case of a provider of a provider type for which the state agency does not require such enrollment, a provider that received payment under the state plan in the 12-month period preceding the date on which the directory is published or updated (as applicable) under this bill.  A provider is an individual who is an Indian or an Alaska Native.

Fluke Fairness Act of 2013 - Directs the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (themselves of the Mid-Atlantic Fishery Management Council) to submit to the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of the Interior a modified fishery management plan for the commercial and recreational management of summer flounder under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act. Requires the plan to be based on the best scientific information available, reflects changes in the distribution, abundance, and location of summer flounder in establishing distribution of the commercial and recreational catch quotas, considers regional, coastwide, or other management measures for summer flounder that comply with the National Standards, and prohibits the allocation of commercial or recreational catch quotas for summer flounder on a state-by-state basis using historical landings data that does not reflect the status of the summer flounder stock, based on the most recent scientific information. Directs the Comptroller General to submit to Congress an assessment of whether the modified plan or amendment implemented by the Commission complies with the National Standards.

Ending Maternal Mortality Act of 2018 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop and submit to Congress a national plan to reduce the rate of preventable maternal mortality. The plan must include: (1) a list of objectives for meeting the goals, and (2) a strategy for implementing the plan across HHS agencies and offices. The Department must also address specific issues, including: (1) increasing public understanding of maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity, (2) improving public understanding of the root causes of maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity, (3) improving data collection, (4) identifying at-risk populations, (5) supporting and expanding maternal mortality review committees, (6) assessing hospital culture of safety in maternity care, (7) improving health and treatment services for expectant mothers struggling with substance use and mental health disorders, (8) studying and supporting local and targeted responses to maternal death, and (9) identifying federal programs and activities to reduce maternal mortality. HHS must make each plan publicly accessible on the HHS website.

Backcountry Landing Strip Access Act - Prohibits the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture from taking any action that would permanently close, restrict, or render or declare unserviceable any aircraft landing strip located on federal land under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior or the Department of Agriculture (USDA).

Directs the Secretaries to jointly establish a national policy for governing backcountry aviation issues relating to the management of federal land under their respective jurisdictions and to require officials with jurisdiction over such land to adhere to such policy.

Requires any such policy to: (1) acknowledge that the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has the sole authority to control aviation and airspace over the United States; and (2) be developed after seeking and considering comments from state and other interested parties.

Requires the Secretaries to consult with the head of the aviation department of each state in which an aircraft landing strip is located and to ensure that such land is maintained in a manner consistent with the resource values of any adjacent area.

Prohibits the federal government from acquiring private or public property on which an aircraft landing strip is located and requires the federal government to acquire such land for unrestricted use.

Medicare and Medicaid Hospital Self-Referral Amendments of 1996 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require the discharge plan to specify or otherwise limit the qualified provider that may provide post-hospital care and to identify any such provider in which the hospital has a disclosable financial interest or in which the hospital has such an interest in providing medical assistance under Medicare. 
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to make such information available to the public.

Veterans Acquiring Community Care Expect Safe Services Act of 2017 or the Veterans ACCESS Act (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to deny or revoke a health care provider's eligibility to provide non-VA health care services to veterans if the provider: (1) was removed from employment with the VA due to conduct that violated a policy relating to the delivery of safe and appropriate health care; (2) violated the requirements of a medical license of the provider; (3) had a VA credential revoked and the grounds for such revocation impacts the ability of the provider to deliver safe and appropriate health care; or (4) violated a law for which a term of imprisonment of more than one year may be imposed.  The VA may deny, revoke, or suspend the eligibility of a health care provider to provide non-VA health care services to veterans if the provider: (1) is under investigation by the medical licensing board of a state in which the health care provider is licensed or practices, or (2) has entered into a settlement agreement for a disciplinary charge relating to the practice of medicine by the health care provider. Scenic Columbia Gorge Restoration Act of 2017 This bill directs the Department of Agriculture (USDA), acting through the Chief of the Forest Service, to begin proposing response activities for National Scenic Area (NSCA) lands adversely impacted by a catastrophic event. USDA shall allow 30 days for public scoping and comment regarding a NSCA response activity, 15 days for filing an objection to such response, and 15 days for the agency's response to the filing of an objection. Upon completion of this process and expiration of the period specified in this section, USDA shall implement the response activity.  The NSCA response activities shall be completed within 60 days after the catastrophic event conclusion.  The bill prohibits consultation for a response activity that: (1) does not exceed 10,000 acres within the NSCA; and (2) includes lands that are part of a municipal watershed or contain utility or power transmission right-of-ways.  The bill requires consultation under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 for a response activity that is not likely to adversely affect a listed species or designated critical habitat.  The bill prohibits restraining orders, preliminary injunctions, and injunctions pending appeal

Treatment of Indian Tribal Natural Resource Income Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from Federal income tax income derived from a natural resources-related activity by Indians: (1) any extraction of minerals, ores, oil, or gas; and (2) any remuneration paid for services performed in such activities by one member of a tribe for another member of such tribe or for a qualified Indian entity.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) require the appointment of a Commissioner of Internal Revenue to the position of Commissioner of Internal Revenue to be made by the President from individuals recommended by the Selection Commission; and (2) provide for a minimum of three recommended individuals.

Terminates the Commission 6 years after the date on which an individual recommended by the Commission is sworn in as Commissioner of Internal Revenue.

Government Audit Reform Act of 2010 - Expresses the sense of Congress that the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) should follow the recommendations of the Government Accountability Office (GAO) report "Single Audit: Opportunities Exist to Improve the Single Audit Process and Oversight," issued March 13, 2009.

Requires the Director, or the head of the office or entity designated by the Director, to: (1) monitor the risk, cost-benefit, efficiency, and effectiveness of the implementation by federal agencies of this Act; and (2) report to Congress on the findings of the GAO report and the resources necessary to improve such implementation.

Directs the Director to: (1) evaluate the process for the single audit and the program-specific audit to identify simplified alternatives for achieving the purposes of the Single Audit Act of 1984 (PAYDA) and the Single Audit Act Amendments of 1996 for audits of small recipients that also achieve the proper balance between risk and cost-effective accountability for small and large recipients; and (2) report to Congress on the results of such evaluation.

Amends the Truth in Lending Act to provide that, in the event of the death of a borrower of a private educational loan, or of a veteran whose disability renders such loan inapplicable, neither the estate of the borrower nor any cosigner of such loan shall be obligated to repay the outstanding principal or interest on the loan.
Authorizes the Director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to promulgate regulations to reinstate the obligation of such loans in any case in which the Director determines necessary to protect the public interest.

Critical Infrastructure Protection Act or CIPA (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to include in national planning scenarios the threat of electromagnetic pulse (EMP) events. In furtherance of domestic preparedness and response, DHS must conduct research and development to mitigate the consequences of EMP events.  The bill also requires DHS to conduct research and development to mitigate the consequences of EMP events.  The bill limits the scope of research and development to: (1) an objective scientific analysis of the risks to critical infrastructures from a range of EMP events; (2) an objective scientific analysis of the risks to critical infrastructures from a specific range of EMP events; (3) an evaluation of emergency planning and response technologies that would address the findings and recommendations of experts, including those of the Commission to Assess the Threat to the United States from Electromagnetic Pulse Attack (EMPulseAtt); and (4) an analysis of technology options that are available to improve the resiliency of critical infrastructure to EMP.  DHS must submit a recommended strategy to Congress and biennial updates on the status of the recommended strategy.  DHS must report to Congress on progress made

Professional's Access to Health Workforce Integration Act of 2015 This bill authorizes the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities, or the Office of Minority Health, to award grants to eligible entities to carry out activities related to health professional employment and education.  Health professionals are individuals trained for employment or intended employment in the field of public health, health management, dentistry, health administration, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, psychology, social work, psychiatry, other mental and behavioral health, allied health, community health or wellness work, including fitness and nutrition, or other fields as determined appropriate by HHS and the Department of Health and Human Services.  Such grants may be used to: (1) assist skilled immigrants entering the American health workforce with employment matching their health professional skills and education, and (2) educate employers regarding the abilities andcapacities of internationally educated health professionals.

Veterans Benefits Administration Improvement Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit to the congressional veterans' committees a comprehensive plan for the improvement of the processing of veterans compensation and pension claims. Requires the Secretary to implement such plan by 60 days after the submittal of the plan to the committees.

Healthy Schools Partnerships Act of 2010 - Amends the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a demonstration project to award grants to eligible entities to fund collaborations of academic experts, nonprofit organizations, registered dietitians or other nutrition professionals, community partners, and local schools to test and evaluate innovative models to improve nutrition education, student decisionmaking, and healthy school environments.

Gives grant priority to entities that demonstrate: (1) a severe need to improve the school environment, (2) a commitment by community partners to make in-kind or cash contributions, and (3) the ability to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention.

Small Business Investment Improvement Act of 1999 - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to revise the Small Business Investment Program (SBIP) to include interest as a mandatory interest payment amount. 
Revises the definition of "interest" for purposes of the SBIP to include only the maximum mandatory sum, expressed in dollars or as a percentage rate, that is payable with respect to the business loan amount received by the small business, and does not include the value, if any, of contingent obligations, including warrants, royalty, or conversion rights, granting the small business investment company an ownership interest in the equity or increased future revenue of the small business receiving the business loan. 
Revises the definition of "small business concern" to include a small business that is not required by law to pay Federal income taxes at the enterprise level and is required to pass income through to the shareholders, partners, beneficiaries, or other equitable owners of the business. 
Revises the definition of "small business concern" for purposes of the SBIP to exclude a small business that is not required by law to pay State (and local, if any) income taxes at the enterprise level and is required to pass income through to the shareholders, partners,

Pro-Growth Budgeting Act of 2012 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to prepare for each major legislation reported by any congressional committee, as a supplement to estimates prepared under the Congressional Budget Projections Act, a macroeconomic impact analysis of the budgetary effects of such legislation for the ten fiscal-year period beginning with the first fiscal year for which an estimate was prepared under the Act and each of the next three subsequent fiscal-year periods.

Requires the CBO to submit to such committees a macroeconomic impact analysis of the budgetary effects of the legislation for the preceding fiscal year, the preceding fiscal year, the preceding fiscal year, and the ensuing fiscal year.

Requires the CBO to submit to such committees a supplemental projection assuming extension of current tax policy for the fiscal year commencing on October 1 of that year with a supplemental projection for the 10 fiscal-year period beginning with that fiscal year, assuming the extension of current tax policy.

Federal Land Freedom Act of 2015 This bill authorizes a state to lease, permit, and regulate the exploration and development of oil, gas, and other forms of energy on federal land located in the state in lieu of the federal government.  Any action by a state to lease, permit, or regulate the exploration and development of oil, gas, and other forms of energy pursuant to this bill shall not be considered a federal action, federal permit, or federal license under the Administrative Procedure Act, the National Historic Preservation Act, the Endangered Species Act of 1973, or the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969.  Any lease or permit issued by a state pursuant to this bill shall include provisions for the collection of royalties or revenues in an amount equal to the amount of royalties or revenues that would have been collected if the lease or permit had been issued by the federal government.  Any revenues collected by a state from leasing or permitting on federal land pursuant to this bill shall be deposited in the same federal account in which the revenues would have been deposited if the lease or permit had been issued by the federal government.

Pink Tax Repeal Act - Prohibits any person from selling or offering for sale in interstate commerce any two consumer products from the same manufacturer that are substantially similar if the products are priced differently based on the gender of the individuals for whose use the products are intended or marketed.

Defines "consumer product" with respect to this Act as a device or cosmetics, as defined under the Consumer Product Safety Act, including a child restraint system, as defined under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act - Allows an employee of a land management agency serving under a time-limited appointment in the competitive service to compete for a permanent appointment in the agency's merit promotion procedures if: (1) the employee was appointed initially under open, competitive examination to the time-limited appointment; (2) the employee has served under one or more time-limited appointments for a period or periods totaling not less than 24 months without an intervening break of two or more years; and (3) the employee's performance has been at an acceptable level throughout the period or periods (as the case may be) referred to in this Act.

Requires such an employee to be offered any successor permanent position that the agency decides to fill and, upon his or her concurrence, appointed to such position if: (1) such individual was appointed initially under open, competitive examination to the time-limited appointment; (2) the job announcement for the time-limited position stated that there was potential for the position to become permanent or that the employee's first time-limited appointment by such agency occurred before the date of enactment of this Act; and (3) the employee has served under a time-limited appointment or appointments in a position or positions in such

Amends the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act of 1986 and the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 to require facilities operating on National Priorities List activities to notify the appropriate agencies within one hour of having knowledge of a release of a hazardous substance from such facility.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that if a common trust fund transfers substantially all of its assets to one or more regulated investment companies in exchange solely for stock in the company or companies to which such assets are so transferred, and such stock is distributed by such common trust fund to participants in such common trust fund in exchange solely for their interests in such company, no gain or loss shall be recognized by the common trust fund, and no gain or loss shall be recognized by any participant in such common trust fund, under any exchange.  Requires the basis of any asset received by a regulated investment company in such a transfer to be the same as that of the property exchanged. 
Requires the assumption by any such company of liability and the fact that any property transferred by the common trust fund is subject to liability to be disregarded. 
Requires the common trust fund to meet diversification rules.

Nuclear Power Plant Safety Act of 2011 - Amends the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to direct the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to initiate a rulemaking proceeding to revise its regulations to ensure that each utilization facility licensed under such Act can withstand and adequately respond to: (1) an earthquake, tsunami (for a facility located in a coastal area), strong storm, or other event that threatens a major impact to the facility; (2) a loss of the primary operating power source for at least 14 days; and (3) a loss of the primary backup operating power source for at least 72 hours.

Requires the NRC to ensure that the cost of the obligation for a nuclear energy facility loan guarantee is calculated using a consideration of the Tohoku earthquake of 2011 to estimate the risk characteristics of the project.

Peer Support Communities of Recovery Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to allow a federal grant to a national nonprofit entity that: (1) is focused on substance use disorder with a network of local affiliates and partners that are geographically and organizationally diverse, or (2) is established by individuals in personal or family recovery and serving prevention, treatment, recovery, payor, faith-based, and criminal justice stakeholders in the implementation of local addiction and recovery initiatives.  Recovery community organizations are eligible for grants to: (1) build infrastructure to carry out the activities described in this Act, and (2) establish regional technical assistance centers to provide regional technical assistance for implementation of such activities.  The bill also authorizes a nonprofit organization to award grants to eligible entities to establish regional technical assistance centers to provide regional technical assistance for implementation of the following: (1) implementation of regionally driven, peer-delivered addiction recovery support services before, during, after, or in conjunction with addiction treatment, and (2) establishment of recovery community organizations.  The bill also authorizes a nonprofit organization to award grants to eligible entities to establish regional technical assistance centers to provide regional technical assistance for the establishment of recovery community centers. Child Care Criminal Background Check Act of 2009 - Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to require a State to require child care providers that are licensed by the State or that receive funds under the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to obtain a comprehensive criminal background check of each employee who provides child care services, each applicant for employment to provide such services, and each family child care provider who provides or applies to provide such services.

Requires the State to carry out a comprehensive criminal background check of each employee of, and each applicant for employment by, a child care provider that is licensed by the State or receives funds under the Act by the State's request.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to reduce by 10% the State allotment for the fiscal year following the fiscal year with respect to which noncompliance is found.

Volunteer Emergency Services Recruitment and Retention Act of 2006 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from the definition of "eligible deferred compensation plan" any length of service award plan that is an employer-provided benefit plan for a volunteer who has performed a bona fide volunteer service on account of qualified services.

Medicaid Reform and Personal Responsibility Act of 2017 This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require states to apply a work requirement for able-bodied adults without dependents (i.e., a work requirement and a work requirement) to an able-bodied adult who otherwise would be eligible for Medicaid.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Commerce to develop and implement a comprehensive program for fish screens, fish passage devices, and other measures agreed to by local interests and relevant Federal agencies for water diversions by local governmental entities in Oregon, Washington, Montana, and Idaho that provide water supplies.

Randy Barrett Act - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to direct the Commissioner of Social Security to waive the five-month waiting period for entitlement to benefits based on disability in cases in which an individual is terminally ill and is not entitled to widow's insurance benefits under OASDI.

DMZ War Veterans Recognition Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service (NPS), to place a plaque in the Korean War Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., at the graves of those soldiers who served, were wounded, or were killed from 1953 until the present in the defense of the Republic of Korea, that contains the following inscription: (1) Dedicated to the soldiers of the United States and the Republic of Korea who served, were wounded, or were killed from 1953 until the present in the defense of the Republic of Korea.

Requires the inscription to include the date on which the plaque is placed.

Makes this Act a public service achievement for the Republic of Korea.

Hydrographic Services Improvement Act Amendments of 2008 - Amends the Hydrographic Services Improvement Act of 1998 to revise the duties of the Coast and Geodetic Survey (CGS) to include the acquisition, interpretation, certification, and dissemination of bathymetric, hydrogeographic, and coastal and ocean-related surveying data, including the production of nautical charts, nautical information databases, and other products derived from hydrographic data.

Authorizes the Administrator of the CGS to create, support, and maintain a Joint Hydrographic Institute.

Authorizes the Administrator to acquire hydrographic data and provide hydrographic services to: (1) support the conservation and management of coastal and ocean resources; (2) save and protect life and property; (3) support the resumption of commerce in response to emergencies, natural disasters, and man-made disasters; and (4) meet homeland security and maritime domain awareness needs.

Authorizes the Administrator to contract for hydrographic surveys and operate hydrographic survey vessels.

Authorizes appropriations.

Community Gardening and Nutrition Act of 2014 - Amends the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973 to require the Director of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a Community Garden Pilot Program to carry out the work described in this Act. Directs the Director to give priority to: (1) volunteers with experience in health, nutrition, and gardening; (2) projects located in varied geographic regions; and (3) selecting a balance of urban and rural projects. Authorizes appropriations for FY2014.

Federal Internship Improvement Act - Requires the head of each executive agency to appoint an internship coordinator within the agency to serve as an internship coordinator.

Requires the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to make publicly available on the Internet: (1) the name and contact information of the coordinator for each agency; and (2) information regarding application procedures and deadlines for each internship program.
