Requires the agency operating an internship program to conduct an exit interview and administer a survey (which shall be in conformity with OPM's guidelines to ensure uniformity across agencies) with each intern who completes the program.

Requires the head of each agency operating an internship program to annually submit to OPM a report assessing the internship program.

Concussion Treatment and Care Tools Act of 2010 or the ConTACT Act of 2010 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), after a specified date, to establish concussion management guidelines that address the prevention, identification, treatment, and management of concussions in school-aged children.

Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to states to assist in the establishment of such guidelines.

Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to states to assist in the establishment of such guidelines after establishing such guidelines.

Requires the Secretary to convene a conference of medical, athletic, and educational stakeholders to assist in the establishment of such guidelines.

Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to states to assist in the establishment of such guidelines after establishing such guidelines.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) submit to Congress a report on the implementation of such guidelines; and (2) submit to Congress a report on the implementation of such guidelines, including the number of states that have adopted the guidelines, the number of target entities that have implemented preseason baseline and post-injury testing for school-aged children, and the data collected with respect to the incidence of concussions and

Hunter and Farmer Protection Act of 2015 This bill amends the Migratory Bird Treaty Act to define "baiting" as the direct or indirect placing, exposing, depositing, distributing, or scattering of salt, grain, or other feed that could lure or attract migratory game birds to, on, or over any areas on which a hunter is attempting to take migratory game birds.  A "baiting" area is any area on which a hunter is attempting to take migratory game birds, including waterfowl, that has been treated with a normal agricultural practice, has standing crops that have not been manipulated, or has standing crops that have been or are flooded.  A "normal agricultural practice" is any practice in one annual growing season that: (1) is carried out in order to produce a marketable crop, including planting, harvest, post-harvest, or soil conservation practices; and (2) is recommended for the successful harvest of a given crop by the applicable state office of the Cooperative Extension System.

International Money Transfer Disclosure Act - Requires any financial institution or money transmitting business which initiates an international money transfer on behalf of a consumer to provide the consumer with: (1) any fees to be charged to the recipient, including any exchange rate or currency conversion fees; (2) a final itemization of all costs to the consumer, which would include all fees charged, for the remittance; and (3) the exact amount of foreign currency to be received by the recipient in the foreign country.

Requires the disclosures to be in English and in the same language as the language principally used by the financial institution or money transmitting business, or any of its agents, to advertise, solicit, or negotiate at the office of the institution or business at which the international money transfer is initiated.

Requires the disclosures to be in English and in the same language, if other than English, as the language principally used by the financial institution or money transmitting business, or any of its agents, to advertise, solicit, or negotiate at the office of the institution or business at which the international money transfer is initiated.

Requires the appropriate federal banking agency and the Federal Trade Commission to enforce such requirements.

Mental Health First Act of 2013 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), acting through the Administrator of the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, to award grants to states, political subdivisions, Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and nonprofit private entities to initiate and sustain mental health first aid training programs. Requires such training to: (1) be designed to train individuals to assist in crisis situations; (2) ensure that training is conducted by qualified and credentialed trainers; and (3) include at a minimum, a core live training course on the skills, resources, and knowledge to assist individuals in crisis to connect with appropriate local mental health care services, training on mental health resources, and action plans and protocols for referral to such resources; and (4) where feasible, continuing education and updated training for individuals in such skills and resources. Requires the training to be designed to train individuals to: (1) recognize the signs and symptoms of mental illness, including such common psychiatric conditions as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major clinical depression, and anxiety disorders; and (2) be able to immediately refer to mental health services in the early stages of developing mental disorders in order to avoid costly behavioral health care

Mandate Prevention Act of 2010 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require legislation that increases the direct costs of federal private sector mandates by an amount that causes such costs to exceed specified thresholds to: (1) provide new budget authority or new entitlement authority in the House of Representatives or direct spending authority in the Senate for each fiscal year for such mandates included in the legislation joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report; or (2) include an authorization for appropriations in an amount equal to or exceeding such direct costs and identify a specific dollar amount of such costs for each year up to 10 years during which such mandate shall be in effect, and report on the determination of whether there are insufficient appropriations for such fiscal year.

Requires any legislation that increases the direct costs of federal private sector mandates by an amount that causes such costs to exceed specified thresholds to: (1) provide for federal funding of such costs for any fiscal year; and (2) identify any appropriation bill that is expected to provide for federal funding of such costs and that provides for expedited procedures for the consideration of such statement or legislative recommendations.

Free File Act of 2016 This bill directs the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to continue to operate the IRS Free File Program as established by the Internal Revenue Service and published in the Federal Register on November 4, 2002, including any subsequent agreements and governing rules.  The IRS shall continue to provide free commercial-type online individual income tax preparation and electronic filing services to the lowest 70% of taxpayers by income. The IRS shall continue to work with the private sector through the IRS Free File Program to implement innovative new program features to improve and simplify the taxpayer's experience with completing and filing individual income tax returns in voluntary compliance. Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to use from receipts from the sale of migratory bird hunting and conservation stamps an amount not to exceed $1 million for each of FY 1999 through 2003 for the promotion of additional stamp sales.

Renewable Energy Investment Act of 2009 - Title I: Investment in Renewable Energy - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) extend through 2014 the renewable electricity production tax credit; (2) extend through 2015 the new clean renewable energy bonds; (3) extend through 2019 the investment tax credit for alcohol fuels; (4) extend through 2019 the credit for biodiesel and renewable diesel; (5) extend through 2019 the credit for clean energy property; (6) extend through 2019 the credit for investment in advanced energy facilities; and (7) extend through 2019 the credit for fungible biofuels.

Title II: Investment in Alternative Fuels - Amends the American Recovery and Reinvestment Tax Act of 2009 to extend through 2019 the tax credit for investment in advanced biofuels and the investment tax credit for biodiesel and renewable diesel.

Title III: Investment in Alternative Fuels - Authorizes appropriations for advanced biofuels research, development, and demonstration.

National Reconstruction Study Area Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service, to complete a study of the area comprised of historical sites in the historic district of Beaufort, South Carolina, relating to the Reconstruction Era.

Requires the Secretary to report to specified congressional committees describing the findings of the study and any conclusions and recommendations of the Secretary.

Directs the Attorney General to provide for the granting of posthumous citizenship to a person who died as a result of an injury incurred in the following events:  (1) the hijacking of American Airlines Flight 11 on September 11, 2001; (2) the crash of that aircraft into the World Trade Center in New York, New York; (3) the hijacking of United Airlines Flight 175 on such date, the crash of that aircraft into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia; and (4) the hijacking of United Airlines Flight 93 on such date, and the crash of that aircraft in Stony Creek Township, Pennsylvania. 
Requires the Attorney General to provide for the granting of posthumous citizenship to a person who died as a result of an injury incurred in the following events:  (1) the hijacking of American Airlines Flight 11 on September 11, 2001; (2) the crash of that aircraft into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia; and (3) the hijacking of United Airlines Flight 175 on such date, the crash of that aircraft into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, and the subsequent destruction that resulted.

Strengthening Background Checks Act of 2013 - Amends the NICS Improvement Amendments Act of 2007 to direct the Attorney General (DOJ) to withhold 10% of the amount that would otherwise be allocated to a state under the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (OCSLA) if the state fails to comply with certain requirements of the Act, including an inability to comply due to court order or other legal restriction. Authorizes the Attorney General to waive such requirement for one year if the state provides substantial evidence that the state is making a reasonable effort to comply with such requirements. Requires the state to provide to the Attorney General, for each fiscal year after the expiration of such period, at least 90% of the required records. Requires the state to implement such requirements in the same manner as requirements under OCSLA. Authorizes appropriations for the NICS Improvement Amendments Act of 2007 for FY2012-FY2015.

Freedom to Fish Act - Amends the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act to prohibit any fishery management plan prepared by a Regional Fishery Management Council from establishing areas closed to recreational fishing unless: (1) there is a clear indication that recreational fishermen are the cause of a specific conservation problem and that less severe conservation measures will not adequately provide for conservation and management of the affected stocks of fish; (2) the closed area regulation includes specific measurable criteria to determine the conservation benefit of the closed area on such fish and provides a timetable for periodic review of the continued need for the closed area; (3) the closed area is no larger than that which is supported by the best available scientific information; or (4) provision is made to reopen the closed area to recreational fishing whenever the condition in such area that was the basis of the closure no longer exists.

Amends the National Marine Sanctuaries Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior to provide the appropriate Regional Fishery Management Council with the opportunity to propose and revise all regulations applicable to fishing within designated marine sanctuaries according to the standards and procedures of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act.

State Court Interpreter Grant Program Act - Directs the Administrator of the Office of Justice Programs of the Department of Justice to make grants to States to develop and implement programs to assist individuals with limited English proficiency to access and understand State court proceedings in which they are a party.

Authorizes appropriations.

The bill also defines "chronically dependent individual" as an individual who: (1) is dependent on a daily basis on verbal reminding, physical cueing, supervision, or other assistance provided to the individual by another person in the performance of at least two of the activities of daily living, and (2) without such assistance, could

Sexual Assault Prosecution Act of 2002 - Amends the Federal criminal code to provide that an indictment for any offense committed in violation of federal criminal code provisions shall be open to the public.Requires the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to develop a plan to award voluntary awards to facilitate DNA analysis of all casework evidence of unsolved crimes.Directs the FBI, in coordination with the Assistant Attorney General of the Office of Justice Programs of the Department of Justice, to develop criteria for the granting of awards including: (1) the number of unsolved crimes awaiting DNA analysis in the state that is applying for an award; and (2) a comprehensive plan to collect and analyze DNA evidence by the state that is applying for an award.Requires the FBI to: (1) develop applications for awards to be granted to states; (2) consider all applications submitted by states; and (3) disburse all awards.Requires the state receiving awards to require that each laboratory performing DNA analysis meet quality assurance standards and utilize state-of-the-art DNA testing methods.

Over-the-Counter Hearing Aid Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require hearing aids to meet certain requirements, including that they use the same fundamental scientific technology as air conduction hearing aids or wireless air conduction hearing aids and that are intended to be used by adults over the age of 18 to compensate for perceived mild to moderate hearing impairment. The bill exempts hearing aids from certain requirements for prescription hearing aids, including those for hearing aids that use the same fundamental scientific technology as hearing aids or wireless air conduction hearing aids, or that use the same fundamental scientific technology as hearing aids or wireless air conduction hearing aids, but that are intended to be used by adults over the age of 18 to compensate for perceived mild to moderate hearing impairment. The bill also exempts hearing aids from certain requirements for consumer products, including requirements that they be available over-the-counter, without the supervision, prescription, or other order, involvement, or intervention of a licensed person, to consumers through in-person transactions, by mail, or online.

Red Cliffs Desert Reserve Completion Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to pay James Doyle, out of money not otherwise appropriated, a sum of money representing the amount to which Doyle may be entitled in order to make Doyle whole for any damages and losses sustained by Doyle by reason of the Federal Government's taking of approximately 2,000 acres of his land located in the St. George area of Utah, now designated as the Red Cliffs Desert Reserve and set aside as habitat for the Mojave desert tortoise, a species listed under the Endangered Species Act of 1973.

Teaching Children to Save Lives Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Education to carry out a program under which the Secretary is authorized to award grants to eligible local educational agencies or targeted schools for implementing nationally recognized CPR and AED training courses.

Authorizes local educational agencies or targeted schools to use the grant for: (1) training individuals in CPR and AED skills and instruction; (2) obtaining printed informational or instructional materials; (3) obtaining manikins; (4) obtaining AED training devices; and (5) obtaining other equipment as appropriate.

Requires local educational agencies or targeted schools to demonstrate to the Secretary that they have implemented or intend to implement an AED training program in conjunction with a CPR training program.

Directs the Secretary to award such grants based on: (1) demonstrated need for initiating a CPR or AED training program in a targeted school or community served by targeted schools; (2) demonstrated need for continued support of an existing training programs in targeted schools or communities served by targeted schools; (3) demonstrated need for expanding an existing training program by adding training in the use of an AED; and (4) opportunities to encourage and foster partnerships with and among community organizations to aid in

Comprehensive Problem Gambling Act of 2011 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to include in the National Priorities List programs for the prevention, treatment, and research of pathological and other problem gambling.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to carry out a national campaign to increase knowledge and raise awareness within the general public regarding problem gambling issues.

Authorizes the Secretary, acting through the Administrator, to: (1) coordinate the voluntary donation of, and administer, resources to assist in the implementation of new programs and the augmentation and support of existing national campaigns to provide national strategies for dissemination of information, intended to treat problem gambling; and (2) encourage media outlets to provide information aimed at preventing problem gambling.

Requires the Secretary to establish and implement a national program of research on problem gambling.

Requires the Secretary to develop a treatment improvement protocol specific to problem gambling.

Directs the Secretary, acting through the Administrator, to integrate problem gambling into existing alcohol, tobacco, and other drug prevention programs where practical.

Welfare Improvement Act of 1997 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to prohibit States from using any part of TANF grants for children born to families receiving TANF assistance.

Requires States to establish a program for randomly testing individuals for use of controlled substances.  Terminates assistance under the State TANF program for any individual who tests positive for the use of controlled substances.

Researchers and Farmers Freedom From Terrorism Act of 2000 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit animal enterprise terrorism. Provides for imprisonment for up to five years, or both, for a misdemeanor that results in the intentional damage or destruction of any building, vehicle, or other real or personal property used by an animal enterprise. Provides for enhanced penalties for animal enterprise terrorism, including a prison term of up to 20 years and a fine. Gun Victim Compensation Act - Amends the Federal criminal code to establish civil damages for bodily injury to or the death of a person caused by a transferred firearm.

Small Business Relief and Job Creation Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an eligible unemployed individual who begins work for an eligible small business during 2018 or 2019 to elect to treat such individual as a member of a targeted group for purposes of the work opportunity tax credit.  An "eligible unemployed individual" is any individual who: (1) is certified by the designated local agency as being eligible to receive unemployment compensation under state or federal law during the one-year period ending on the hiring date, or (2) whose employment with the employer was terminated before January 1, 2018.  The bill also modifies the work opportunity tax credit to allow a business-related tax credit for hiring 15 or more employees during 2018 and 2019.

Stop the Sale of Murderabilia Act of 2013 - Amends the federal criminal code to prohibit an inmate of a federal or state correctional, detention, or penal facility from mailing or delivering any property, article, or object with intent that it be placed in interstate or foreign commerce. Provides for a prison term of up to 6 months and a prison sentence of not less than 10 years for any term of imprisonment imposed under this Act. Provides for civil forfeiture of any real or personal property used to commit specified crimes.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to request the Institute of Medicine of the National Academy of Sciences to study the access of Medicare beneficiaries residing in the U.S.  territories to prescription drugs during specified periods before, during, and after the enactment of the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act of 2003.

Volunteer First Responder Housing Act - Makes a qualified volunteer first responder who submits to the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) a verification letter in accordance with this Act ineligible for a direct income tax deduction for the cost of up to $18,000 of the annual income tax deduction for the first responder's home.  Makes such a deduction available to the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the next door sales of homes in the Indian tribe.

Estate and Gift Tax Phase-Out Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to eliminate the estate and gift tax.  Repeals the federal transfer tax.

Common Sense Campaign Reform Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow individual taxpayers a tax credit for contributions to candidates for office in, or Delegates to, the Congress. 
Increases the maximum amount of such credit. 
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require a multicandidate political committee (PAC) to include in its annual report the name and address of the entity that establishes the PAC. 
Requires a separate segregated fund to include in its name any candidate it establishes.

Developing Resourcesmediately and Long-Term through Leases on Our Nation's Offshore Waters Act of 2009 or the DRILL NOW Act of 2009 - Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to repeal the President's authority to withdraw any lands of the outer Continental Shelf (OCS) from disposition for exploration, development, or production of oil and gas, except as the President determines necessary for national security purposes.

Authorizes the governor of a state to submit to the Secretary of the Interior a petition requesting that the Secretary issue leases authorizing the conduct of oil and gas exploration and extraction activities in any area within 50 miles of the coast of the state and within the lateral seaward boundaries of the state extended.

Federal Reserve Board Civil Rights Compliance Act of 1999 - Directs the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to post and keep posted in conspicuous places, upon its premises where such notices to employees and applicants for employment are customarily posted, a notice to be prepared or approved by the Board, and a notice to be prepared or approved by the Commission on Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System respecting the rights and procedures applicable to Board employees and applicants for employment by the Board.

Birthparent Assistance Act of 2008 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide certain services to birthparents who have placed a child for adoption, including: (1) post-legal adoption services; (2) individual, group, and family counseling; and (3) training of hospital staff relating to interaction of such staff with birthparents and adoptive families.

Animal Drug Amendments of 1994 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to exempt a new animal drug approved for human use from the requirements of this Act if the drug:  (1) is approved for use in animals; and (2) is in compliance with regulations that establish the conditions for such different use or intended use. 
Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to by general regulation:  (1) establish a safe level for residue of an animal drug used for such different authorized use; and (2) require the development of a practical analytical method for the detection of residues of the drug. 
Authorizes the Secretary to by order provide access to the records of veterinarians to ascertain any authorized use of the drug that the Secretary has determined may present a risk to the public health. 
Provides that, if the approval of an application is in effect, the drug shall not be deemed unsafe for purposes of this Act and shall be exempt from the requirements of this Act with respect to a use or intended use of the drug in animals if such use or intended use:  (1) is by or on the lawful written or oral order of a licensed veterinarian within the context of a veterinarian-client-patient

Role Models Academy Demonstration Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to establish a four-year, residential, military-style academy to serve as a model, residential, military-style magnet school for at-risk youth from around the Nation who cease to attend secondary school before graduation from secondary school.

Requires the Academy to: (1) offer at-risk youth secondary school coursework and vocational training; (2) focus on the education and vocational training of youth at risk of delinquency or dropping out of secondary school; (3) whose teachers are primarily composed of former members of the Armed Forces or participants in the program assisted under the Topsell Institute's Troops to Teachers Program; (4) operate a mentoring program that utilizes mentors from all sectors of society to serve as role models for Academy students; (5) may contain a Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps unit; (6) is housed on the site of any military installation closed pursuant to a base closure law; and (7) if the Academy is effective, that serves as a model for similar military-style academies throughout the United States.

Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) to authorize a state-chartered public entity health benefits pool (a risk pool) to apply to the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) for a pass-through of funding to cover health care benefits for individuals and small employers who would otherwise qualify for the Medicare Advantage health care benefit program.

Common Sense Nutrition Disclosure Act of 2012 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act to require that the number of calories contained in the standard menu item, as usually prepared and offered for sale, be disclosed in the case of restaurants or similar retail food establishments where the majority of orders are placed by customers who are off-premises at the time such order is placed.

Allows the use of a remote-access menu, such as one available on the internet, for such purposes.

Defines "reasonable basis" for a nutrient disclosure to mean that the disclosure is within acceptable allowances for variation in nutrient content.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require the Attorney General to ensure that numerical limitations on the issuance of the H-1B visa (short for temporary agricultural worker) for nonimmigrant status do not count against any such limitation.

Cell Phone Theft Prevention Act of 2012 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit a provider of commercial mobile service or commercial mobile data service from providing service on a mobile electronic device that has been reported to such provider as stolen: (1) by the person who holds the account with respect to such service, if such person submits a copy of a report made to a law enforcement agency regarding the theft, or by another provider of such service, in accordance with this Act.

Requires a provider of such service to inform all other providers of such service of such reported theft.

Requires a provider of such service to make available to the account holder the capability of deleting from the device, from a remote location, all information that was placed on the device after its manufacture.

Prohibits a person from manufacturing in the United States or importing into the United States for sale or resale to the public a mobile electronic device without such a device.

Requires a provider of such service to report to the FCC within one year of its effective date any progress made toward complying with such requirements.

American Elections Act of 2010 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit foreign principal and substantial foreign influence corporations from making contributions, donations, or expenditures in connection with a federal, state, or local election.

Requires such corporations to certify that they are in compliance with the Act.

Requires a corporation that is a beneficiary of a federal, state, or local election to report to the congressional election committees not later than 45 days after the election day the percentage of voting shares of the corporation controlled by a foreign national or, if no such shares exist, the percentage of gross receipts received from a foreign national in the immediately preceding fiscal year or the current pro-rated fiscal year.

Requires a corporation that is a beneficiary of a federal, state, or local election to report to the congressional election committees the percentage of funds from a foreign national that the corporation received from a foreign national.

Small Business Health Relief Act of 2011 - Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) to repeal: (1) the restriction on over-the-counter medicines, and (2) the annual cap on health savings accounts.

Repeals the requirement that a group health plan or health insurance coverage in which an individual is enrolled on or after March 23, 2010, but before any plan year beginning no later than one year after the enactment of this Act, and which is deemed to be a grandfathered health plan under PPACA, be considered a grandfathered health plan with respect to such individual regardless of any modification to the cost-sharing levels, employer contribution rates, or covered benefits under such plan or coverage as otherwise permitted under PPACA.

Genetic Fairness Act of 1996 - Prohibits an insurer offering a group health plan or a multiple employer welfare arrangement from:  (1) terminating, restricting, limiting, or otherwise applying conditions to coverage of an individual or family member under the plan; (2) requiring an enrollee to be the subject of a genetic test or subjected to questions relating to such test; (3) imposing a rider that excludes coverage for certain benefits or services under the plan; (4) establishing differentials in premium rates or cost sharing for coverage under the plan; or (5) otherwise discriminating against an individual or family member in the provision of health care. 
Requires an insurer offering a health plan to provide an enrollee with a written statement disclosing the rights of the enrollee under this Act. 
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to enforce the requirements established under this Act in the same manner as provided for under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). 
Provides for civil actions by persons in the State insurance commissioner's or the official or officials designated by the State against the insurer for violations of this Act.

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award grants to local educational agencies (LEAs) that have taken steps to improve their teachers' quality and raise their students' achievement.

Education Modernization Fund Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to make loans to states for the purpose of constructing and modernizing elementary and secondary schools.  Establishes the Education Modernization Fund in the Treasury.  Requires the Secretary to allocate funds to states for such loans.  Requires the Secretary to ensure that the formula provides for the allocation of funds to each eligible state. 
Directs the Secretary to transfer to the Fund an amount equal to $5 billion from the modernization fund.  Requires the Secretary to deposit all such transferred funds in the Fund.  Allows investments of such Fund to be made only in interest-bearing obligations of the United States or in obligations guaranteed by the United States. 
Extends the authorization of the issuance of the public debt. 
Requires the Secretary to sell any obligations held in the Fund. 
Requires the proceeds from the sale or redemption of such obligations to be used for making expenditures to carry out the Education Modernization Fund Act.

Derivatives and Hedge Fund Regulatory Improvement Act of 2008 - Directs the appropriate federal banking agencies, in coordination with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), to initiate a coordinated rulemaking with respect to the entities under their respective jurisdictions that engage in transactions involving unregistered hedge funds or over-the-counter derivatives.

Requires such rulemaking to: (1) extend the requirements of regulations relating to the safety and soundness of the financial system applicable to mutual funds under the Investment Company Act of 1940 to unregistered hedge funds; (2) require the fund to disclose its policies on borrowing money and requiring a shareholder vote to change such policy, as in the Investment Company Act of 1940; (3) provide for the regulation of over-the-counter derivatives, including credit default swaps, interest rate swaps, currency swaps, mortgage-backed securities, asset-backed securities, collateralized debt obligations, and other derivatives that are not traded on a national securities exchange or by a registered securities association; and (4) prohibit insured depository institutions from trading derivatives for their own accounts.

Marriage Penalty Relief Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) eliminate the marriage penalty in the standard deduction; (2) eliminate the 15 percent bracket for such penalty; (3) eliminate the 15 percent bracket for the adjusted gross income tax credit for earned income; and (4) increase the phaseout amount for such penalty.

Repatriate Our Patriots Act - Prohibits a special veteran from being removed from the United States.

Makes a special veteran eligible for all military and veterans benefits for which the special veteran would have been eligible if the special veteran had never been ordered removed, been removed, or voluntarilydeparted, from the United States.

Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to identify immigration cases involving special veterans by: (1) inquiring of every alien processed prior to initiating removal proceedings whether the alien is a special veteran; and (2) keeping records of special veterans who have been detained under the Immigration laws, had removal proceedings against them initiated before the date of the enactment of this Act, or been removed before such date.

Mowa Band of Choctaw Indians Recognition Act - Extends federal recognition to the Mowa Band of Choctaw Indians of Alabama. Restores rights and privileges of the Band that may have been abrogated or diminished before its federal recognition was enacted.

Prohibits the Band from using its federal recognition to assert any historical land claim.

Transfers all legal rights, title, and interests in lands held by the Band on this Act's enactment date to the United States.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior to accept any interest in lands acquired after this Act's enactment date in order to hold such lands in trust for the benefit of the Tribe.

Requires the Tribe to be eligible for all federal services and benefits provided to Indians because of its status as federally recognized Indians and, in the case of a reservation, to be eligible for all federal services and benefits provided to Indians without regard to the existence of a reservation.

Requires the Tribe to organize for its common welfare and adopt a constitution and bylaws to be in effect until such time as the United States adopts such a constitution.

Know Before You Fly Act - Amends Federal transportation law to prohibit a covered air carrier from failing to include in an air carrier's onlinefare quotation for a specific itinerary in air transportation selected by a consumer a clear and prominent statement that additional fees for checked baggage and carry-on baggage may apply, along with a prominent link from that online website page directly to a list of all such fees.

Requires a covered air carrier to publish, via a prominent link on its public air carrier website, a clear statement indicating whether or not it will: (1) provide for hotel accommodations, arrange for ground transportation, provide meal vouchers, arrange air transportation on another air carrier or foreign air carrier to the passenger's destination, and arrange for sleeping facilities, food, and water inside the airport terminal; and (2) provide for sleeping facilities, food, and water inside the airport terminal.

Requires a covered air carrier to identify each air carrier and foreign air carrier with which it will arrange air transportation as described in this Act.

Sport Fish Restoration and Recreational Boating Safety Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Aid in Fish Restoration Act to extend through FY2017 the prohibition against federal funds from being transferred to the Department of the Interior for the purpose of funding boating safety and national boating safety activities of national nonprofit public service organizations.

Extends through FY2017 the authorization of appropriations for the National Boating Safety Advisory Council.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through FY2017 the prohibition against federal funds from being transferred to Interior for the purpose of funding: (1) transfers to fund the National Boating Safety Advisory Council, and (2) the increased allowable amount of an annual appropriation for the National Boating Safety Advisory Council.

Disaster-Affected Homeowners Notification Act of 2013 - Requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), or the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) to: (1) notify mortgagors under a mortgage, or any agency head or enterprise, of forbearance relief if the Secretary, the Director, or either agency head makes available such relief; and (2) provide for community-wide notification and awareness of such relief in areas subject to such disaster declaration.

Help Extend Auditory Relief (HEAR) Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of hearing aids and aural rehabilitation services. Includes hearing aids as durable medical equipment (DME) under Medicare.

Forest Service Financial Accountability Restoration Act of 1999 - Requires the total amount appropriated for the Forest Service to carry out discretionary programs and activities for a fiscal year to: (1) not exceed the sum of the amounts appropriated under the Forest Service section of the Department of the Interior and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1999; and (2) terminate on the earlier of the date on which the Forest Service is no longer an agency at high risk of waste, fraud, abuse, and mismanagement due to weaknesses in its accounting and financial reporting systems, or the end of the fifth fiscal year subject to such limitations. 
Requires the Forest Service to no longer be an agency at high risk if the Comptroller General certifies to the Congress that its financial management is no longer at high risk. 
Requires the Forest Service to maintain or increase outputs, relative to the levels achieved during FY 1999, from programs that reduce the natural resources restoration and maintenance backlog within the National Forest System.

Distributed Power Hybrid Energy Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy to develop and transmit to the Congress a distributed power hybrid systems strategy showing: (1) opportunities and priorities that might best be met with distributed power hybrid systems configurations; (2) what barriers exist to the use of distributed power hybrid systems; (3) what technology gaps need to be closed; and (4) what system integration tools are needed to plan, design, build, and operate distributed power hybrid systems for maximum benefits.

Requires the Secretary to implement the strategy and integrate it with other activities of the Department's Office of Distributed Energy Resources.

Directs the Secretary to report annually to Congress on the use of, and experience with, distributed power hybrid systems in the United States, including research and development issues remaining to ensure successful application of distributed power hybrid systems.

National Urban Watershed Model Restoration Act - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to develop and carry out a pilot program to serve as a national model for the restoration of urban watersheds and community environments. 
Requires the Administrator to:  (1) integrate on a community or geographic basis the regulatory and nonregulatory programs of the Environmental Protection Agency with other Federal, State, and local government programs and provide effective coordination among such programs; (2) develop and maintain environmental indicators in conjunction with interested public entities and ensure regular public reporting of such indicators; (3) provide grants to local community groups and nonprofit organizations to foster community involvement in the decision making process, environmental educational goals, and restoration strategies; (4) assist in the establishment of measurable goals for such restoration; (5) maintain annual program plans which provide for public input; (6) develop consensus strategies for the restoration and protection of the watershed in cooperation with other Federal, State, and local groups to address critical issues and needs; (7) maintain a biennial Federal work planning process for Federal landholders and programmatic agencies to identify specific opportunities and needs for Federal activities in support of the pilot program's goals; (8) demonstrate new technologies and approaches which are applicable nationally to stormwater management, combined sewer

Social Security Disability Amendments Act of 1994 - Amends title XVI (State Children's Health Insurance Program) (SCHIP) of the Social Security Act to disregard income and resources of an eligible spouse when determining continued SCHIP eligibility. 
Expands the SCHIP plans for achieving self-support to include housing goals. 
Provides for the effective date of this Act for 1994.

Truth in Video Game Rating Act - Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to prescribe rules to prohibit any rating organization from: (1) assigning a content rating to any video or computer game that is to bear such rating when sold or distributed in interstate commerce unless such rating organization has reviewed the playable content of the game in its entirety; (2) withholding or hiding any playable content of the game from, or in any other manner failing to disclose any such content to, a rating organization; and (3) providing a content rating that grossly mischaracterizes the content of the game.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on: (1) the efficacy of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board (IASB) ratings system in assigning appropriate content ratings to video and computer games; (2) whether such a system should be peer-reviewed; (3) whether an independent ratings system would result in more accurate and effective content ratings for video and computer games than the IASB system; and (4) the efficacy of a universal ratings system for visual content, including films, broadcast and cable television and video, and computer games.

This bill directs the Department of Energy (DOE), acting through the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, to act as the lead federal agency for coordinating and disseminating information on existing federal programs and assistance that may be used to help initiate, develop, and finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy retrofitting projects for schools. DOE must: (1) conduct a review of existing programs and financing mechanisms (including revolving loan funds and loan guarantees) that are currently used to help initiate, develop, and finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy retrofitting projects for schools, and (2) establish a federal cross-departmental collaborative coordination, education, and outreach effort to streamline communication and promote available federal opportunities and assistance for such projects. DOE must also provide technical assistance to states, local educational agencies, and schools to help develop and finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy retrofitting projects.

Nonprofit Energy Efficiency Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to establish a pilot program to award grants for the purpose of retrofitting nonprofit buildings with energy-efficiency improvements.

Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to extend through FY2016 the authorization of appropriations for the Department of Energy (DOE) to carry out the pilot program.

Medicare HMO Protection Act of 1998 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to delay the effectiveness of a Medicare+Choice organization's termination of a plan if:  (1) termination would cause an imminent and serious health risk to enrollees; (2) termination would result in a significant reduction in available Medicare+Choice plans; or (3) the organization terminating coverage is offering such plans in contract areas that are in close proximity to the area affected by termination without suffering considerable financial losses. 
Authorizes the Secretary to negotiate a new contract which will enable the organization to continue coverage. 
Extends the initial Medicare+Choice contract period to three years. 
Requires each contract to require the organization to provide written notice of the termination at least 120 days (currently, 12 weeks) prior to the contract's termination. 
Requires the organization to provide a description of alternatives for obtaining benefits under Medicare+Choice plans and supplemental policies.

Directs the Secretary of Transportation to certify expenses as qualified for a fiscal year on October 1 of such year, in an amount not to exceed the amount estimated to be transferred to the Intercity Passenger Rail Trust Fund for such fiscal year.  Terminates the Fund on October 1, 2002.

Guam War Claims Review Commission Act - Establishes the Guam War Claims Review Commission to: (1) review the facts and circumstances surrounding the implementation and administration of the Guam Meritorious Claims Act and the effectiveness of such Act in addressing the war claims of American nationals residing on Guam between December 8, 1941, and July 21, 1944; (2) review all relevant Federal and Guam territorial laws, records of oral testimony previously taken, and documents in Guam and the Archives of the Federal Government regarding Federal payments of war claims in Guam; (3) receive oral testimony of persons who personally experienced the taking and occupation of Guam by Japanese military forces; (4) determine whether there was parity of war claims paid to the residents of Guam under the Guam Meritorious Claims Act as compared with awards made to other similarly affected U.S. citizens or nationals in territory occupied by the Imperial Japanese military forces during World War II; (5) advise on any additional compensation that may be necessary to compensate the people of Guam for death, personal injury, forced labor, forced march, and internment; and (6) not later than nine months after its establishment, report to the Secretary of the Interior, the Committee on Resources and the

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to carry out a program to provide low-income, minority, or disadvantaged college students with the information, preparation, and financial assistance to gain access to and complete law school study.

Authorizes the Secretary to enter into a contract with, or make a grant to, the Council on Legal Education Opportunity to: (1) identify such students; (2) prepare such students for study at accredited law schools; (3) assist such students to select the right law school, make application for entry into law school, and receive financial assistance for such study; (4) provide support services to such students who are first-year law students to improve their retention and success in law school studies; and (5) motivate and prepare such students to study law school in low-income communities.

Federal Public Safety Officer Surviving Spouse Protection Act of 2005 - Provides for the continuation of survivor annuities for remarried Federal public safety officers killed in the line of duty.

Drug Rebate Equalization Act of 2009 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to extend Medicaid coverage to certain individuals enrolled with a Medicaid managed care organization (MCO) who are covered under Medicare.

Requires payment for covered outpatient drugs dispensed to individuals eligible for medical assistance who are enrolled with the entity to be subject to the same rebate as under state law, and capitation rates paid to the entity to be based on actual cost experience related to rebates and subject to federal regulations requiring commercially sound rates.

Improving Department of State Oversight Act of 2015 This bill provides for competitive hiring of former Secretaries of State for the Department of Defense (DOD) for positions in the Department's competitive service for which the Secretary of State has made allegations of:  waste, fraud, or abuse in a DOD program or operation; criminal or serious misconduct on the part of a DOD employee at the FS-1, GS-15, GM-15 level or higher; criminal misconduct on the part of any DOD employee; and serious, noncriminal misconduct on the part of any individual authorized to carry a weapon, make arrests, or conduct searches, such as conduct that, if proven, would constitute perjury or material dishonesty, warrant suspension as discipline for a first offense, or result in loss of law enforcement authority.  The bill amends the Foreign Service Act of 1980 to require the Department of State to certify to Congress that it has made reasonable efforts to ensure the integrity and independence of the Office of the Inspector General Information Technology systems. Partnering to Detect and Defeat Tunnels Act This bill directs the Department of Defense (DOD) to: (1) seek to partner with Israel to develop and deploy technologies to detect and counter tunnels, and (2) designate a military department or other element of DOD to carry out a report on tunnels.  DOD may seek to enter into similar agreements with allies of the United States to develop technologies to detect and counter tunnels.  DOD shall report to Congress on instances of tunnels being used to attack U.S. or U.S. allies and trends or developments in tunnel attacks throughout the world.

Public Pension Parity Act of 1995 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income any amount received by an individual as a governmental pension under a public retirement system.  Limits the aggregate amount excluded for the taxable year to the maximum benefits payable under title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) of the Social Security Act which could have been excluded from income.

Directs the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture to jointly establish a broad-based advisory group to review the following criteria for determining fair market values and next best alternative use:  (1) the methodology used in any previous studies; (2) the validity of the results of such studies; and (3) the method of the determination of the next best alternative use.

Directs the President to take necessary steps, by imposing quotas, tariff surcharges, negotiated enforceable voluntary export restraint agreements, or otherwise, to ensure that the volume of steel products imported into the United States during any month does not exceed the average volume of steel products that was imported monthly before July 1997.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury, through the U.S. Customs Service and the Secretary of Commerce, to establish and implement a program for administering and enforcing the restraints on imports.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce to establish and implement a steel import notification and monitoring program. Requires any person who imports a product classified under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States that is initially entered into a bonded warehouse or foreign trade zone to obtain an import notification certificate before such product is entered into U.S. customs territory.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce to compile and publish information concerning such imports.

Requires the Secretary to make such information available to the public.

Directs the Secretary of Commerce to make publicly available information concerning imports from a foreign producer or exporter that is the only producer or exporter of goods subject to this Act available to the public.

Protecting Employees and Retirees in Municipal Bankruptcies Act of 2014 - Amends federal bankruptcy law to revise the criteria for determining municipal bankruptcy. Requires creditors who are employees or retirees of municipal bankruptcy courts to be considered creditors under the National Labor Relations Act. Repeals the limitation on the authority of a municipal bankruptcy court to issue a stay pending appeal. Directs the appropriate court of appeals to have jurisdiction of an appeal of a bankruptcy court determination that an entity is eligible to be a debtor under federal bankruptcy law and to consider and determine such appeal on an expedited basis. Prohibits the appropriate court of appeals from allowing a stay pending appeal to be dismissed on the basis of an equitable mootness doctrine. Directs the appropriate court of appeals to appoint, on a proportional basis per capita based on organization membership, individuals chosen from among members of organizations that represent the retirees with respect to whom such order is entered. Prohibits a municipal bankruptcy court from recommending modification of any right to a retiree benefit unless at least 2/3 of the members vote in support of such recommendation.

Health Care Fraud and Abuse Advisory Opinion Act of 1994 - Amends title XI (General Provisions) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue advisory opinions as to:  (1) what constitutes prohibited remuneration within the meaning of Federal law; (2) whether an arrangement or proposed arrangement satisfies the criteria set forth in Federal law as amended for activities which do not result in prohibited remuneration; (3) whether an arrangement or proposed arrangement satisfies the criteria which the Secretary has established, or shall establish by regulation for activities which do not result in prohibited remuneration; and (4) what constitutes an inducement to reduce or limit services to individuals entitled to benefits under part A (Hospital Insurance) of title XVIII or part B (Supplementary Medical Insurance) of title XVIII. 
Prohibits the Secretary from addressing matters not subject to advisory opinions. 
Authorizes the Secretary to issue advisory opinions on whether an arrangement or proposed arrangement will result in a prohibited referral within the meaning of Federal law.

Alternative Minimum Tax Repeal Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to eliminate the tax on the alternative minimum tax on individuals.

Requires the Secretary to maximize public participation in the issuance of regulations required by this Act, by: (1) publishing an advance notice of proposed rulemaking; (2) publishing the advance notice of proposed rulemaking and the proposed rule through means designed to reach persons likely to be subject to or affected by the regulations, including electronic means; (3) making the text of the advance notice of proposed rulemaking and of the proposed rule available through electronic means; (4) providing not less than 120 days for public comment on the proposed rule; (5) providing for an effective date that is not less than 30 days after the date of publication of the final rule; and (6) such other means as the Secretary considers appropriate.
Requires the Secretary to issue final regulations required by this Act.
Ethanol Stimulus Act of 2006 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a small ethanol producer a three-year credit for ethanol production in two-two states.

Requires the Attorney General to make electronic copies of all records released to any person under this Act available by December 31, 1999. 
Requires each agency to make such records available by computer telecommunications or, if computer telecommunications means have not been established by the agency, by other electronic means. 
Requires the Attorney General to submit annual reports on or before April 1 of each calendar year which shall include for the prior calendar year a listing of the number of cases arising under this Act, the exemption involved in each case, the disposition of such case, and the cost, fees, and penalties assessed, and (F) a description of the efforts undertaken by the Department of Justice to encourage agency compliance with this Act.

Amends the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 to prohibit the Export-Import Bank from guaranteeing, insuring, extending credit, or participating in the extension of credit to an entity with respect to the export of any good or service destined for the People's Republic of China unless the Board of Directors of the Export-Import Bank determines that the entity has established and is adhering to a code of conduct.

Requires the Bank to: (1) provide a safe and healthy workplace; (2) ensure fair employment; (3) pay not less than the minimum wage required by law or the prevailing industry wage; and (4) comply with U.S. and local laws promoting good business practices.

Requires a small business to include in its annual report a description of its actions taken to comply with this Act.

Expresses the sense of the Congress that the Export-Import Bank and the Clearinghouse on Corporate Responsibility that is being developed by the Department of Commerce should work together to ensure that businesses are made aware of, and have access to, resources and organizations that can assist businesses in developing, implementing, and monitoring global corporate codes of conduct.

Army Arsenal Strategic Workload Enhancement Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Defense (DOD) to develop and promulgate measurable and enforceable guidelines for DOD, defense agencies, and the military services to have supplies, components, end items, parts, assemblies, and sub-assemblies made in factored formulae in order to have supplies, components, end items, parts, assemblies, and sub-assemblies made on an economical basis while preserving the ability to provide an effective and timely response to mobilization, national defense contingency situations, and other emergency requirements.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to assign government-owned and government-operated Department of the Army (Dagle) factories and arsenals sufficient workload to ensure cost efficiency and technical competence in peacetime while preserving the ability to provide an effective and timely response to emergencies.

Authorizes the Secretary to waive the requirement for such a work load waiver if necessary for national defense.

Janey Ensminger Act of 2016 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to review the scientific literature relevant to the relationship between the employment or residence of individuals at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, for at least 30 days during the period beginning on August 1, 1953, and ending on December 21, 1987, and specific illnesses or conditions incurred by those individuals.  The VA must also categorize the evidence of connection of the illness or condition to such exposure as sufficient or modest in the most recent list published under the Public Health Service Act to include: (1) illnesses or conditions for which a determination has been made that exposure was a cause of the illness or condition; and (2) illnesses or conditions for which a determination has been made that such exposure was not a cause of the illness or condition.  The VA must transfer to the Chief Business Office and Financial Services Center of the VA for FY2017 and FY2018 a specified amount to be used to continue building and enhancing the claims processing system, eligibility system, and web portal for the Camp Lejeune Family Member Program.

Veterans Equal Treatment Act - Terminates the Department of Veterans Affairs medical care funding allocation formula established under the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) medical care system. Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to develop a new formula for the allocation of VA medical care funds to the national service regions, known as VISNs, of the VA. Authorizes appropriations for such formula.

Safe and Affordable Drugs from Canada Act of 2015 Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to promulgate regulations permitting individuals to safely import into the United States a prescription drug purchased from an approved Canadian pharmacy that: (1) is dispensed by a pharmacist licensed in Canada; (2) is purchased for personal use in quantities not greater than a 90-day supply; (3) is filled using a valid prescription issued by a physician licensed to practice in the United States; and (4) has the same active ingredient or ingredients, route of administration, dosage form, and strength as a prescription drug approved under the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) program. Directs the Secretary to publish on the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) website a list of approved Canadian pharmacies, including their website address, from which individuals may purchase prescription drugs.

Off-Reservation Land Acquisition Guidance Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior, before determining whether to take off-reservation land into trust for the benefit of an Indian tribe, to evaluate: (1) the anticipated benefits to the tribe associated with taking the off-reservation land into trust; and (2) any concerns raised by applicable State and local governments relating to the acquisition of the off-reservation land.

Requires the Secretary, in evaluating such concerns, to prepare a report that includes an assessment of: (1) the impacts of taking the applicable off-reservation land into trust on the on-reservation unemployment rate, the impacts of taking the applicable off-reservation land into trust on reservation life and tribal membership if members, dependents, and descendants of the Indian tribe relocate to the off-reservation land or adjacent communities, and the specific on-reservation benefits of taking the off-reservation land into trust; and (2) whether the tribal government can efficiently exercise the governmental and regulatory responsibilities of the tribal government if a gaming facility is constructed on the off-reservation land.

Save Our Seas Act of 2017 or the SOS Act of 2017 This bill amends the Marine Debris Act to authorize the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to work with other federal agencies to develop outreach and education strategies to address both land- and sea-based sources of marine debris. The bill also amends the Marine Debris Act to authorize the Department of State and the U.S. Coast Guard to work with each other and with foreign countries to promote international action to reduce the incidence of marine debris.

Great Lakes Federal Effectiveness Act - Establishes a Great Lakes Research Council. Directs the Council to: (1) advise and promote the coordination of Federal research activities to avoid unnecessary duplication and ensure greater effectiveness in achieving ecosystem protection of the Great Lakes through the goals of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement; (2) no later than one year after enactment of this Act, prepare and provide to interested parties a document which includes an assessment of research activities needed to fulfill the Agreement's goals, an assessment of existing Federal expertise and capabilities in those activities, and recommendations for priorities for research; (3) identify topics for and participate in meetings, workshops, conferences, and symposia on Great Lakes research issues; (4) make recommendations for the uniform collection of data for enhancing research and management protocols relating to the Great Lakes ecosystem; (5) advise and cooperate in the establishment of a comprehensive, multi-media data base for the Great Lakes ecosystem; and (6) ensure that the results, findings, and information regarding research programs conducted or sponsored by the federal government be disseminated in a timely manner, and in useful forms, to interested persons, using as much as possible existing mechanisms.Requires the Council to invite the International Joint Commission to serve as Secretariat and principal coordinating body for the Council

Cuba Sanctions Reform Act of 2004 - Extends the one-year period for the renewal of the Cuban Sanctions Reform Act of 2004. Community Investment and Empowerment Act - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to direct the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to make competitive grants to communities for: (1) the creation of a grant and/or revolving loan fund program that helps develop financing packages for Class 1 commercial investment; (2) lowering real estate property tax rates; (3) conducting community-wide market analysis to help recruit and/or retain Class 1 commercial investment; (4) creating employment training programs for Class 1 business customer service, sales, and managerial positions; (5) retail marketing strategies to solicit new Class 1 commercial investment starts in the community; (6) program allowances for activities such as the publication of marketing materials, development of economic development web pages, and educational outreach activities with retail trade associations; and (7) hiring business recruitment specialists.

Requires the Administrator to make matching funds available to eligible community-wide organizations for the costs incurred by the community in carrying out the activities for which the grant is awarded.

Local Farm Vehicle Flexibility Act - Prohibits the Secretary of Agriculture from reducing, limiting, or otherwise interfering with the amount or timing of grants a state is otherwise eligible to receive under the Federal Farm Vehicle Program under the Tariff and Trade Act of 1977.

True Understanding of the Economy and Safety Act or the TRUE Safety Act - Directs the Comptroller General (GAO) to assess the methodology followed by the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) in carrying out the efficacy of the trucking industry's 34-hour start rule, which is the law that requires full and fair scientific research, analysis, and operational testing for commercial truck drivers.

Cure for AIDS Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Defense, acting through the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Program, to establish and support an accelerated research program dedicated to the discovery of a cure for HIV/AIDS.

Requires the Secretary to ensure that research conducted under this Act is highly targeted to address: (1) HIV persistence; (2) where HIV persists beyond the reach of antiretroviral therapy; (3) whether the immune system is struggling to clear the infection; (4) why the immune system reduces but does not eliminate levels of the virus; (5) interventions that may eliminate the virus from infected individuals; and (6) interventions that may help an infected individual permanently control the virus without antiretroviral therapy.

Requires the Secretary to coordinate with at least one eligible nonprofit entity whose primary mission is ending the AIDS epidemic through innovative research and that has experience carrying out programs dedicated to AIDS cure research.

Prohibits the use of funds appropriated or otherwise made available to the Department of Defense or any other U.S. department or agency to carry out any covert action for the purpose of causing regime change in Iran or to carry out any military action against Iran in the absence of an imminent threat, in accordance with international law and constitutional and statutory requirements for congressional authorization.

Requires the Secretary to make a final determination within six months after the submittal of such petition as to whether or not such a lease will be eligible for such an incentive program.

TPS Reform Act of 2016 This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to allow a foreign state to designate a foreign state as an eligible foreign state upon the enactment of an Act that satisfies specified requirements, including that the Act contains a finding that there is an ongoing armed conflict within the state and that the state's return would pose a serious threat to the state's personal safety.  The bill also amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to extend the effective period of an initial designation of a foreign state that no longer meets the conditions for designation under the Act.  The bill defines "aliens lacking lawful immigration status" as aliens who lack a lawful immigration status.

Military Call-Up Relief Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to waive the early withdrawal penalty for certain distributions from qualified retirement plans to individuals called to active duty during the national emergency declared by the President on September 14, 2001.

Fair Credit Reporting Act Amendments of 2000 - Amends the Fair Credit Reporting Act to require: (1) each consumer reporting agency to make all disclosures pursuant to such Act annually upon consumer request; and (2) such agencies to disclose credit risk scores or other predictors on the Internet or the World Wide Web.Requires: (1) the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to review and monitor the extent to which consumer reporting agencies and furnishers of consumer information to consumer reporting agencies are complying with the procedures, time lines, and requirements under the Act for the prompt investigation of the disputed accuracy of any consumer information; and (2) the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Trade Commission to each submit a progress report to Congress on the results of such review.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make permanent the small business expensing allowance of $500,000; (2) increase the expensing allowance for computer software placed in service in a taxable year from $200,000 to $1,000,000; and (3) allow a deduction for the purchase of domestically manufactured automobiles.

State Veterans Home Nurse Recruitment Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make payments to assist States for the purpose of assisting State homes in the hiring and retention of nurses and the reduction of nursing shortages at State homes.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a small manufacturer of computer hardware and software a business tax credit for the depreciation of such hardware and software property. Defines "computer hardware" as: (1) a computer software property for use in a small manufacturer located in the United States; and (2) a computer software property for use in a taxable year.

Residential and Commuter Toll Fairness Act of 2009 - Authorizes states, counties, municipalities, and multi-jurisdictional transportation authorities to establish programs that offer discounted transportation tolls, user fees, or fares for residents of specific geographic areas in order to reduce or alleviate toll burdens imposed upon such residents.

Authorizes such authorities to enact rules or regulations necessary to establish such programs.

Taxpayer's Right to View Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit a cable operator from collecting any separate charges for any video programming of a sporting, theatrical, or other entertainment event if the event is performed at a facility constructed, maintained, or renovated with tax revenues or by an organization that receives public financial support.

Communities Committed to College Tax Credit Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer who is a current or former registered donor of a qualified scholarship funding trust a tax credit for 50% of designated qualified college scholarship funding contributions. Limits the amount of such credit to $1 million.

Clinical Trials Modernization Act of 2015 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to establish a framework through which: (1) sponsors of drugs, biological products, or devices may submit a proposal for the incorporation of adaptive trial designs, Bayesian methods, or other alternative statistical methods into proposed clinical protocols and marketing applications for such products and devices; and (2) the FDA will commit to timelines for reviewing and providing feedback on proposals so submitted. The FDA must publish a final guidance on the use of Bayesian methods in the development and regulatory review and approval of drugs, biological products, and devices. The FDA must establish a process to evaluate a postapproval study or clinical trial required to be conducted to determine whether: (1) the trial or study is no longer scientifically warranted, or (2) the design, or the timelines applicable to the completion of, the study or trial should be renegotiated because of changes in medical practice or the standard of care.

Medicare Home Health Equity Act of 1998 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to:  (1) restore cost limits for home health services furnished by home health agencies; and (2) require the Director of the Congressional Budget Office to estimate the amount of savings to the Medicare program resulting from the interim payment system for home health services established by this Act.

Business Relief and Incentives for Small Entrepreneurs Act of 2007 or the Business RAISE Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) extend the 15-year recovery period for depreciation of certain retail space improvements; (2) revise the definition of "qualified retail improvement property" to include certain improvements placed in service before January 1, 2008; and (3) expand the eligibility for the work opportunity tax credit to include individuals who have a disability rating of not less than 10% under the Federal Employees' Disability Insurance Program.

Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to study and report to Congress on: (1) the economic and trade impact of agricultural exports of food products from cloned animals; (2) the content of such study; and (3) the study with the Government Accountability Office on Monitoring Food Products from Cloned Animals (Sustainability Report).

Directs the Secretary to study and report to Congress on the programs in place at the Department of Agriculture to monitor food products from cloned animals if such products enter the food supply.

The credit is allowed to employees who: (1) while participating in the job skills training program is employed at least 40 hours per week, and (2) are employed at least 40 hours per week for at least 2 years.

Allows bond proceeds to be used for a park facility project.

Strengthening Homeland Security, Intelligence, and Essential Law Enforcement Departments Act of 2011 or the SHIELD Act of 2011 - Directs that: (1) the pay and allowances of members of the U.S. armed forces be made available to members during a period of lapsed appropriations for the Armed Forces; and (2) the Secretary of the Treasury make available to the Secretary of Defense (DOD) and the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) and the head of a federal agency, during a period of lapsed appropriations for a federal agency that employs critical law enforcement officers, such as those who perform emergency work involving the safety of human life or property, available to continue to provide pay and allowances (without interruption) to such officers during such period of lapsed appropriations.

Security Enhancement and Jobs Act of 2011 - Requires the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to approve or deny an airport application within 120 days of receipt of an application submitted by an airport operator under the air transportation security (AT&S) screening program.

The bill requires the FCC to: (1) review and issue a notice of apparent liability without first issuing a Notice of Unlicensed Operations, (2) publish a database of all licensed radio stations operating in the AM and FM bands, and (3) identify entities operating without a FCC license or authorization.
