Security Clearance Family Review Act This bill prohibits the Department of Justice (DOJ) from granting security clearances to a relative of the President unless the President submits a determination to the agency that the relative's access to classified information is necessary for federal employment. DOJ must review the determination within 60 days.

Provides that Cape Fox, notwithstanding section 16 (the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act), shall not be required to select or receive conveyance of specified federal land located within T.75 S., R.91 E., Copper River Meridian. 
Authorizes Cape Fox to select, and, on receiving written notice of the selection, conveyance of specified surface and subsurface lands to the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Board.

This bill authorizes the Department of the Interior to take certain actions to ensure the protection of the historic Gateway Arch in St. Louis, Missouri, as specified by the bill.  The Gateway Arch is a symbol of the St. Louis Riverfront and is one of the seven National Historic Landmarks of the Jefferson National Expansion Memorial Trust.  Interior may take certain actions to ensure the protection of the grounds surrounding the Arch, including:   entering into agreements with the Jefferson National Expansion Memorial Trust to develop the St. Louis riverfront between Eays and Poplar Street bridges, the Memorial grounds including the interstate highway and roadways now traversing them, Luther Ely Smith Square, and the Old Courthouse as a single project area, and the Old Courthouse and Ely Smith Square being included on the National Register of Historic Places.  Interior may also enter into agreements with the Trust to:   facilitate the planning, construction, and operation of a cultural facility on federal land within the boundary of the Trust and enter into agreements with the Trust for the Trust to assist in the implementation of the Final General Management Plan and Record of Decision.  Interior may also enter into agreements with the Trust to assist in the implementation of the Trust's administrative jurisdiction for conveyance of the grounds and facilities.

Department of Defense Office of the Victim Advocate Act of 2004 - Establishes in the Office of the Secretary of Defense an Office of the Victim Advocate to: (1) coordinate programs and activities of the military departments to the extent that they relate to victims of interpersonal violence among members of the armed forces or between members and family members and partners (including former spouses, children, significant others, children-in-common, girls friends, and boy friends); and (2) serve as the headquarters program manager for the victim advocates and the victim service specialists in the Department of Defense (DOD) authorized by law.

Requires the Director of the Office to: (1) evaluate the prevalence of interpersonal violence associated with members of the armed forces; (2) evaluate the services provided by the military departments to victims of such violence; (3) evaluate the delivery of such services to victims of such violence; (4) review the facilities of the military departments providing such services; (5) evaluate the hotline programs for victims of violence; and (6) review disciplinary actions taken against members of the armed forces who commit acts of interpersonal violence.

Requires any person or entity that disposes of or controls a cultural item to comply with the requirements of this Act. 
Provides for the recording and status of items excavated or discovered after November 16, 1990, except those items whose ownership or control is established under this Act. 
Provides for the study and recording of any human remains and associated funerary objects for which no lineal descendants have been identified and in cases of all other cultural items:  (1) if the cultural affiliation of a cultural item has not been established, studies may be conducted; and (2) if the cultural affiliation has been established, the Federal agency or museum having custody of the cultural item shall notify any culturally affiliated Indian tribe or Native Hawaiian organization of their affiliation. 
Provides for the study and recording of any cultural item that has been determined to be of value to the tribe or organization.

Transparency and Accountability ofFailed Exchanges Act This bill amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require state exchange construction grants to terminate or transfer to an entity other than the state to provide to the state a refund of exchange funds.  The bill also prohibits the False Claims Act from preempting state enforcement actions for fraud, waste, or abuse of funds.

Transnational Criminal Organization Illicit Spotter Prevention and Elimination Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to prohibit a person from knowingly transmitting, by any means, to another person the location, movement, or activities of any federal, state, local, or tribal law enforcement agency with intent to further a federal criminal crime relating to U.S. immigration, Customs, controlled substances, agriculture, monetary instruments, or other border controls.

Prohibits a person from intentionally destroying, altering, or damaging any fence, barrier, sensor, camera, or other physical or electronic device deployed by the federal government to control the border or a port of entry to: (1) prevent the installation of such devices; or (2) create obstacles to such devices; or (3) make such devices ineffective or unobvious.

Prohibits a person from attempting or conspiring to violate such prohibition.

Amends the criminal code to prohibit a person from carrying or using a firearm during and in relation to an alien smuggling crime.

Amends the bankruptcy code to make bankruptcy a predicate offense for the seizure and forfeiture of any property used to conceal or commit fraud.

Energy-Efficient Cool Roof Jobs Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) allow 20-year property depreciation for qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property placed in service before the enactment of this Act; and (2) allow 25% depreciation of qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property placed in service after the enactment of this Act.

Nye County Higher Education Campus Conveyance Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the University system without consideration the Federal land for use as a campus for the Nye County Nevada Higher Education Campus in Pahrump Valley, Nevada, a component of the University system.

Requires the University system to use the land conveyed for educational and recreational purposes, to erect an appropriate monument, and to assist the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) in providing information to the students of the College and the citizens of Nevada.

Permits the use of the land for any purpose relating to the establishment, operation, growth, and maintenance of the College, and any uses relating to those purposes, including residential and commercial development that would generally be associated with an institution of higher education.

Permits the University system to lease or otherwise provide property or space at the College with or without consideration, to religious, public interest, community, or other groups for services and events that are of interest to the College, the University system, or any community located in the County.

Protect Marriage from the Courts Act of 2015 This bill amends the federal judicial code to prohibit a court created by federal law or the Supreme Court from having jurisdiction, and the Supreme Court from having no appellate jurisdiction, to adjudicate or enforce any claim pertaining to the validity, under the U.S. Constitution, of a state law, or state administrative or judicial decision, that: (1) defines marriage as limited to the union of one man and one woman, or (2) refuses state recognition of or allows the state to refuse recognition of same-sex marriages performed and licensed in other states.  The bill also limits the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court to only those claims that it has entered before the effective date of this bill.

Fairness for Working Americans Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the refundable credit for the child tax credit; (2) exclude from gross income amounts excluded by reason of this Act; and (3) prevent a U.S. corporation from expatriating its employees to avoid the U.S. income tax.
Higher Education Savings Plan Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow taxpayers to receive penalty-free withdrawals from annuities for higher education expenses.
Grants a Federal charter to the National Academy of Inventors.

Accelerating Kids' Access to Care Act This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require state Medicaid programs to provide for streamlined screening and enrollment in the state plan for eligible out-of-state providers and suppliers.

Public Library Innovation Space Act This bill amends the Museum and Library Services Act to require the National Museum of American History to make public libraries and makerspaces available to public libraries and makerspaces that are owned or operated by the museums.

Rural Equity Payment Index Reform Act of 2003 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise the physician work adjustment factor schedule wage index. Prohibits the work geographic index from being less than: (1) 0.976 for services furnished during 2004, 0.987 for services furnished during 2005, 0.995 for services furnished during 2006, and 1.000 for services furnished during 2007 and subsequent years; and (2) 0.987 for services furnished during 2008 and thereafter.

Campaign Sunlight Act of 2012 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to direct the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to establish and operate the Campaign Accountability Site through which members of the public may view the contents of political advertisements.

Requires the sponsor of a political advertisement to submit the contents of the advertisement to the FEC in a format the FEC may require to enable the FEC to include the advertisement on the Site.

Requires the sponsor of a political advertisement to submit the contents of the advertisement to the FEC in a hyperlink on the FEC's official public website.

Requires the FEC to make the Website available through a hyperlink on the FEC's official public website.

Requires the sponsor of a political advertisement to submit the contents of the advertisement to the FEC in a hyperlink on the FEC's official public website if the content includes references to any quotation, article, hyperlink, or other source for any statement made in the advertisement.

Requires the FEC to make the Website available through a hyperlink on the FEC's official public website if the content includes a hyperlink to the full source of the advertisement.

Veterans Justice Outreach Act of 2015 This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to carry out a program to support veterans in contact with the criminal justice system by: (1) encouraging the diversion of law enforcement to mental health treatment and substance abuse services for veterans in contact with local law enforcement who can be appropriately diverted from arrest to mental health treatment, (2) providing support for courts and their officers, and (3) establishing coordinators to provide outreach under the program.

Higher Education Family Opportunity Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow individual taxpayers a deduction for qualified tuition and related expenses in lieu of the Hope and Lifetime Learning tax credit.
Grants a Federal charter to the Black Veterans of America (a nonprofit corporation organized under the laws of the State of Minnesota).

Anti-Pyramid Promotional Scheme Act of 2016 This bill prohibits any person from establishing, operating, or promoting a pyramid promotional scheme. A pyramid promotional scheme is a plan or operation by which a person gives consideration to a participant for the right to receive compensation that is derived primarily from a participant's introduction of another person into the plan or operation rather than from the sale of products to ultimate users. A person who practices a pyramid promotional scheme is subject to the Federal Trade Commission's enforcement powers.

Medical Savings Account Availability Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the current limitation on the number of medical savings accounts (MSAs) that may be created. (Currently, there is a one-time limitation of 12 for any one month.)Repeals the current limitation on the amount of the deductible for contributions to an MSA.Increases the amount of the deductible for contributions to an MSA.Allows both employers and employees to contribute to an MSA.Reduces the permitted deductible for employers.Increases the amount of the allowable amount of the deductible for employees.Allows a taxpayer to contribute to an MSA without penalty if the taxpayer is a preventive care patient.

International Peacekeeping Reform Act of 1997 - Prohibits any funds made available to the Department of State under the Account Contributions for International Peacekeeping Activities or any other funds to pay for assessed or voluntary contributions to United Nations peacekeeping activities from being available for obligation or expenditure to the United Nations to establish, expand, or modify in mission a United Nations peacekeeping operations unless the President certifies to the appropriate congressional committees that the United Nations peacekeeping operation meets specified requirements.  Directs the President, if an emergency exists which prevented submission of a 15-day advance notification and that the proposed action is in the direct national security interest, to notify the appropriate congressional committees that the United Nations peacekeeping operation meets specified requirements. 
Requires the President to certify to the Congress that the United Nations peacekeeping operation meets specified requirements.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a limited refundable tax credit for amounts paid for qualified child disability education and training expenses. Defines "qualified child disability expenses" as amounts paid for services and equipment related to education and training of a child with a developmental disability, including behavioral therapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, assistive communication technology, and other services as the Secretary of Health and Human Services may provide by regulation.

Amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to recognize Alexander Creek, Incorporated as an eligible Native village under the provisions of that Act.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to negotiate with Alexander Creek to fairly and equitably settle any aboriginal land claims and any other claims that he or she has against the United States.

Rural Broadband Enhancement Act - Amends the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act to direct the Rural Utilities Service of the Department of Agriculture to make loans or other extensions of credit to eligible entities to provide funds for the construction, improvement, or acquisition of facilities and equipment for the provision of broadband service in eligible rural communities.

Sets forth certain project requirements, including that the area to be served by the project is unserved or underserved by broadband service and that the potential number of subscribers to the broadband service available through the project is sufficient to make the service generally available throughout the area.

Prohibits such loans or other extensions from affecting the validity of any loan or extension of credit made under this Act before FY 2006.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to include within the definition of "qualified hazardous duty pay" for purposes of the tax deduction for retired military pay a member who performed qualifying hazardous duty and who retires on or after the date of this Act's enactment. 
Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on:  (1) whether members of the National Guard and reserve comprise a disproportionately large portion of the employees of any size or type of business, including small business concerns; (2) the amount of Federal tax benefit that would be appropriate to compensate such a business for costs associated with employing members of the National Guard and reserve units and having such members called to active duty; and (3) whether changes can be made to the small business loan program to assist small business concerns to deal with the costs associated with employing members of the National Guard and reserve units and having such members called to active duty. 
Directs the Secretary of the military department concerned to report to Congress on the feasibility and desirability of expanding the Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps program of each of the military departments, the Civil Air Patrol, the Naval Sea Cadet Corps, and the Young Marines of the Marine Corps League.

Rebuild American Manufacturing Act of 2013 - Directs the President to develop a comprehensive national manufacturing strategy. Requires the President to include in such strategy short- and long-term goals for U.S. manufacturing, including goals: (1) to increase the aggregate number of manufacturing jobs in the United States so that such number is not less than 20% of the sum of all nonfarm jobs in the United States; (2) to identify emerging technologies to strengthen the competitiveness of U.S. manufacturing in the global marketplace; and (3) to strengthen the manufacturing sectors of the United States in which the United States is most competitive in the global economy. Requires the national manufacturing strategy to include: (1) a survey of all persons with U.S. headquarters that maintain manufacturing facilities outside of the United States to identify the categories of products manufactured at such facilities and the number of manufacturing jobs located at such facilities; (2) a survey of all federal agencies that provide assistance to U.S. manufacturers, including the Department of Commerce, the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, the Department of Labor, the Small Business Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of Science and Technology Policy, the Office of the

Higher Education Fairness Act of 1997 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to provide for a family tax deduction for dependent students. 
Provides for a family tax deduction for independent students without dependents other than a spouse. 
Provides for a family tax deduction for dependent students with dependents other than a spouse. 
Provides for a family tax deduction for academic years after 1997-1998. 
Provides for a revised income protection allowance for dependent students. 
Provides for a revised income protection allowance for academic years after 1997-1998. 
Provides for a tax deduction for the income of taxpayers who are expending tax-exempt funds.
Grants a Federal charter to the American Military Retirees Association.

National Park Centennial Challenge Fund Act - Establishes in the Treasury the National Park Centennial Challenge Fund. Requires the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service (NPS), to develop a list of eligible projects and programs for funding from the Challenge Fund.

Authorizes the Secretary to transfer to the Fund cash donations received by the NPS.

Prohibits the Secretary from obligating any amounts based on a letter of credit, or amounts to match a letter of credit, until amounts from that letter of credit are deposited in the Fund.

Air Traffic Supervisor Retirement Reform Act of 1995 - Amends Federal civil service and employee Retirement System provisions to provide for the Civil Service Retirement System and the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) retirement plans for air traffic controllers and other civilian employees.

Public Servant Priority Placement Act of 1995 - Directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to establish a Government-wide program and each agency to establish an agency program to facilitate employment placement for Federal employees who:  (1) are scheduled to be separated from service under a reduction in force action; or (2) are separated from service under such a reduction in force. 
Requires each agency placement program to provide a system to require the offer of a vacant position in an agency to an employee of such agency affected by a reduction in force action, if:  (1) the position cannot be filled within the agency; (2) the employee to whom the offer is made is qualified for the offered position; (3) the classification of the offered position is equal to or no more than one grade below the employee's present or last held position; or (4) the basic rate of pay of the offered position is equal to the basic rate of pay of the employee's present or last held position. 
Requires each agency placement program to:  (1) coordinate with programs established by agencies for the placement of agency employees affected by a reduction in force action within such agency; and (2)

Sportsmanship in Hunting Act of 2008 - Amends the federal criminal code to prohibit the transfer, transporting, or possessing a confined exotic animal for the purpose of allowing the killing or injuring of that animal for entertainment or for the collection of a trophy.

Defines "confined exotic animal" as a mammal of a species not historically indigenous to the United States, that has been held in captivity, whether or not the defendant knows the length of the captivity, for the shorter of: (1) the majority of the animal's life; or (2) a period of one year.

Defines "captivity" as a period during which an animal lives as it would in the wild, surviving primarily by foraging for naturally occurring food and roaming at will over an open area of at least 1,000 acres.

Authorizes any person authorized by the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, to: (1) without a warrant, arrest any person that violates this prohibition; (2) execute any warrant or other process issued by an officer or court of competent jurisdiction to enforce this prohibition; and (3) search for and seize any taken or possessed animal.

Helping College Students Cross the Finish Line Act This bill amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Department of Education (ED) to award grants to institutions of higher education to establish programs of financial assistance for undergraduate and vocational students with financial need to assist in completing their degree and certificate programs.  ED must create and provide to each institution receiving a grant an online survey of its students on financial literacy.
